  evaluate policy.toExpr request entities = .error err →
  policy.resourceScope.scope.bound = .some uid →
  inₑ request.resource uid entities = true

modules.doc: This file contains useful lemmas about the `Evaluator` functions.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.producesBool
items.doc: `producesBool` means the expression evaluates to a bool (and not an error)
items.statement: def producesBool (e : Expr) (request : Request) (entities : Entities) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.producesNonBool
items.doc: `producesNonBool` means the expression evaluates to a non-bool (and not an error)
items.statement: def producesNonBool (e : Expr) (request : Request) (entities : Entities) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.and_bool_operands_is_boolean_and
items.statement:
theorem and_bool_operands_is_boolean_and {b₁ b₂ : Bool} {e₁ e₂ : Expr} {request : Request} {entities : Entities} :
  evaluate e₁ request entities = .ok b₁ →
  evaluate e₂ request entities = .ok b₂ →
  evaluate (Expr.and e₁ e₂) request entities = .ok (b₁ && b₂)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.left_false_implies_and_false
items.statement:
theorem left_false_implies_and_false {e₁ e₂ : Expr} {request : Request} {entities : Entities} :
  evaluate e₁ request entities = .ok false →
  evaluate (Expr.and e₁ e₂) request entities = .ok false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.left_bool_right_false_implies_and_false
items.statement:
theorem left_bool_right_false_implies_and_false {e₁ e₂ : Expr} {request : Request} {entities : Entities} :
  producesBool e₁ request entities →
  evaluate e₂ request entities = .ok false →
  evaluate (Expr.and e₁ e₂) request entities = .ok false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.and_true_implies_left_true
items.statement:
theorem and_true_implies_left_true {e₁ e₂ : Expr} {request : Request} {entities : Entities} :
  evaluate (Expr.and e₁ e₂) request entities = .ok true →
  evaluate e₁ request entities = .ok true

items.name: Cedar.Thm.and_true_implies_right_true
items.statement:
theorem and_true_implies_right_true {e₁ e₂ : Expr} {request : Request} {entities : Entities} :
  evaluate (Expr.and e₁ e₂) request entities = .ok true →
  evaluate e₂ request entities = .ok true

items.name: Cedar.Thm.ways_and_can_error
items.doc:
If an `and` expression results in an error, it's because either:
- the left subexpression had that error
- the right subexpression had that error (and the left subexpression evaluated to .ok true)
- the left subexpression evaluated to .ok with a non-bool
- the right subexpression evaluated to .ok with a non-bool (and the left subexpression evaluated to .ok true)
items.statement:
theorem ways_and_can_error {e₁ e₂ : Expr} {request : Request} {entities : Entities} {err : Error} :
  evaluate (Expr.and e₁ e₂) request entities = .error err →
  evaluate e₁ request entities = .error err ∨
  (evaluate e₁ request entities = .ok true ∧ evaluate e₂ request entities = .error err) ∨
  (err = Error.typeError ∧ producesNonBool e₁ request entities) ∨
  (err = Error.typeError ∧ evaluate e₁ request entities = .ok true ∧ producesNonBool e₂ request entities)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.and_produces_bool_or_error
items.doc: Every `and` expression produces either .ok bool or .error
items.statement:
theorem and_produces_bool_or_error (e₁ e₂ : Expr) (request : Request) (entities : Entities) :
  match (evaluate (Expr.and e₁ e₂) request entities) with
  | .ok (.prim (.bool _)) => true
  | .error _ => true
  | _ => false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.policy_produces_bool_or_error
items.doc:
Corollary of the above:
Evaluating a policy produces either .ok bool or .error
items.statement:
theorem policy_produces_bool_or_error (p : Policy) (request : Request) (entities : Entities) :
  match (evaluate p.toExpr request entities) with
  | .ok (.prim (.bool _)) => true
  | .error _ => true
  | _ => false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.record_produces_record_value
items.doc: If evaluating a record produces a value, then it always produces a record value.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.record_value_contains_evaluated_attrs
items.doc:
If evaluating a record produces a record value containing an attribute, then
that attribute existed in the original record, and corresponding expression
evaluates to the same value.
items.statement:
theorem record_value_contains_evaluated_attrs {rxs : List (Attr × Expr)} {rvs : Map Attr Value} {a : Attr} {av : Value} {request : Request} {entities : Entities}
  (he : evaluate (.record rxs) request entities = .ok (.record rvs))
  (hfv : rvs.find? a = some av) :
  ∃ x, (Map.make rxs).find? a = some x ∧ evaluate x request entities = .ok av

modules.doc: This file contains definitions relevant to slicing.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IsSoundPolicySlice
items.doc:
A policy slice is a subset of a collection of policies.  This slice is sound for
a given request and entities if every policy in the collection that is not in
the slice is also not satisfied with respect to the request and entities, and
doesn't produce an error when evaluated.
items.statement: def IsSoundPolicySlice (req : Request) (entities : Entities) (slice policies : Policies) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.sound_slice_transitive
items.statement:
theorem sound_slice_transitive :
  IsSoundPolicySlice r es slice₁ ps →
  IsSoundPolicySlice r es slice₂ slice₁ →
  IsSoundPolicySlice r es slice₂ ps

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IsSoundPolicySliceFalseDef
items.doc:
Alternate definition of soundness for policy slicing. Rather than showing
that a policy doesn't evaluate to `true` or error, we can show that it
does evaluate to `false`.
items.statement: def IsSoundPolicySliceFalseDef (req : Request) (entities : Entities) (slice policies : Policies) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.is_sound_policy_slice_def_equiv
items.statement:
theorem is_sound_policy_slice_def_equiv {req : Request} {entities : Entities} {slice policies : Policies} :
  IsSoundPolicySlice req entities slice policies ↔ IsSoundPolicySliceFalseDef req entities slice policies

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IsSoundPolicyBound
items.doc:
A bound is sound for a given policy if the bound is satisfied for every request
and entities for which the policy is satisfied or for which the policy produces
an error.
items.statement: def IsSoundPolicyBound (bound : PolicyBound) (policy : Policy) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IsSoundBoundAnalysis
items.doc: A bound analysis is sound if it produces sound bounds for all policies.
items.statement: def IsSoundBoundAnalysis (ba : BoundAnalysis) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.sound_policy_slice_is_equisatisfied
items.statement:
theorem sound_policy_slice_is_equisatisfied (effect : Effect) {request : Request} {entities : Entities} {slice policies : Policies} :
  IsSoundPolicySlice request entities slice policies →
  slice.filterMap (satisfiedWithEffect effect · request entities) ≡
  policies.filterMap (satisfiedWithEffect effect · request entities)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.satisfiedPolicies_eq_for_sound_policy_slice
items.statement:
theorem satisfiedPolicies_eq_for_sound_policy_slice (effect : Effect) {request : Request} {entities : Entities} {slice policies : Policies} :
  IsSoundPolicySlice request entities slice policies →
  satisfiedPolicies effect slice request entities = satisfiedPolicies effect policies request entities

items.name: Cedar.Thm.sound_policy_slice_is_equierror
items.statement:
theorem sound_policy_slice_is_equierror {request : Request} {entities : Entities} {slice policies : Policies} :
  IsSoundPolicySlice request entities slice policies →
  slice.filter (hasError · request entities) ≡ policies.filter (hasError · request entities)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.errorPolicies_eq_for_sound_policy_slice
items.statement:
theorem errorPolicies_eq_for_sound_policy_slice {request : Request} {entities : Entities} {slice policies : Policies} :
  IsSoundPolicySlice request entities slice policies →
  errorPolicies slice request entities = errorPolicies policies request entities

modules.doc: This file defines the main theorems for batched authorization and evaluation.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.batched_evaluate_eq_evaluate
items.doc:
The main correctness theorem for batched evaluation:
Batched evaluation with an entity loader produces the same result
as normal evaluation with the complete entity store.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.batched_authorize_ok_equiv
items.doc:
A successful batched authorization returns `isAuthorizedFromResiduals` of a list equivalent to the
policies, so any property of it transfers to the batched path without a second induction.
items.statement:
theorem batched_authorize_ok_equiv
  {schema : Schema} {policies : List Policy} {req : Request}
  {es : Entities} {response : TPE.Response} :
  EntityLoader.WellBehaved es loader →
  schema.validateWellFormed = .ok () →
  validateEntities schema es = .ok () →
  batchedAuthorize schema policies req loader iters = .ok response →
  ∃ rps, response = isAuthorizedFromResiduals rps ∧
    ResidualPoliciesEquiv policies rps req es

items.name: Cedar.Thm.batched_authorize_decision_eq_authorize
items.doc:
The main correctness theorem for batched authorization:
If the batched authorizer reaches a definitive decision, that decision
agrees with the concrete authorizer.
items.statement:
theorem batched_authorize_decision_eq_authorize
  {schema : Schema} {policies : List Policy} {req : Request}
  {es : Entities} {response : TPE.Response} {d : Decision} :
  EntityLoader.WellBehaved es loader →
  schema.validateWellFormed = .ok () →
  validateEntities schema es = .ok () →
  batchedAuthorize schema policies req loader iters = .ok response →
  response.decision = some d →
  (Spec.isAuthorized req es policies).decision = d

modules.doc:
Soundness of batched authorization: if the batched authorizer reaches a
definitive decision, that decision agrees with the concrete authorizer.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.evaluatePolicy_ok_implies_env_some
items.statement:
theorem evaluatePolicy_ok_implies_env_some {schema : Schema} {p : Policy}
  {preq : PartialRequest} {pes : PartialEntities} {r : Residual} :
  evaluatePolicy schema p preq pes = .ok r →
  ∃ env, schema.environment? preq.principal.ty preq.resource.ty preq.action = .some env

items.name: Cedar.Thm.evaluatePolicy_ok_implies_requestMatchesEnvironment
items.statement:
theorem evaluatePolicy_ok_implies_requestMatchesEnvironment
  {schema : Schema} {p : Policy} {req : Request} {r : Residual} {pes : PartialEntities} :
  evaluatePolicy schema p req.asPartialRequest pes = .ok r →
  ∀ env, schema.environment? req.asPartialRequest.principal.ty req.asPartialRequest.resource.ty req.asPartialRequest.action = .some env →
  requestMatchesEnvironment env req

items.name: Cedar.Thm.evaluatePolicy_ok_implies_well_formed_env
items.doc:
If `evaluatePolicy` succeeds on a concrete request, and the schema and entities
pass validation, then `InstanceOfWellFormedEnvironment` holds for the
environment determined by the schema and request.
items.statement:
theorem evaluatePolicy_ok_implies_well_formed_env
  {schema : Schema} {p : Policy} {req : Request} {es : Entities} {r : Residual}
  {pes : PartialEntities} :
  evaluatePolicy schema p req.asPartialRequest pes = .ok r →
  schema.validateWellFormed = .ok () →
  validateEntities schema es = .ok () →
  ∃ env,
    schema.environment? req.asPartialRequest.principal.ty req.asPartialRequest.resource.ty req.asPartialRequest.action = .some env ∧
    InstanceOfWellFormedEnvironment req es env

items.name: Cedar.Thm.ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped
items.statement:
def ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped
  (env : TypeEnv)
  (policies : List Policy)
  (residuals : List ResidualPolicy)
  (req : Request)
  (es : Entities) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.equiv_well_typed_implies_equiv
items.statement:
theorem equiv_well_typed_implies_equiv
  (h : ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped env policies residuals req es) :
  ResidualPoliciesEquiv policies residuals req es

items.name: Cedar.Thm.residuals_equiv_preserved
items.statement:
theorem residuals_equiv_preserved
  {env : TypeEnv} {policies : List Policy} {residuals : List ResidualPolicy}
  {req : Request} {es : Entities} {pes : PartialEntities}
  (h_sound : ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped env policies residuals req es)
  (h_wf : InstanceOfWellFormedEnvironment req es env)
  (h_ref : RequestAndEntitiesRefine req es req.asPartialRequest pes) :
  ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped env policies
    (residuals.map λ rp => ⟨rp.id, rp.effect, Cedar.TPE.evaluate env rp.residual req.asPartialRequest pes⟩)
    req es

items.name: Cedar.Thm.batched_authorize_loop_equiv
items.doc: The loop's response is `isAuthorizedFromResiduals` of a list still equivalent to the policies.
items.statement:
theorem batched_authorize_loop_equiv
  {policies : List Policy} {residuals : List ResidualPolicy} {req : Request}
  (es : Entities) {current_store : PartialEntities} {env : TypeEnv} :
  EntityLoader.WellBehaved es loader →
  ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped env policies residuals req es →
  RequestAndEntitiesRefine req es req.asPartialRequest current_store →
  InstanceOfWellFormedEnvironment req es env →
  ∃ rps, batchedAuthorizeLoop env residuals req loader current_store iters
      = isAuthorizedFromResiduals rps ∧
    ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped env policies rps req es

items.name: Cedar.Thm.batched_authorize_loop_decision_agrees
items.doc: The loop's decision agrees with concrete authorization.
items.statement:
theorem batched_authorize_loop_decision_agrees
  {policies : List Policy} {residuals : List ResidualPolicy} {req : Request}
  (es : Entities) {current_store : PartialEntities} {env : TypeEnv} {d : Decision} :
  EntityLoader.WellBehaved es loader →
  ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped env policies residuals req es →
  RequestAndEntitiesRefine req es req.asPartialRequest current_store →
  InstanceOfWellFormedEnvironment req es env →
  (batchedAuthorizeLoop env residuals req loader current_store iters).decision = some d →
  (Spec.isAuthorized req es policies).decision = d

items.name: Cedar.Thm.evaluatePolicies_equiv_and_well_typed
items.statement:
theorem evaluatePolicies_equiv_and_well_typed
  {schema : Schema} {policies : List Policy} {rps : List ResidualPolicy}
  {req : Request} {es : Entities} {preq : PartialRequest}
  {pes : PartialEntities} {env : TypeEnv} :
  List.Forall₂ (λ p rp => ResidualPolicy.mk p.id p.effect <$> evaluatePolicy schema p preq pes = .ok rp) policies rps →
  schema.environment? preq.principal.ty preq.resource.ty preq.action = .some env →
  InstanceOfWellFormedEnvironment req es env →
  RequestAndEntitiesRefine req es preq pes →
  ResidualPoliciesEquivAndWellTyped env policies rps req es

items.name: Cedar.Thm.EntityLoader.WellBehaved
items.doc:
A well behaved entity loader
1. Loads all the requested entities, returning none for missing entities
2. Refines the backing entity store

The first condition is required for convergence of
batched evaluation, which has not been proven. It is unused
in the code base at the moment.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.batched_evaluate_loop_eq_evaluate
items.statement:
theorem batched_evaluate_loop_eq_evaluate
  {x : Residual}
  {req : Request}
  (es : Entities)
  {current_store : PartialEntities}
  {env : TypeEnv} :
  EntityLoader.WellBehaved es loader →
  Residual.WellTyped env x →
  RequestAndEntitiesRefine req es req.asPartialRequest current_store →
  InstanceOfWellFormedEnvironment req es env →
  (Residual.evaluate (batchedEvaluateLoop env x req loader current_store iters) req es).toOption = (Residual.evaluate x req es).toOption

items.name: bind_ne_error
items.doc:
Monadic bind preserves "not this error": if neither the first computation nor
the continuation (on success) yields error `e`, the bind does not either.
items.statement:
public theorem bind_ne_error {α β ε} {r : Except ε α} {f : α → Except ε β} {e : ε}
  (hr : r ≠ .error e)
  (hf : ∀ a, r = .ok a → f a ≠ .error e) :
  (r >>= f) ≠ .error e

items.name: List.Equiv
items.statement: public def Equiv {α} (a b : List α) : Prop

items.name: List.Equiv.refl

public theorem Equiv.refl {a : List α} :

items.name: List.Equiv.symm

public theorem Equiv.symm {a b : List α} :
  a ≡ b → b ≡ a

items.name: List.Equiv.trans
items.statement:
public theorem Equiv.trans {a b c : List α} :
  a ≡ b → b ≡ c → a ≡ c

items.name: List.equiv_nil
items.statement:
public theorem equiv_nil (xs : List α) :
  xs ≡ [] ↔ xs = []

items.name: List.cons_equiv_cons
items.statement:
public theorem cons_equiv_cons (x : α) (xs ys : List α) :
  xs ≡ ys → x :: xs ≡ x :: ys

items.name: List.cons_equiv_implies_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem cons_equiv_implies_equiv (x : α) (xs ys : List α) :
  x :: xs ≡ x :: ys → x ∉ xs → x ∉ ys → xs ≡ ys

items.name: List.dup_head_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem dup_head_equiv (x : α) (xs : List α) :
  x :: x :: xs ≡ x :: xs

items.name: List.dup_head_equiv'
items.statement:
public theorem dup_head_equiv' {x : α} {xs : List α} :
  x ∈ xs → x :: xs ≡ xs

items.name: List.swap_cons_cons_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem swap_cons_cons_equiv (x₁ x₂ : α) (xs : List α) :
  x₁ :: x₂ :: xs ≡ x₂ :: x₁ :: xs

items.name: List.filter_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem filter_equiv (f : α → Bool) (xs ys : List α) :
  xs ≡ ys → xs.filter f ≡ ys.filter f

items.name: List.map_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem map_equiv (f : α → β) (xs ys : List α) :
  xs ≡ ys → xs.map f ≡ ys.map f

items.name: List.filterMap_equiv

items.name: List.append_swap_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem append_swap_equiv (xs ys : List α) :
  xs ++ ys ≡ ys ++ xs

items.name: List.append_left_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem append_left_equiv (xs ys zs : List α) :
  xs ≡ ys → xs ++ zs ≡ ys ++ zs

items.name: List.append_right_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem append_right_equiv (xs ys zs : List α) :
  ys ≡ zs → xs ++ ys ≡ xs ++ zs

items.name: List.SortedBy
items.statement:
public inductive SortedBy [LT β] (f : α → β) : List α → Prop where
  | nil : SortedBy f []
  | cons_nil {x} : SortedBy f (x :: nil)
  | cons_cons {x y ys} :
      f x < f y →
      SortedBy f (y :: ys) →
      SortedBy f (x :: y :: ys)

items.name: List.Sorted
items.statement: public abbrev Sorted [LT α] (xs : List α)

items.name: List.tail_sortedBy
items.statement:
public theorem tail_sortedBy [LT β] {f : α → β} {x : α} {xs : List α} :
  SortedBy f (x :: xs) → SortedBy f xs

items.name: List.sortedBy_implies_head_lt_tail
items.statement:
public theorem sortedBy_implies_head_lt_tail [LT β] [StrictLT β] {f : α → β} {x : α} {xs : List α} :
  SortedBy f (x :: xs) → ∀ y, y ∈ xs → f x < f y

items.name: List.sortedBy_equiv_implies_head_eq
items.statement:
public theorem sortedBy_equiv_implies_head_eq [LT β] [StrictLT β] (f : α → β) {x y : α} {xs ys : List α} :
  SortedBy f (x :: xs) →
  SortedBy f (y :: ys) →
  (x :: xs) ≡ (y :: ys) →
  x = y

items.name: List.sortedBy_equiv_implies_tail_subset
items.statement:
public theorem sortedBy_equiv_implies_tail_subset [LT β] [StrictLT β] (f : α → β) {x : α} {xs ys : List α} :
  SortedBy f (x :: xs) →
  SortedBy f (x :: ys) →
  (x :: xs) ⊆ (x :: ys) →
  xs ⊆ ys

items.name: List.sortedBy_equiv_implies_tail_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem sortedBy_equiv_implies_tail_equiv [LT β] [StrictLT β] (f : α → β) {x : α} {xs ys : List α} :
  SortedBy f (x :: xs) →
  SortedBy f (x :: ys) →
  (x :: xs) ≡ (x :: ys) →
  xs ≡ ys

items.name: List.sortedBy_equiv_implies_eq
items.statement:
public theorem sortedBy_equiv_implies_eq [LT β] [StrictLT β] (f : α → β) {xs ys : List α} :
  SortedBy f xs → SortedBy f ys → xs ≡ ys → xs = ys

items.name: List.sortedBy_cons
items.statement:
public theorem sortedBy_cons [LT β] [StrictLT β] {f : α → β} {x : α} {ys : List α} :
  SortedBy f ys →
  (∀ y, y ∈ ys → f x < f y) →
  SortedBy f (x :: ys)

items.name: List.mem_of_sortedBy_unique
items.statement:
public theorem mem_of_sortedBy_unique {α β} [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] [DecidableEq β]
  {f : α → β} {x y : α} {xs : List α} :
  xs.SortedBy f → x ∈ xs → y ∈ xs → f x = f y →
  x = y

items.name: List.mem_of_sortedBy_implies_find?
items.statement:
public theorem mem_of_sortedBy_implies_find? {α β} [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] [DecidableEq β]
  {f : α → β} {x : α} {xs : List α} :
  x ∈ xs → xs.SortedBy f →
  xs.find? (fun y => f y == f x) = x

items.name: List.map_eq_implies_sortedBy
List.filter_sortedBy
items.statement:
public theorem filter_sortedBy [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] {f : α → β} (p : α → Bool) {xs : List α} :
  SortedBy f xs → SortedBy f (xs.filter p)

items.name: List.filterMap_sortedBy
items.statement:
public theorem filterMap_sortedBy [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] {f : α → β} {g : α → Option γ} {f' : γ → β} {xs : List α} :
  (∀ x y, g x = some y → f x = f' y) →
  SortedBy f xs →
  SortedBy f' (xs.filterMap g)

List.mapM_key_id_sortedBy_key
items.statement:

items.name: List.isSortedBy_correct
items.statement:
public theorem isSortedBy_correct {α β} [LT β] [DecidableLT β] {l : List α} {f : α → β} :
  l.SortedBy f ↔ l.isSortedBy f

items.name: List.isSorted_correct

items.name: List.Forallᵥ
items.statement: public def Forallᵥ {α β γ} (p : β → γ → Prop) (kvs₁ : List (α × β)) (kvs₂ : List (α × γ)) : Prop

items.name: List.forallᵥ_def
items.statement:
public theorem forallᵥ_def {α β γ} {p : β → γ → Prop} {kvs₁ : List (α × β)} {kvs₂ : List (α × γ)} :
  List.Forallᵥ p kvs₁ kvs₂ = List.Forall₂ (λ kv₁ kv₂ => kv₁.fst = kv₂.fst ∧ p kv₁.snd kv₂.snd) kvs₁ kvs₂

modules.title: Properties of list canonicalization
modules.doc: This file contains lemmas about list canonicalization.

items.name: List.insertCanonical_singleton
items.statement:
public theorem insertCanonical_singleton [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β)  (x : α) :
  insertCanonical f x [] = [x]

items.name: List.insertCanonical_not_nil
items.statement:
public theorem insertCanonical_not_nil [DecidableEq β] [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (x : α) (xs : List α) :
  insertCanonical f x xs ≠ []

items.name: List.insertCanonical_mem
items.statement:
public theorem insertCanonical_mem [LT β] [Cedar.Data.StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β]
  {f : α → β} {xs : List α} (x : α) :
  x ∈ List.insertCanonical f x xs

items.name: List.insertCanonical_find?
items.statement:
public theorem insertCanonical_find?
  [LT β] [Cedar.Data.StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] [BEq β] [LawfulBEq β]
  {f : α → β} {xs : List α} (x : α) :
  (List.insertCanonical f x xs).find? (λ e => f e == f x) = x

items.name: List.insertCanonical_preserves_non_duplicate_element
items.statement:
theorem insertCanonical_preserves_non_duplicate_element
  [LT β] [Cedar.Data.StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] [DecidableEq β]
  {f : α → β} {xs : List α} {x : α} {y : α}
  (hmem : y ∈ xs)
  (hneq : f x ≠ f y) :
  y ∈ List.insertCanonical f x xs

items.name: List.insertCanonical_preserves_find_other_element
items.statement:
public theorem insertCanonical_preserves_find_other_element
  [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [BEq α] [StrictLT α]
  (k : α)
  (x : (α × β)) (xs : List (α × β))  :
  (x.fst == k) = false →
  (List.insertCanonical Prod.fst x xs).find? (λ x => x.fst == k) =
  xs.find? (λ x => x.fst == k)

items.name: List.insertCanonical_sortedBy
List.insertCanonical_cases
items.statement:
theorem insertCanonical_cases [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (x y : α) (ys : List α) :
  (f x < f y ∧ insertCanonical f x (y :: ys) = x :: y :: ys) ∨
  (¬ f x < f y ∧ f x > f y ∧ insertCanonical f x (y :: ys) = y :: insertCanonical f x ys) ∨
  (¬ f x < f y ∧ ¬ f x > f y ∧ insertCanonical f x (y :: ys) = x :: ys)

items.name: List.insertCanonical_subset
items.statement:
public theorem insertCanonical_subset [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (x : α) (xs : List α) :
  insertCanonical f x xs ⊆ x :: xs

items.name: List.insertCanonical_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem insertCanonical_equiv [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] (x : α) (xs : List α) :
  x :: xs ≡ insertCanonical id x xs

items.name: List.insertCanonical_preserves_forallᵥ
List.insertCanonical_map_fst
List.insertCanonical_map_fst_canonicalize
List.canonicalize_nil
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_nil [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) :
  canonicalize f [] = []

items.name: List.canonicalize_nil'
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_nil' [DecidableEq β] [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (xs : List α) :
  xs = [] ↔ (canonicalize f xs) = []

items.name: List.canonicalize_not_nil
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_not_nil [DecidableEq β] [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (xs : List α) :
  xs ≠ [] ↔ (canonicalize f xs) ≠ []

items.name: List.canonicalize_cons
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_cons [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (xs : List α) (a : α) :
  canonicalize f xs = canonicalize f ys → canonicalize f (a :: xs) = canonicalize f (a :: ys)

items.name: List.canonicalize_singleton
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_singleton [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (x : α) :
  canonicalize f [x] = [x]

items.name: List.canonicalize_sortedBy
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_sortedBy [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (xs : List α) :
  SortedBy f (canonicalize f xs)

items.name: List.sortedBy_implies_canonicalize_eq
items.statement:
public theorem sortedBy_implies_canonicalize_eq [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] {f : α → β} {xs : List α} :
  SortedBy f xs → (canonicalize f xs) = xs

items.name: List.canonicalize_subseteq
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_subseteq [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (xs : List α) :
  xs.canonicalize f ⊆ xs

items.name: List.in_canonicalize_in_list
items.doc: Corollary of `canonicalize_subseteq`
items.statement:
public theorem in_canonicalize_in_list [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] {f : α → β} {x : α} {xs : List α} :
  x ∈ xs.canonicalize f → x ∈ xs

items.name: List.canonicalize_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_equiv [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] (xs : List α) :
  xs ≡ canonicalize id xs

items.name: List.equiv_implies_canonical_eq
items.statement:
public theorem equiv_implies_canonical_eq [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] (xs ys : List α) :
  xs ≡ ys → (canonicalize id xs) = (canonicalize id ys)

items.name: List.canonicalize_idempotent
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_idempotent {α β} [LT β] [StrictLT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (xs : List α) :
  canonicalize f (canonicalize f xs) = canonicalize f xs

items.name: List.canonicalize_id_filter
items.statement:
public theorem canonicalize_id_filter {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) :
  (canonicalize id xs).filter p = (xs.filter p).canonicalize id

items.name: List.canonicalize_preserves_forallᵥ
List.canonicalize_of_map_fst
List.list_find?_in_tail
items.doc:
If the head of the list is not k, then finding in the tail
returns the same result as finding the entire list.
items.statement:
public theorem list_find?_in_tail
  [LT β] [DecidableLT β] [BEq β] [LawfulBEq β] [StrictLT β]
  {f : α → β} {hd : α} {tl : List α} {k : β} :
  (f hd == k) = false →
  (List.canonicalize f (hd :: tl)).find? (λ x => f x == k) =
  (List.canonicalize f tl).find? (λ x => f x == k)

items.name: List.list_find?_at_head
items.doc:
If the head of the list matches k, then finding in the canonicalized list
returns that head element.
items.statement:
public theorem list_find?_at_head
  [LT β] [DecidableLT β] [BEq β] [LawfulBEq β] [StrictLT β]
  {f : α → β} {hd : α} {tl : List α} {k : β} :
  (f hd == k) = true →
  (List.canonicalize f (hd :: tl)).find? (λ x => f x == k) = some hd

items.name: List.mergeCanonical_nil_left
items.statement:
public theorem mergeCanonical_nil_left [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (ys : List α) :
  mergeCanonical [] ys = ys

items.name: List.mergeCanonical_nil_right
items.statement:
public theorem mergeCanonical_nil_right [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (xs : List α) :
  mergeCanonical xs [] = xs

items.name: List.mem_mergeCanonical
items.doc: Membership in a merge does not require its inputs to be canonical.
items.statement:
public theorem mem_mergeCanonical [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {xs ys : List α} {a : α} :
  a ∈ mergeCanonical xs ys ↔ a ∈ xs ∨ a ∈ ys

items.name: List.mergeCanonical_self
items.doc: Merging a list with itself does not require the list to be canonical.
items.statement:
public theorem mergeCanonical_self [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (xs : List α) :
  mergeCanonical xs xs = xs

items.name: List.mergeCanonical_comm
items.doc: Merging is commutative even if its inputs are not canonical.
items.statement:
public theorem mergeCanonical_comm [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (xs ys : List α) :
  mergeCanonical xs ys = mergeCanonical ys xs

items.name: List.mergeCanonical_assoc
items.doc: Merging is associative even if its inputs are not canonical.
items.statement:
public theorem mergeCanonical_assoc [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (xs ys zs : List α) :
  mergeCanonical (mergeCanonical xs ys) zs = mergeCanonical xs (mergeCanonical ys zs)

items.name: List.mergeCanonical_sortedBy
items.statement:
public theorem mergeCanonical_sortedBy [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {xs ys : List α} :
  xs.SortedBy id → ys.SortedBy id → (mergeCanonical xs ys).SortedBy id

modules.title: Properties of Lists
modules.doc:
This file contains useful lemmas about standard list functions and
our custom variations on these.

items.name: List.any_of_mem
items.statement:
public theorem any_of_mem {f : α → Bool} {x : α} {xs : List α}
  (h₁ : x ∈ xs)
  (h₂ : f x) :
  any xs f = true

items.name: List.all_pmap_subtype
items.doc: Copied from Mathlib. We can delete this if it gets added to Batteries.
items.statement:
public theorem all_pmap_subtype
  {p : α → Prop}
  (f : α → Bool)
  (as : List α)
  (h : ∀ a, a ∈ as → p a)
  : List.all (List.pmap Subtype.mk as h) (λ x : { a : α // p a } => f x.val)
    =
    List.all as f

items.note: ### map, map₁, map₂, map₃, and `attach` variants

items.name: List.map_congr
items.doc: Copied from Mathlib. We can delete this if it gets added to Batteries.
items.statement:
public theorem map_congr {f g : α → β} : ∀ {l : List α},
  (∀ x ∈ l, f x = g x) → map f l = map g l

items.name: List.map_eq_doubleton
items.doc:
Similar to the standard library's `map_eq_singleton_iff`, but for doubleton.

We could probably make this an iff but currently don't need to.

items.name: List.map_pmap_subtype
items.doc: Copied from Mathlib. We can delete this if it gets added to Batteries.
items.statement:
public theorem map_pmap_subtype
  {p : α → Prop}
  (f : α → β)
  (as : List α)
  (h : ∀ a, a ∈ as → p a)
  : List.map (λ x : { a : α // p a } => f x.val) (List.pmap Subtype.mk as h)
    =
    List.map f as

items.name: List.map_pmap_subtype_snd
items.doc:
Not actually a special case of `map_pmap_subtype` -- you can use this in
places you can't use `map_pmap_subtype` because the LHS function (being
mapped) doesn't fit the `map_pmap_subtype` form but does fit this form (where
the application of `f` is not the outermost AST node of the function,
basically)
items.statement:
public theorem map_pmap_subtype_snd
  {p : (α × β) → Prop}
  (f : β → γ)
  (xs : List (α × β))
  (h : ∀ pair ∈ xs, p pair)
  : List.map (λ x : { pair : (α × β) // p pair } => (x.val.fst, f x.val.snd)) (List.pmap Subtype.mk xs h)
    =
    xs.map λ pair => (pair.fst, f pair.snd)

items.name: List.attach_def
items.statement:
public theorem attach_def {as : List α} :
  as.attach = pmap Subtype.mk as λ _ => id

items.name: List.mem_attach₂
items.statement:
public theorem mem_attach₂ [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β] {as : List (α × β)} {pair : {x : α × β // sizeOf x.snd < 1 + sizeOf as}} :
  pair ∈ as.attach₂ → (pair.val.fst, pair.val.snd) ∈ as

items.name: List.mem_attach₂_iff
items.statement:
public theorem mem_attach₂_iff [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β] {xs : List (α × β)} {pair : {x : α × β // sizeOf x.snd < 1 + sizeOf xs}} :
  pair ∈ xs.attach₂ ↔ pair.val ∈ xs

items.name: List.all_attach₂
items.statement:
public theorem all_attach₂ [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β] {as : List (α × β)} {f : (α × β) → Bool} :
  as.attach₂.all (λ ⟨pair, _⟩ => f pair) = as.all f

items.name: List.all_attach₂_snd
items.statement:
public theorem all_attach₂_snd [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β] {as : List (α × β)} {f : β → Bool} :
  as.attach₂.all (λ ⟨(_, b), _⟩ => f b) = as.all λ (_, b) => f b

items.name: List.map₁_eq_map
List.map₂_eq_map
List.map₃_eq_map
List.map₂_eq_map_snd
items.doc:
Not actually a special case of `map₂_eq_map` -- you can use this in places you
can't use `map₂_eq_map` because the LHS function (being mapped) doesn't fit
the `map₂_eq_map` form but does fit this form (where the application of `f` is
not the outermost AST node of the function, basically)

items.name: List.map₃_eq_map_snd
items.doc: same as `map₂_eq_map_snd` but for `map₃`

items.name: List.exists_iff_mem_flatMap
items.doc:
As of this writing, the standard-library lemma `List.exists_of_mem_flatMap` is a
`→`, but it's trivial to extend it to `↔` and makes some things easier, so we do
that here

public theorem exists_iff_mem_flatMap {α β} [DecidableEq β] {f : α → List β} {xs : List α} {b : β} :

items.doc: In key-preserving related lists, an entry found for a key has a related entry found for it.
items.statement:
public theorem forall₂_find?_some {α β} [DecidableEq α]
  {r : α × β → α × β → Prop} {xs ys : List (α × β)} {k : α} {x : α × β}
  (hkeys : ∀ x y, r x y → y.fst = x.fst)
  (hrel : List.Forall₂ r xs ys)
  (hfind : xs.find? (·.fst == k) = some x) :
  ∃ y, ys.find? (·.fst == k) = some y ∧ r x y

items.statement:
theorem mapM_pmap_subtype [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
  {p : α → Prop}
  (f : α → m β)
  (as : List α)
  (h : ∀ a, a ∈ as → p a)
  : List.mapM (λ x : { a : α // p a } => f x.val) (List.pmap Subtype.mk as h)
    =
    List.mapM f as

items.name: List.mapM_pmap_subtype_snd
items.statement:
theorem mapM_pmap_subtype_snd [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
  {p : (α × β) → Prop}
  (f : β → m γ)
  (xs : List (α × β))
  (h : ∀ pair ∈ xs, p pair)
  : (List.mapM (λ x : { pair : (α × β) // p pair } => do pure (x.val.fst, ← f x.val.snd))) (List.pmap Subtype.mk xs h)
    =
    (xs.mapM λ pair => do pure (pair.fst, ← f pair.snd))

modules.title: Map properties
modules.doc:
This file proves useful properties of canonical list-based maps defined in
`Cedar.Data.Map`.

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.if_wellformed_then_exists_make
items.statement:

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.wf_iff_sorted

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.wf_empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.key_maps_to_one_value
items.doc:
In well-formed maps, if there are two pairs with the same key, then they have
the same value
items.statement:
public theorem key_maps_to_one_value [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (k : α) (v₁ v₂ : β) (m : Map α β) :
  m.WellFormed →
  (k, v₁) ∈ m.toList →
  (k, v₂) ∈ m.toList →
  v₁ = v₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.eq_iff_toList_eq
items.doc:
If two maps have exactly equal (k,v) sets, then the maps are equal

This doesn't require WellFormed, but we use it in the proof of
`eq_iff_toList_equiv` below
items.statement:
public theorem eq_iff_toList_eq {m₁ m₂ : Map α β} :
  m₁.toList = m₂.toList ↔ m₁ = m₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.eq_iff_toList_equiv
items.doc:
If two well-formed maps have equivalent (k,v) sets, then the maps are actually
equal
items.statement:
public theorem eq_iff_toList_equiv [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {m₁ m₂ : Map α β}
  (wf₁ : m₁.WellFormed)
  (wf₂ : m₂.WellFormed) :
  m₁.toList ≡ m₂.toList ↔ m₁ = m₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mem_make_mem_list
items.doc:
Note that the converse of this is not true:
counterexample `xs = [(1, false), (1, true)]`.
(The property here would not hold for either `x = (1, false)` or `x = (1, true)`.)

For a limited converse, see `mem_list_mem_make` below.
items.statement:
public theorem mem_make_mem_list [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {xs : List (α × β)} :
  x ∈ (Map.make xs).toList → x ∈ xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.make_cons

Note that the converse of this is not true:
counterexample `xs = [(1, false)]`, `ys = []`, `ab = (1, false)`.

  make xs = make ys → make (ab :: xs) = make (ab :: ys)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.singleton_contains

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.list_find?_some_iff_map_find?_some
Cedar.Data.Map.list_find?_mapM_implies_exists_mapped
items.statement:
public theorem list_find?_mapM_implies_exists_mapped {α β γ : Type} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] {ls : List (α × β)} (fn : β → Option γ) {ys: List (α × γ)} {k: α} {x : β} :
  List.mapM (fun x =>
              (fn x.2).bind
                (fun v => some (x.fst, v))) ls = some ys →
  ls.find? (λ x => x.1 == k) = .some (k, x) →
  ∃y, fn x = .some y ∧  ys.find? (λ x => x.1 == k) = .some (k, y)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.list_find?_mapM_implies_exists_unmapped
items.statement:

  List.mapM (fun x =>
              (fn x.2).bind
                (fun v => some (x.fst, v))) ls = some ys →
  ys.find? (λ x => x.1 == k) = .some (k, y) →
  ∃ x, fn x = some y ∧ (ls.find? (λ x => x.1 == k) = .some (k, x))

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapOnValues_mapOnValues

public theorem mapOnValues_congr {f g : β → γ} {m : Map α β} :

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_mapOnValues
items.statement:
public theorem findOrErr_mapOnValues [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {f : β → γ} {m : Map α β} {k : α} {e : Error} :
  (m.mapOnValues f).findOrErr k e = (m.findOrErr k e).map f

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_ok_iff_find?_some
items.statement:
public theorem findOrErr_ok_iff_find?_some [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} {e : Error} :
  m.findOrErr k e = .ok v ↔ m.find? k = some v

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_err_iff_find?_none
items.statement:
public theorem findOrErr_err_iff_find?_none [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {m : Map α β} {k : α} {e : Error} :
  m.findOrErr k e = .error e ↔ m.find? k = none

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_eq_match
items.doc: Equation lemma for `findOrErr`, for clients that cannot unfold it.
items.statement:
public theorem findOrErr_eq_match {α β ε} [BEq α] (m : Map α β) (k : α) (e : ε) :
  m.findOrErr k e = match m.find? k with | some v => .ok v | _ => .error e

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_ok_implies_in_toList
items.doc:
The converse requires the `wf` precondition, and is available in
`findOrErr_ok_iff_in_toList` below
items.statement:
public theorem findOrErr_ok_implies_in_toList [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} {e : Error} :
  m.findOrErr k e = .ok v → (k, v) ∈ m.toList

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_ok_iff_in_toList
items.doc:
The `mp` direction of this does not need the `wf` precondition and, in fact,
is available separately as `findOrErr_ok_implies_in_toList` above

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find?_some_implies_in_values
items.doc:
The converse requires the `wf` precondition, and is available in

items.statement:
public theorem find?_some_implies_in_values [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} :
  m.find? k = .some v → v ∈ m.values

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_ok_implies_in_values
items.doc:
The converse requires the `wf` precondition, and is available in
`findOrErr_ok_iff_in_values` below
items.statement:
public theorem findOrErr_ok_implies_in_values [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} {e : Error} :
  m.findOrErr k e = .ok v → v ∈ m.values

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find?_some_iff_in_values
items.doc:
The `mp` direction of this does not need the `wf` precondition and, in fact,
is available separately as `find?_some_implies_in_values` above

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.findOrErr_ok_iff_in_values
items.doc:
The `mp` direction of this does not need the `wf` precondition and, in fact,

Cedar.Data.Map.in_toList_in_mapOnValues
items.doc:
The converse requires the extra precondition that `f` is injective, and is
available as `in_mapOnValues_in_toList`
items.statement:
public theorem in_toList_in_mapOnValues [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] (f : β → γ) {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} :
  (k, v) ∈ m.toList → (k, f v) ∈ (m.mapOnValues f).toList

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find?_none_iff_findorErr_errors
items.doc: TODO: This is redundant with `findOrErr_err_iff_find?_none`
items.statement:
public theorem find?_none_iff_findorErr_errors [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {m : Map α β} {k : α} (e : Error) :
  m.find? k = none ↔ m.findOrErr k e = .error e

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.in_mapOnValues_in_toList
items.doc: Converse of `in_toList_in_mapOnValues`; requires the extra precondition that `f` is injective
items.statement:
public theorem in_mapOnValues_in_toList [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] {f : β → γ} {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} :
  (k, f v) ∈ (m.mapOnValues f).toList →
  (∀ v', f v = f v' → v = v') → -- require f to be injective
  (k, v) ∈ m.toList

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.in_mapOnValues_in_toList'
items.doc: Slightly different formulation of `in_mapOnValues_in_toList`

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues₂_eq_mapMOnValues
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues₂_eq_mapMOnValues {α β γ : Type 0} [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β] [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (map : Map α β) (f : β → m γ) :
  map.mapMOnValues₂ (λ x : { x : β // sizeOf x < sizeOf map } => f x.1) = map.mapMOnValues f

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_empty
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_empty [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (f : β → m γ) :
  (empty : Map α β).mapMOnValues f = pure empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_mapOnValues
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_mapOnValues [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (map : Map α β) (f : β → γ) (g : γ → m φ) :
  mapMOnValues g (map.mapOnValues f) = map.mapMOnValues (g ∘ f)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some
items.doc: Mapping every value to `some` preserves the map.
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_some {α β} [LT α] [DecidableLT α]
    (m : Map α β) :
    m.mapMOnValues some = some m

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_isSome
items.doc: Mapping map values succeeds exactly when every application succeeds.
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_isSome {α β γ} [LT α] [DecidableLT α]
    (m : Map α β) (f : β → Option γ) :
    (m.mapMOnValues f).isSome = m.values.all (fun value => (f value).isSome)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_preserves_keys
items.doc:
This is not stated in terms of `Map.keys` because `Map.keys` produces a `Set`,
and we want the even stronger property that it not only preserves the key-set,
but also the key-order. (We'll use this to prove `mapMOnValues_some_wf`.)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some_wf
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_some_wf [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {f : β → Option γ} {m₁ : Map α β} {m₂ : Map α γ} :
  m₁.WellFormed →
  (m₁.mapMOnValues f = some m₂) →
  m₂.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some_wf_alt_proof
items.doc:
Alternate proof of `mapMOnValues_some_wf`, that relies on
`List.mapM_some_eq_filterMap` instead of `mapMOnValues_preserves_keys`. Which do
we prefer?
items.statement:
theorem mapMOnValues_some_wf_alt_proof [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {f : β → Option γ} {m₁ : Map α β} {m₂ : Map α γ} :
  m₁.WellFormed →
  (m₁.mapMOnValues f = some m₂) →
  m₂.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_ok_wf
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_ok_wf [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {f : β → Except ε γ} {m₁ : Map α β} {m₂ : Map α γ} :
  m₁.WellFormed →
  (m₁.mapMOnValues f = .ok m₂) →
  m₂.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_cons
Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some_implies_forall₂
items.statement:
theorem mapMOnValues_some_implies_forall₂ [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Option γ} {m₁ : Map α β} {m₂ : Map α γ} :
  m₁.mapMOnValues f = some m₂ →
  List.Forall₂ (λ kv₁ kv₂ => kv₁.fst = kv₂.fst ∧ f kv₁.snd = some kv₂.snd) m₁.toList m₂.toList

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapOnValues_eq_of_mapMOnValues_some
items.doc:
If a partial map of values succeeds, mapping a corresponding total function
produces the same map.
items.statement:
public theorem mapOnValues_eq_of_mapMOnValues_some
    {α β γ} [LT α] [DecidableLT α]
    {m : Map α β} {out : Map α γ} {f : β → Option γ}
    (g : β → γ)
    (hmap : m.mapMOnValues f = some out)
    (hfg : ∀ input output, f input = some output → g input = output) :
    m.mapOnValues g = out

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_some
Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_some_alt_proof
items.doc:
alternate proof of `mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_some`, which instead of
relying on `mapMOnValues_some_implies_forall₂`, relies on
`List.mapM_some_implies_all_some`.  Which do we prefer?
items.statement:
theorem mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_some_alt_proof [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Option γ} {m₁ : Map α β} {m₂ : Map α γ} :
  m₁.mapMOnValues f = some m₂ →
  ∀ kv ∈ m₁.toList, ∃ v, (kv.fst, v) ∈ m₂.toList ∧ f kv.snd = some v

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_from_some
Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_from_some_alt_proof
items.doc:
alternate proof of `mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_from_some`, which instead of
relying on `mapMOnValues_some_implies_forall₂`, relies on
`List.mapM_some_implies_all_from_some`. Which do we prefer?
items.statement:
theorem mapMOnValues_some_implies_all_from_some_alt_proof [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Option γ} {m₁ : Map α β} {m₂ : Map α γ} :
  m₁.mapMOnValues f = some m₂ →
  ∀ kv ∈ m₂.toList, ∃ v, (kv.fst, v) ∈ m₁.toList ∧ f v = kv.snd

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_none_iff_exists_none
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_none_iff_exists_none {α : Type 0} [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Option γ} {m : Map α β} :
  m.mapMOnValues f = none ↔ ∃ v ∈ m.values, f v = none

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_ok_implies_all_ok
items.doc:
Note that the converse is not true:
counterexample `m₁` is `[(1, false)]`, `m₂` is `[(1, false), (2, true)]`, `f` is `Except.ok`

But for a limited converse, see `all_ok_implies_mapMOnValues_ok`

Cedar.Data.Map.all_ok_implies_mapMOnValues_ok
Cedar.Data.Map.mapMOnValues_error_implies_exists_error
items.statement:
public theorem mapMOnValues_error_implies_exists_error [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Except ε γ} {m : Map α β} {e : ε} :
  m.mapMOnValues f = .error e → ∃ v ∈ m.values, f v = .error e

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.wellFormed_correct
items.statement:
public theorem wellFormed_correct {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {m : Map α β} :
  m.wellFormed = true ↔ m.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.make_find?_eq_list_find?
items.statement:
public theorem make_find?_eq_list_find?
  [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α]
  [Cedar.Data.StrictLT α]
  {l : List (α × β)}
  {k : α} :
  (make l).find? k = (List.find? (λ x => x.fst == k) l).map Prod.snd

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.make_toList_map_find?
items.doc: Rebuilding a map from its entries with key-dependent values.
items.statement:
public theorem make_toList_map_find? {α β γ}
  [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α]
  (m : Map α β) (g : α → β → γ) (k : α) :
  (Map.make (m.toList.map fun kv => (kv.fst, g kv.fst kv.snd))).find? k =
    (m.find? k).map (g k)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.list_find?_iff_make_find?
items.statement:
public theorem list_find?_iff_make_find?
  [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α]
  [Cedar.Data.StrictLT α]
  {l : List (α × β)}
  {k : α} {v : β} :
  List.find? (λ x => x.fst == k) l = some (k, v) ↔
  (make l).find? k = some v

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.list_find?_iff_mk_find?
items.statement:
public theorem list_find?_iff_mk_find?
  [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α]
  [Cedar.Data.StrictLT α]
  {l : List (α × β)}
  {k : α} {v : β} :
  List.find? (λ x => x.fst == k) l = some (k, v) ↔
  (mk l).find? k = some v

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.map_make_append_find_disjoint
items.doc:
If a key exists in `l₂` but not in `l₁`,
then `Map.make (l₁ ++ l₂)` contains that key.
items.statement:
public theorem map_make_append_find_disjoint
  [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableLT α]
  [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β]
  {l₁ : List (α × β)} {l₂ : List (α × β)} {k : α}
  (hfind₁ : l₁.find? (λ ⟨k', _⟩ => k' == k) = none)
  (hfind₂ : (l₂.find? (λ ⟨k', _⟩ => k' == k)).isSome) :
  ∃ v,
    (Map.make (l₁ ++ l₂)).find? k = some v ∧
    (k, v) ∈ l₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.make_map_values_find
Cedar.Data.Map.map_toList_findSome?
items.statement:
public theorem map_toList_findSome?
  [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
  {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} {v' : γ}
  {f : α × β → Option γ}
  (hfind : Map.find? m k = .some v)
  (hf : ∀ kv, (∃ v', f kv = .some v') → kv.1 = k)
  (hkv : f (k, v) = .some v') :
  m.toList.findSome? f = .some v'

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.map_find?_to_list_find?
items.statement:
public theorem map_find?_to_list_find?
  [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
  {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β}
  (hfind : Map.find? m k = .some v) :
  List.find? (λ x => x.fst == k) (Map.toList m) = .some (k, v)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.map_make_append_find_disjoint'
items.doc: A variant of `map_make_append_find_disjoint`.
items.statement:
public theorem map_make_append_find_disjoint'
  [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableLT α]
  [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β]
  {l₁ : List (α × β)} {l₂ : List (α × β)} {k : α} {v : β}
  (hfind₁ : l₁.find? (λ ⟨k', _⟩ => k' == k) = none)
  (hfind₂ : l₂.find? (λ ⟨k', _⟩ => k' == k) = .some (k, v))
  (heq : ∀ x₁ x₂, x₁ ∈ l₂ → x₂ ∈ l₂ → x₁.fst = x₂.fst → x₁ = x₂) :
  (Map.make (l₁ ++ l₂)).find? k = some v

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.map_find?_implies_find?_weaker_pred
items.statement:
public theorem map_find?_implies_find?_weaker_pred
  [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
  {m : Map α β} {k : α} {v : β} {f : α × β → Bool}
  (hfind : Map.find? m k = .some v)
  (hf : ∀ kv, f kv → kv.1 = k)
  (hkv : f (k, v)) :
  List.find? f (Map.toList m) = .some (k, v)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.map_keys_empty_implies_map_empty
items.statement:
public theorem map_keys_empty_implies_map_empty
  {m : Map α β}
  (h : m.keys.toList = []) :
