items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find?_append
items.statement:
public theorem find?_append
  [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableLT α]
  {m₁ m₂ : Map α β} {k : α}:
  (m₁ ++ m₂).find? k = (m₁.find? k).or (m₂.find? k)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.contains_append
items.statement:
public theorem contains_append
  [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α][DecidableEq α] {m₁ m₂ : Map α β} {k : α} :
  (m₁ ++ m₂).contains k ↔ m₁.contains k ∨ m₂.contains k

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find?_append_right
items.statement:
public theorem find?_append_right
  [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableLT α]
  {m₁ m₂ : Map α β} {k : α} :
  m₁.contains k = false → (m₁ ++ m₂).find? k = m₂.find? k

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find?_append_left
items.statement:
public theorem find?_append_left
  [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableLT α]
  {m₁ m₂ : Map α β} {k : α} :
  m₂.contains k = false → (m₁ ++ m₂).find? k = m₁.find? k

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.filter_wf
Cedar.Data.Map.find?_filter_if_find?
items.statement:
public theorem find?_filter_if_find? {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
  {k : α} {val : β} {m : Map α β} {p : α → β → Bool} :
  m.find? k = some val → p k val = true →
  ((m.filter p).find? k = some val)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find?_filter_iff_find
items.statement:
public theorem find?_filter_iff_find {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α]
  {k : α} {val : β} {m : Map α β} {p : α → β → Bool} :
  m.WellFormed →
  ((m.find? k = some val ∧ p k val = true) ↔ ((m.filter p).find? k = some val))

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.filter_contains_if_find_matching
items.statement:
public theorem filter_contains_if_find_matching {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
  {k : α} {m : Map α β} {p : α → β → Bool} :
  (∃ v, m.find? k = some v ∧ p k v = true) → (m.filter p).contains k

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.find_matching_iff_filter_contains
items.statement:
public theorem find_matching_iff_filter_contains {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α]
  {k : α} {m : Map α β} (p : α → β → Bool) :
  m.WellFormed →
  ((∃ v, m.find? k = some v ∧ p k v = true) ↔ (m.filter p).contains k)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Map.filter_not_contains
items.statement:
public theorem filter_not_contains {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (k : α) (m : Map α β) :
  (m.filter (λ k' _ => k' != k)|>.contains k) = false

items.note: ### List.mapUnion generically (`f` returning any collection type)

items.name: List.mapUnion_pmap_subtype
items.statement:
theorem mapUnion_pmap_subtype
  [Union β] [EmptyCollection β]
  {p : α → Prop}
  (f : α → β)
  (as : List α)
  (h : ∀ a, a ∈ as → p a) :
    List.mapUnion (λ x : { a : α // p a } => f x.val) (List.pmap Subtype.mk as h)
    =
    List.mapUnion f as

items.name: List.mapUnion₁_eq_mapUnion
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion₁_eq_mapUnion [Union β] [EmptyCollection β] (f : α → β) (as : List α) :
  as.mapUnion₁ (λ x : { a : α // a ∈ as } => f x.val) = as.mapUnion f

items.name: List.mapUnion₂_eq_mapUnion
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion₂_eq_mapUnion [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β] [Union γ] [EmptyCollection γ] (f : (α × β) → γ) (xs : List (α × β)) :
  xs.mapUnion₂ (λ x : { x : α × β // sizeOf x.snd < 1 + sizeOf xs } => f x.1) = xs.mapUnion f

items.name: List.mapUnion₃_eq_mapUnion
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion₃_eq_mapUnion [SizeOf α] [SizeOf β] [Union γ] [EmptyCollection γ] (f : (α × β) → γ) (xs : List (α × β)) :
  xs.mapUnion₃ (λ x : { x : α × β // sizeOf x.snd < 1 + (1 + sizeOf xs) } => f x.1) = xs.mapUnion f

items.name: List.mapUnion_nil
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_nil [Union β] [EmptyCollection β] (f : α → β) :
  [].mapUnion f = ∅

items.name: List.mapUnion_wf
List.mapUnion_cons
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_cons {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {hd : β} {tl : List β} :
  (hd :: tl).mapUnion f = f hd ∪ tl.mapUnion f

items.name: List.mapUnion_singleton
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_singleton {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {x : β} :
  [x].mapUnion f = f x

items.name: List.mapUnion_pair
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_pair {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {x y : β} :
  [x, y].mapUnion f = f x ∪ f y

items.name: List.mapUnion_map
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_map [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {g : γ → β} {xs : List γ} :
  List.mapUnion f (xs.map g) = xs.mapUnion (f ∘ g)

items.name: List.mem_foldl_union_iff_mem_or_exists
items.statement:
public theorem mem_foldl_union_iff_mem_or_exists {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {xs : List β} {init : Set α} {a : α} :
  a ∈ List.foldl (λ as b => as ∪ f b) init xs ↔ (a ∈ init ∨ ∃ s ∈ xs, a ∈ f s)

items.name: List.foldl_union_wf
items.doc: A fold of unions is well-formed if it starts from a well-formed set and adds well-formed sets.

items.name: List.mem_mapUnion_iff_mem_exists
items.statement:
public theorem mem_mapUnion_iff_mem_exists {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {xs : List β} :
  ∀ e, e ∈ xs.mapUnion f ↔ ∃ s ∈ xs, e ∈ f s

items.name: List.mem_mem_implies_mem_mapUnion
items.statement:
public theorem mem_mem_implies_mem_mapUnion {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {xs : List β} {e : α} {s : β} :
  e ∈ f s → s ∈ xs → e ∈ xs.mapUnion f

items.name: List.mem_implies_subset_mapUnion
items.statement:
public theorem mem_implies_subset_mapUnion {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] (f : β → Set α) {xs : List β} {s : β} :
  s ∈ xs → f s ⊆ xs.mapUnion f

items.name: List.mapUnion_filterMap
List.mapUnion_congr
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_congr {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] (f g : β → Set α) {xs : List β} :
  (∀ b ∈ xs, f b = g b) → xs.mapUnion f = xs.mapUnion g

items.name: List.mapUnion_eq_mapUnion_id_map
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_eq_mapUnion_id_map {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] (f : β → Set α) {xs : List β} :
  xs.mapUnion f = (xs.map f).mapUnion id

items.name: List.mapUnion_eq_of_map_eq
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_eq_of_map_eq {α β γ} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {f : β → Set α} {g : γ → Set α} {xs : List β} {ys : List γ} :
  xs.map f = ys.map g → xs.mapUnion f = ys.mapUnion g

items.name: List.mapUnion_append
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_append {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f : β → Set α} {xs ys : List β} :
  (xs ++ ys).mapUnion f = xs.mapUnion f ++ ys.mapUnion f

items.name: List.mapUnion_union_mapUnion
items.doc: Corollary of `mapUnion_append`, stated in reverse for some reason, and using `∪` instead of `++` (which are synonyms in the case of Data.Set)
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_union_mapUnion {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] (f : β → Set α) (xs ys : List β) :
  List.mapUnion f xs ∪ List.mapUnion f ys = List.mapUnion f (xs ++ ys)

items.name: List.mapUnion_union_mapUnion'
items.doc:
`mapUnion_union_mapUnion` applies when you have the same function `f` and different input lists.
`mapUnion_union_mapUnion'` applies when you have different functions `f`/`g` and the same input list.
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_union_mapUnion' {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {f g : β → Set α} {xs : List β} :
  List.mapUnion f xs ∪ List.mapUnion g xs = List.mapUnion (λ x => f x ∪ g x) xs

items.name: List.mapUnion_comm
items.statement:
public theorem mapUnion_comm {α β} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {f : β → Set α} {xs ys : List β} :
  (xs ++ ys).mapUnion f = (ys ++ xs).mapUnion f

items.name: List.map_eqv_implies_mapUnion_eq
items.statement:
public theorem map_eqv_implies_mapUnion_eq {α β γ} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {f : β → Set α} {g : γ → Set α} {xs : List β} {ys : List γ} :
  xs.map f ≡ ys.map g → xs.mapUnion f = ys.mapUnion g

items.name: Option.mapD
items.statement: public def mapD {α β} (f : α → β) (default : β) : Option α → β

items.name: Option.mapD_some
items.statement:
public theorem mapD_some {α β} (f : α → β) (default : β) (a : α) :
  (Option.some a).mapD f default = f a

items.name: Option.mapD_none
items.statement:
public theorem mapD_none {α β} (f : α → β) (default : β) :
  Option.none.mapD f default = default

modules.title: Paths along a relation
modules.doc:
Facts about `Relation.TransGen`, and about walks: paths that record the vertex
each of their edges leaves from.

They live in `Cedar.Relation` rather than `Relation`, like the Mathlib copies in
`Cedar.List`, so that a file can import both Cedar and Mathlib.

items.name: Cedar.Relation.transGen_head
items.doc: A path starts with an edge.
items.statement:
public theorem transGen_head {α} {r : α → α → Prop} {a b : α}
  (h : Relation.TransGen r a b) : ∃ c, r a c

items.name: Cedar.Relation.transGen_tail
items.doc: A path ends with an edge.
items.statement:
public theorem transGen_tail {α} {r : α → α → Prop} {a b : α}
  (h : Relation.TransGen r a b) : ∃ c, r c b

items.name: Cedar.Relation.transGen_mono
items.doc: A path stays a path along a larger relation.
items.statement:
public theorem transGen_mono {α} {r s : α → α → Prop} (hrs : ∀ a b, r a b → s a b)
  {a b : α} (h : Relation.TransGen r a b) : Relation.TransGen s a b

items.name: Cedar.Relation.Walk
items.doc: A path along `edge` from `x` to `y` whose edges leave from `srcs`, in order.
items.statement:
public inductive Walk {α} (edge : α → α → Prop) : α → α → List α → Prop
  | single {x y} : edge x y → Walk edge x y [x]
  | cons {x z y srcs} : edge x z → Walk edge z y srcs → Walk edge x y (x :: srcs)

items.name: Cedar.Relation.Walk.append
items.doc: Walks compose.
items.statement:
public theorem Walk.append {α} {edge : α → α → Prop} {x y z : α} {s₁ s₂ : List α}
  (h₁ : Walk edge x y s₁) (h₂ : Walk edge y z s₂) : Walk edge x z (s₁ ++ s₂)

items.name: Cedar.Relation.Walk.of_transGen
items.doc: Every path is a walk.
items.statement:
public theorem Walk.of_transGen {α} {edge : α → α → Prop} {x y : α}
  (h : Relation.TransGen edge x y) : ∃ srcs, Walk edge x y srcs

items.name: Cedar.Relation.Walk.source_edge
items.doc: Every vertex a walk leaves from has an edge.
items.statement:
public theorem Walk.source_edge {α} {edge : α → α → Prop} {x y : α} {srcs : List α}
  (h : Walk edge x y srcs) : ∀ v ∈ srcs, ∃ w, edge v w

items.name: Cedar.Relation.Walk.suffix
items.doc: A walk through `v` continues from `v` along a suffix of its sources.

items.name: Cedar.Relation.Walk.nodup
items.doc: Every walk can be shortened to one that leaves from each vertex at most once.

modules.title: Set properties
modules.doc:
This file proves useful properties of canonical list-based sets defined in
`Cedar.Data.Set`.

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.WellFormed
items.statement: public def WellFormed {α} [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (s : Set α)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.if_wellformed_then_exists_make
items.statement:
public theorem if_wellformed_then_exists_make [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (s : Set α) :
  WellFormed s → ∃ list, s = Set.make list

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.wf_iff_sorted
items.statement:
public theorem wf_iff_sorted {α} [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α]  (s : Set α) :
  s.WellFormed ↔ s.elts.Sorted

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mapOrErr_eq_match
items.doc: Equation lemma for `Set.mapOrErr`, for clients that cannot unfold it.
items.statement:
public theorem mapOrErr_eq_match {α β ε} [DecidableEq β] [LT β] [DecidableRel (α := β) (· < ·)] (f : α → Except ε β) (s : Set α) (err : ε) :
  s.mapOrErr f err = match s.elts.mapM f with | .ok elts => .ok (make elts) | .error _ => .error err

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.contains_prop_bool_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem contains_prop_bool_equiv [DecidableEq α] {v : α} {s : Set α} :
  s.contains v = true ↔ v ∈ s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.not_contains_prop_bool_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem not_contains_prop_bool_equiv [DecidableEq α] {v : α} {s : Set α} :
  s.contains v = false ↔ v ∉ s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_elts_iff_mem_set
items.statement:
public theorem mem_elts_iff_mem_set {α : Type u} (v : α) (s : Set α) :
  v ∈ s.elts ↔ v ∈ s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_set_iff_mem_mk
items.statement:
public theorem mem_set_iff_mem_mk {α : Type u} (v : α) (xs : List α) :
  v ∈ xs ↔ v ∈ mk xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_mk_hd
items.statement:
public theorem mem_mk_hd {α : Type u} (hd : α) (tl : List α) :
  hd ∈ Set.mk (hd :: tl)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_mk_tl
items.statement:
public theorem mem_mk_tl {α : Type u} (a : α) (hd : α) (tl : List α) :
  a ∈ Set.mk tl → a ∈ Set.mk (hd :: tl)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_cons
items.statement:
public theorem mem_cons {a : α} {hd : α} {tl : List α} :
  a ∈ Set.mk (hd :: tl) ↔ a = hd ∨ a ∈ tl

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_set_implies_elts_non_empty
items.statement:
public theorem mem_set_implies_elts_non_empty {α : Type u} (v : α) (s : Set α) :
  v ∈ s → ¬(s.elts = [])

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.empty_eq_mk_nil
items.statement:
public theorem empty_eq_mk_nil {α} :
  (Set.empty : Set α) = Set.mk []

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.elts_empty
items.statement:
public theorem elts_empty {α} :
  (Set.empty : Set α).elts = []

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.not_mem_empty
items.doc: Like `List.not_mem_nil`, lifted to Sets
items.statement:
public theorem not_mem_empty {α : Type u} (v : α) :
  ¬ v ∈ Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.empty_wf
items.statement:
public theorem empty_wf {α : Type u} [LT α] [DecidableLT α] :
  Set.WellFormed (Set.empty : Set α)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map_empty
items.statement:
public theorem map_empty [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) :
  Set.empty.map f = Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.all_empty
items.statement:
public theorem all_empty (f : α → Bool) :
  Set.empty.all f = true

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.any_empty
items.statement:
public theorem any_empty (f : α → Bool) :
  Set.empty.any f = false

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.isEmpty_empty
items.statement:
public theorem isEmpty_empty [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] :
  (Set.empty : Set α).isEmpty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.isEmpty_iff_eq_empty
items.statement:
public theorem isEmpty_iff_eq_empty [DecidableEq α] {s : Set α} :
  s.isEmpty ↔ s = Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.isEmpty_make
items.statement:
public theorem isEmpty_make [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {xs : List α} :
  (Set.make xs).isEmpty ↔ xs = []

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.isEmpty_make_eq_false
items.statement:
public theorem isEmpty_make_eq_false [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (xs : List α) :
  (Set.make xs).isEmpty = false ↔ xs ≠ []

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.non_empty_iff_exists
items.statement:
public theorem non_empty_iff_exists [DecidableEq α] (s : Set α) :
  (¬ s.isEmpty) ↔ ∃ a, a ∈ s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.empty_iff_not_exists
items.doc: Corollary of `non_empty_iff_exists`
items.statement:
public theorem empty_iff_not_exists [DecidableEq α] (s : Set α) :
  s.isEmpty ↔ ¬ ∃ a, a ∈ s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.singleton_wf
items.statement:
public theorem singleton_wf [DecidableEq α] [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (a : α) :
  WellFormed (Set.singleton a)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_singleton
items.statement:
public theorem mem_singleton [DecidableEq α] (a b : α) :
  a ∈ Set.singleton b ↔ a = b

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_singleton_self
items.statement:
public theorem mem_singleton_self [DecidableEq α] (a : α) :
  a ∈ Set.singleton a

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_wf
items.statement:
public theorem make_wf [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (xs : List α) :
  WellFormed (Set.make xs)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_elts
items.statement:
public theorem make_elts [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {s : Set α} :
  WellFormed s → Set.make s.elts = s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_sorted
items.statement:
public theorem make_sorted {α} [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {xs : List α} :
  xs.Sorted → Set.make xs = Set.mk xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_make
items.statement:
public theorem mem_make [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (x : α) (xs : List α) :
  x ∈ Set.make xs ↔ x ∈ xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_mk_eqv
items.statement:
public theorem make_mk_eqv [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {xs ys : List α} :
  Set.make xs = Set.mk ys → xs ≡ ys

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_make_eqv
items.statement:
public theorem make_make_eqv [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {xs ys : List α} :
  Set.make xs = Set.make ys ↔ xs ≡ ys

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.elts_make_eqv
items.statement:
public theorem elts_make_eqv [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {xs : List α} :
  Set.elts (Set.make xs) ≡ xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_nil
items.statement:
public theorem make_nil [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] :
  Set.make [] (α := α) = Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_eq_empty
items.statement:
public theorem make_eq_empty [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {xs : List α} :
  Set.make xs = Set.empty ↔ xs = []

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_singleton_nonempty
items.statement:
public theorem make_singleton_nonempty [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] (a : α) :
  Set.make [a] ≠ Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.eq_means_eqv
Cedar.Data.Set.any_make
items.statement:
public theorem any_make [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (f : α → Bool) (xs : List α) :
  (Set.make xs).any f = xs.any f

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_elts_make
items.statement:
public theorem make_elts_make [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (xs : List α) :
  Set.make (Set.elts (Set.make xs)) = Set.make xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.elts_make_implies_equiv
items.statement:
public theorem elts_make_implies_equiv [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {xs ys : List α} :
  Set.elts (Set.make xs) = ys → ys ≡ xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_cons
items.doc:
Note that the converse of this is not true:
counterexample `xs = [1]`, `ys = []`, `a = 1`.
items.statement:
public theorem make_cons [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {xs ys : List α} {a : α} :
  make xs = make ys → make (a :: xs) = make (a :: ys)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.inter_def
items.statement:
public theorem inter_def {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∩ s₂ = s₁.intersect s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_inter_iff
items.statement:
public theorem mem_inter_iff {α} [DecidableEq α] {x : α} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  x ∈ s₁ ∩ s₂ ↔ x ∈ s₁ ∧ x ∈ s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.inter_wf
Cedar.Data.Set.inter_empty_left
items.statement:
public theorem inter_empty_left {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] (s : Set α) :
 Set.empty ∩ s = Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.inter_empty_right
items.statement:
public theorem inter_empty_right {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] (s : Set α) :
 s ∩ Set.empty = Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.inter_self
items.statement:
public theorem inter_self {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] (s : Set α) :
 s ∩ s = s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.intersects_def
items.statement:
public theorem intersects_def {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
 s₁.intersects s₂ = ¬ (s₁ ∩ s₂).isEmpty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.intersects_iff_exists
items.statement:
public theorem intersects_iff_exists {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
 s₁.intersects s₂ ↔ ∃ a, a ∈ s₁ ∧ a ∈ s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_wf
items.statement:
public theorem union_wf [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  s₁.WellFormed → s₂.WellFormed → WellFormed (s₁ ∪ s₂)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.make_cons_eq_singleton_union
items.statement:
public theorem make_cons_eq_singleton_union [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (a : α) (xs : List α) :
  Set.make (a :: xs) = Set.singleton a ∪ Set.make xs

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.append_eq_union
items.doc: The `++` notation on sets  is definitionally `∪`.
items.statement:
public theorem append_eq_union [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :
  s₁ ++ s₂ = s₁ ∪ s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_union
items.statement:
public theorem mem_union [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (s₁ s₂ : Set α) (a : α) :
  a ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂ ↔ (a ∈ s₁ ∨ a ∈ s₂)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.prop_union_iff_prop_and
items.statement:
public theorem prop_union_iff_prop_and [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (p : α → Prop) (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :
  ((∀ a ∈ s₁, p a) ∧ (∀ a ∈ s₂, p a)) ↔ ∀ a ∈ (s₁ ∪ s₂), p a

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_comm
items.doc: Union is commutative even if its operands are not well-formed.
items.statement:
public theorem union_comm [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :
  s₁ ∪ s₂ = s₂ ∪ s₁

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_assoc
items.doc: Union is associative even if its operands are not well-formed.
items.statement:
public theorem union_assoc [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (s₁ s₂ s₃ : Set α) :
  (s₁ ∪ s₂) ∪ s₃ = s₁ ∪ (s₂ ∪ s₃)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_empty_right
items.doc: Union with the empty set does not require well-formedness.
items.statement:
public theorem union_empty_right [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {s : Set α} :
  s ∪ Set.empty = s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_empty_left
items.doc: Union with the empty set does not require well-formedness.
items.statement:
public theorem union_empty_left [LT α] [DecidableLT α] {s : Set α} :
  Set.empty ∪ s = s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_idempotent
items.doc: Union with itself does not require well-formedness.
items.statement:
public theorem union_idempotent [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] {s : Set α} :
  s ∪ s = s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.elts_subset_then_subset
items.statement:
public theorem elts_subset_then_subset [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] {xs ys : List α} :
  xs ⊆ ys → Set.make xs ⊆ Set.make ys

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.subset_def
items.doc: Like `List.subset_def`, but lifted to Sets
items.statement:
public theorem subset_def [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ⊆ s₂ ↔ ∀ a, a ∈ s₁ → a ∈ s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.subset_empty
items.statement:
public theorem subset_empty [DecidableEq α] {s : Set α} :
  Set.empty ⊆ s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.superset_empty_subset_empty
items.statement:
public theorem superset_empty_subset_empty [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₂.isEmpty → s₁.isEmpty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.subset_iff_subset_elts
items.statement:
public theorem subset_iff_subset_elts [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ⊆ s₂ ↔ s₁.elts ⊆ s₂.elts

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.subset_iff_eq
Cedar.Data.Set.subset_trans
items.statement:
public theorem subset_trans [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ s₃ : Set α} :
  s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₂ ⊆ s₃ → s₁ ⊆ s₃

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.subset_refl
items.statement:
public theorem subset_refl [DecidableEq α] {s : Set α} :
  s ⊆ s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_subset_mem
items.statement:
public theorem mem_subset_mem [DecidableEq α] {a : α} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  a ∈ s₁ → s₁ ⊆ s₂ → a ∈ s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.subset_union
items.statement:
public theorem subset_union [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :
  s₁ ⊆ s₁ ∪ s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_subset
items.statement:
public theorem union_subset [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ s₃ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∪ s₂ ⊆ s₃ ↔ s₁ ⊆ s₃ ∧ s₂ ⊆ s₃

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.union_subset_eq
items.statement:
public theorem union_subset_eq [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] {s₁ s₂ : Set α} :
  s₁.WellFormed → s₂.WellFormed → s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₁ ∪ s₂ = s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.wellFormed_correct
items.statement:
public theorem wellFormed_correct {α} [LT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableLT α] {s : Set α} :
  s.wellFormed = true ↔ s.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map_wf
items.statement:
public theorem map_wf [LT β] [DecidableLT β] [StrictLT β] (f : α → β) (s : Set α) :
  (s.map f).WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map_id
items.statement:
public theorem map_id [LT α] [DecidableLT α] (s : Set α) :
  s.WellFormed → s.map id = s

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_map
items.doc: Analogue of `List.mem_map` but for sets
items.statement:
public theorem mem_map [LT β] [DecidableLT β] [StrictLT β] {b : β} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} :
  b ∈ s.map f ↔ ∃ a ∈ s, f a = b

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map_congr
items.doc: Analogue of `List.map_congr`, but for sets
items.statement:
public theorem map_congr [LT β] [DecidableLT β] {f g : α → β} {s : Set α} :
  (∀ a ∈ s, f a = g a) → s.map f = s.map g

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.isEmpty_map
items.statement:
public theorem isEmpty_map [DecidableEq α] [LT β] [DecidableLT β] [DecidableEq β] {f : α → β} {s : Set α} :
  (s.map f).isEmpty = s.isEmpty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map_make
items.statement:
public theorem map_make [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [LT β] [DecidableLT β] [StrictLT β] {f : α → β} {xs : List α} :
  (Set.make xs).map f = Set.make (xs.map f)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map_def
items.statement:
public theorem map_def [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (s : Set α) :
  s.map f = Set.make (s.elts.map f)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map_union
items.doc: `Set.map` distributes over `∪`.
items.statement:
public theorem map_union [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [LT β] [DecidableLT β] [StrictLT β]
  (f : α → β) (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :
  (s₁ ∪ s₂).map f = s₁.map f ∪ s₂.map f

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.filter_wf
Cedar.Data.Set.mem_filter
items.statement:
public theorem mem_filter [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] (p : α → Bool) (s : Set α) (e : α):
  e ∈ s.filter p ↔ (e ∈ s ∧ p e)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.difference_wf
Cedar.Data.Set.mem_difference
items.statement:
public theorem mem_difference [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] (s₁ s₂ : Set α) (e : α):
  e ∈ s₁.difference s₂ ↔ (e ∈ s₁ ∧ e ∉ s₂)

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.difference_subset
items.statement:
public theorem difference_subset [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [StrictLT α] [DecidableEq α] (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :
  (s₁.difference s₂) ⊆ s₁

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.all_eq_true
items.doc: Like `List.all_eq_true`, but for `Set.all`
items.statement:
public theorem all_eq_true {f : α → Bool} {s : Set α} :
  s.all f = true ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, f x = true

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.all_eq_false
items.doc: Like `List.all_eq_false`, but for `Set.all`
items.statement:
public theorem all_eq_false {f : α → Bool} {s : Set α} :
  s.all f = false ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ¬ f x = true

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.any_eq_true
items.doc: Like `List.any_eq_true`, but for `Set.any`
items.statement:
public theorem any_eq_true {f : α → Bool} {s : Set α} :
  s.any f = true ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, f x = true

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.any_eq_false
items.doc: Like `List.any_eq_false`, but for `Set.any`
items.statement:
public theorem any_eq_false {f : α → Bool} {s : Set α} :
  s.any f = false ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ¬ f x = true

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.map₁_eq_map
items.statement:
public theorem map₁_eq_map [LT α] [DecidableLT α] [LT β] [DecidableLT β] (f : α → β) (s : Set α) :
  (s.map₁ λ ⟨elt, _⟩ => f elt) = s.map f

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.all₁_eq_all
items.statement:
public theorem all₁_eq_all {s : Set α} {f : α → Bool} :
  (s.all₁ λ ⟨elt, _⟩ => f elt) = s.all f

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.any₁_eq_any
items.statement:
public theorem any₁_eq_any {s : Set α} {f : α → Bool} :
  (s.any₁ λ ⟨elt, _⟩ => f elt) = s.any f

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.mem_product
items.doc: An element is in `s₁.product s₂` iff its components are in `s₁` and `s₂`.
items.statement:
public theorem mem_product {α β} {a : α} {b : β} {s₁ : Set α} {s₂ : Set β} :
  (a, b) ∈ s₁.product s₂ ↔ a ∈ s₁ ∧ b ∈ s₂

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.product_empty
items.statement:
public theorem product_empty {α β} (s : Set α) :
  s.product (Set.empty : Set β) = Set.empty

items.name: Cedar.Data.Set.empty_product
items.statement:
public theorem empty_product {α β} (s : Set β) :
  (Set.empty : Set α).product s = Set.empty

modules.doc:
==============================================================================================
# Digit strings (`Digit⁺`) and their correspondence with `toNat?'`

`IsDigits` is the grammar-level notion of a non-empty run of digit characters — the
`Digit⁺` production common to numeric grammars. These lemmas connect it to the stdlib
natural-number parser `toNat?'`: a digit string is exactly one `toNat?'` accepts (modulo the
`'_'` separator, which `toNat?'` rejects and `Char.isDigit` never admits). The `IsDigits.*`
projections at the end give dot-notation for the facts parser proofs consume.
==============================================================================================

items.name: String.IsDigits
items.doc: `Digit⁺`: a non-empty string all of whose characters are decimal digits.
items.statement: public def IsDigits (s : String) : Prop

items.name: String.IsFixedDigits
items.doc:
`Digit{n}`: a run of exactly `n` decimal digits. The fixed-width refinement of `IsDigits`,
used wherever a grammar pins a field's width (the datetime grammar's `YYYY`, `MM`, `SSS`, …).
items.statement: public def IsFixedDigits (n : Nat) (s : String) : Prop

items.name: String.IsAtMostNDigits
items.doc:
`Digit{1,n}`: between one and `n` decimal digits. `IsDigits` supplies the lower bound and the
length constraint the upper (the decimal grammar's `Fraction ::= Digit{1,4}`).
items.statement: public def IsAtMostNDigits (n : Nat) (s : String) : Prop

items.name: String.IsWfSign
items.doc:
`['-']`: an optional leading minus sign, either present or absent. Shared by the numeric
grammars that admit a signed literal (decimal's `Sign`, duration's leading `'-'`).
items.statement: public def IsWfSign (s : String) : Prop

items.name: String.natOf
items.doc:
Natural-number value of a captured decimal digit string, defaulting to `0` when parsing fails.
On a field satisfying `IsDigits`, the default is never taken.
items.statement: public def natOf (s : String) : Nat

items.name: String.lenOf
items.doc: Length of a captured string as an integer, for use in grammar value formulas.
items.statement: public def lenOf (s : String) : Int

items.name: String.signOf
items.doc: Sign denoted by a captured optional-minus field.
items.statement: public def signOf (s : String) : Int

items.name: String.no_underscore_of_isDigits
items.doc:
A digit string contains no `'_'`, so `toInt?'`/`toNat?'` (which reject `'_'`) do not
short-circuit on it.
items.statement: theorem no_underscore_of_isDigits {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) : s.contains '_' = false

items.name: String.isNat_of_isDigits
items.doc: A digit string is a well-formed natural-number literal (`String.isNat`).
items.statement: theorem isNat_of_isDigits {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) : s.isNat = true

items.name: String.isDigits_of_isNat
items.doc: Conversely, a natural-number literal with no `'_'` is a digit string.
items.statement:
theorem isDigits_of_isNat {s : String} (hisnat : s.isNat = true)
    (hnc : s.contains '_' = false) : IsDigits s

items.name: String.toNat?'_isSome_of_isDigits
items.doc: Forward bridge: a `Digit⁺` string parses as a natural number.
items.statement:
theorem toNat?'_isSome_of_isDigits {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) :
    (toNat?' s).isSome = true

items.name: String.isDigits_of_toNat?'_isSome
items.doc: Backward bridge: anything `toNat?'` accepts is a `Digit⁺` string.
items.statement:
theorem isDigits_of_toNat?'_isSome {s : String} (h : (toNat?' s).isSome = true) :
    IsDigits s

items.name: String.toNat?'_toString
items.doc:
Rendering a natural number and parsing it with Cedar's underscore-rejecting parser
recovers the original number.
items.statement: public theorem toNat?'_toString (n : Nat) : toNat?' (toString n) = some n

items.name: String.toNat?'_repr
items.doc: `Nat.repr` is accepted by Cedar's natural-number parser.
items.statement: public theorem toNat?'_repr (n : Nat) : toNat?' (Nat.repr n) = some n

items.name: String.isDigits_toString
items.doc: The canonical decimal rendering of a natural number is a nonempty digit string.
items.statement: public theorem isDigits_toString (n : Nat) : IsDigits (toString n)

items.name: String.isDigits_repr
items.doc: `Nat.repr` is a nonempty digit string.
items.statement: public theorem isDigits_repr (n : Nat) : IsDigits (Nat.repr n)

items.name: String.IsDigits.ne_empty
items.doc: A digit string is nonempty.
items.statement: theorem IsDigits.ne_empty {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) : s ≠ ""

items.name: String.IsDigits.toNat?'_isSome
items.doc:
A digit string is accepted by `toNat?'` (dot-notation alias of `toNat?'_isSome_of_isDigits`,
used to recover the numeric value).
items.statement: theorem IsDigits.toNat?'_isSome {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) : (toNat?' s).isSome = true

items.name: String.IsDigits.all_isDigit
items.doc: Every character of a digit string is a digit (the second component of `IsDigits`).
items.statement:
theorem IsDigits.all_isDigit {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) :
    ∀ c ∈ s.toList, c.isDigit = true

items.name: String.toNat?'_isSome_length_pos
items.doc: If `toNat?'` succeeds then the string is non-empty.
items.statement: theorem toNat?'_isSome_length_pos (s : String) (h : (toNat?' s).isSome) : s.length > 0

items.name: List.splitOnPPrepend_no_sep
items.doc:
If no element of `l` satisfies `P`, then `splitOnPPrepend P l acc` returns
the single segment `[acc.reverse ++ l]` (the accumulator is prepended in reverse).
items.statement:
theorem splitOnPPrepend_no_sep (P : α → Bool) (l acc : List α)
    (h : ∀ x ∈ l, P x = false) :
    List.splitOnPPrepend P l acc = [(acc.reverse ++ l)]

items.name: List.splitOnPPrepend_one_sep
items.doc:
If `as ++ [sep] ++ bs` has exactly one element satisfying `P` (namely `sep`),
then `splitOnPPrepend P (as ++ sep :: bs) acc` returns `[acc.reverse ++ as, bs]`.
items.statement:
theorem splitOnPPrepend_one_sep (P : α → Bool) (as bs acc : List α) (sep : α)
    (hsep : P sep = true) (has : ∀ x ∈ as, P x = false) (hbs : ∀ x ∈ bs, P x = false) :
    List.splitOnPPrepend P (as ++ sep :: bs) acc = (acc.reverse ++ as) :: [bs]

items.name: String.splitToList_eq
items.doc: Splitting `s₁ ++ sep ++ s₂` on `sep` yields `[s₁, s₂]` when neither part contains `sep`.
items.statement:
theorem splitToList_eq (s₁ s₂ : String) (p : Char → Bool) (sep : Char)
    (hsep : p sep = true) (h₁ : ∀ c ∈ s₁.toList, p c = false)
    (h₂ : ∀ c ∈ s₂.toList, p c = false) :
    (s₁ ++ String.singleton sep ++ s₂).splitToList p = [s₁, s₂]

items.name: String.join_splitToList
items.doc:
Converse of `splitToList_eq`: if splitting `s` on `'.'` yields exactly two parts, then `s` is
their concatenation with the separator between them. Rejoining the split is the inverse of
splitting, so this recovers the rendering from the parser's view of a string.

items.name: List.splitOnPPrepend_two_sep
items.doc:
If `as ++ [sep] ++ bs ++ [sep] ++ cs` has exactly two elements satisfying `P` (namely the two
`sep`s), then `splitOnPPrepend P (as ++ sep :: bs ++ sep :: cs) acc` returns the three
segments `[acc.reverse ++ as, bs, cs]`.
items.statement:
theorem splitOnPPrepend_two_sep (P : α → Bool) (as bs cs acc : List α) (sep : α)
    (hsep : P sep = true) (has : ∀ x ∈ as, P x = false) (hbs : ∀ x ∈ bs, P x = false)
    (hcs : ∀ x ∈ cs, P x = false) :
    List.splitOnPPrepend P (as ++ sep :: (bs ++ sep :: cs)) acc = (acc.reverse ++ as) :: bs :: [cs]

items.name: String.splitToList_eq3
items.doc:
Splitting `s₁ ++ sep ++ s₂ ++ sep ++ s₃` on `sep` yields `[s₁, s₂, s₃]` when no part
contains `sep`.
items.statement:
theorem splitToList_eq3 (s₁ s₂ s₃ : String) (p : Char → Bool) (sep : Char)
    (hsep : p sep = true) (h₁ : ∀ c ∈ s₁.toList, p c = false)
    (h₂ : ∀ c ∈ s₂.toList, p c = false) (h₃ : ∀ c ∈ s₃.toList, p c = false) :
    (s₁ ++ String.singleton sep ++ s₂ ++ String.singleton sep ++ s₃).splitToList p = [s₁, s₂, s₃]

items.name: String.splitToList_no_sep
items.doc: Splitting a string that contains no separator yields the whole string as a single segment.
items.statement:
theorem splitToList_no_sep (s : String) (p : Char → Bool)
    (h : ∀ c ∈ s.toList, p c = false) :
    s.splitToList p = [s]

items.name: String.repr_no_dot
items.doc: No character in `toString n` is `'.'` (digits never produce a dot).
items.statement:
theorem repr_no_dot (n : Nat) :
    ∀ c ∈ (toString n).toList, (fun x : Char => decide (x = '.')) c = false

items.name: String.zeros_repr_no_dot
items.doc: No character in a zero-padded `toString n` string is `'.'`.
items.statement:
theorem zeros_repr_no_dot (zeros : String) (n : Nat)
    (hz : ∀ c ∈ zeros.toList, c = '0') :
    ∀ c ∈ (zeros ++ toString n).toList, (fun x : Char => decide (x = '.')) c = false

items.name: String.foldl_no_underscore_eq
items.doc:
When no character in `l` is `'_'`, the underscore-skipping foldl reduces to the plain
digit-accumulating foldl.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_no_underscore_eq (l : List Char) (acc : Nat)
    (hno : ∀ c ∈ l, c ≠ '_') :
    List.foldl (fun n c => if c = '_' then n else n * 10 + (c.toNat - 48)) acc l =
    List.foldl (fun n c => n * 10 + (c.toNat - 48)) acc l

items.name: String.foldl_eq_ofDigitChars
items.doc: The plain digit-accumulating foldl is equivalent to `Nat.ofDigitChars 10 l acc`.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_eq_ofDigitChars (l : List Char) (acc : Nat) :
    List.foldl (fun n c => n * 10 + (c.toNat - 48)) acc l =
    Nat.ofDigitChars 10 l acc

items.name: String.toDigits_foldl_roundtrip
items.doc: Folding the underscore-skipping digit accumulator over `Nat.toDigits 10 n` recovers `n`.
items.statement:
theorem toDigits_foldl_roundtrip (n : Nat) :
    List.foldl (fun acc c => if c = '_' then acc else acc * 10 + (c.toNat - 48)) 0
      (Nat.toDigits 10 n) = n

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.wf_iff_exists_value
items.doc: Well-formed datetime syntax is exactly syntax to which the grammar assigns some value.
items.statement:
public theorem wf_iff_exists_value {str : String} :
    IsWfDatetime str ↔ ∃ v, IsDatetimeValue str v

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_sound
items.doc:
Soundness of `Datetime.parse`: if parsing succeeds, the grammar assigns the input the returned
datetime's value.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_complete
items.doc:
Completeness of `Datetime.parse`: if the grammar assigns a string the value `d.val.toInt`,
then parsing accepts the string as `d`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_eq_none_iff
items.doc:
Because the grammar bounds years to four digits and zone offsets to `±23:59`, every
well-formed datetime value fits in `Int64`. Parsing therefore rejects exactly malformed
strings.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_eq_none_iff (str : String) :
    Datetime.parse str = none ↔ ¬ IsWfDatetime str

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_toString_roundtrip
items.doc:
`parse ∘ toString?` roundtrip: every successfully serialized datetime parses back to the
original value.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.toString?_injective
items.doc:
`toString?` is injective on the values it serializes: datetimes with the same (defined)
canonical string are equal. (Partial-serializer analogue of `Decimal`/`Duration`'s
`toString_injective`.)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq
items.doc:
Equal normal form iff equal parse — normalization decides datetime equality.

Datetime serialization is *partial* (`toString?`), so `normalize = (parse ·).bind toString?`
can collapse two distinct parseable-but-unserializable values to the shared `none`. The forward
direction therefore carries a serializability hypothesis on the parsed values; this is exactly
what a full *serialization-completeness* result (`parse s = some d → (toString? d).isSome`,
which needs the `Std.Time` civil-calendar round-trip) would discharge unconditionally, closing
the gap with `Decimal`/`Duration`'s total-`toString` versions. The backward direction is
unconditional.
items.statement:
public theorem normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq (s s' : String)
    (hs : ∀ d, Datetime.parse s = some d → (toString? d).isSome)
    (hs' : ∀ d, Datetime.parse s' = some d → (toString? d).isSome) :
    normalize s = normalize s' ↔ Datetime.parse s = Datetime.parse s'

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_eq_some_iff_isDatetimeValue
items.doc:
Exact parser characterization derived from soundness and completeness: parsing succeeds with
`d` precisely when the declarative grammar relation assigns the input the value
`d.val.toInt`.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_eq_some_iff_isDatetimeValue (str : String) (d : Datetime) :
    Datetime.parse str = some d ↔ IsDatetimeValue str d.val.toInt

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.bind_parse_toString?
items.doc: Total `Option` formulation of the partial serialization roundtrip.
items.statement:
public theorem bind_parse_toString? (d : Datetime) :
    (toString? d).bind Datetime.parse = (toString? d).map (fun _ => d)

modules.title: Datetime grammar: definitions
modules.doc:
This file gives a direct, parser-independent transcription of the datetime grammar, its component
value function, and the declarative relation connecting a string to its epoch-millisecond value.
Well-formedness takes the same shape as the decimal and duration grammars — the string is the
rendering of well-formed components — but the datetime grammar describes a date optionally
followed by a time, a fractional-seconds field, and a zone designator, so the components form a
nested record rather than a flat sequence of fields.
The `Digit⁺` predicate `IsDigits` and its fixed-width refinement `IsFixedDigits` (the grammar's
`Digit{n}`, used for every numeric field here) are shared with the decimal and duration grammars
and live in `Cedar.Thm.Data.String`, together with the shared `natOf` numeric reader.

items.note:
## Numeric constraints

The grammar's `Constraints` block bounds each numeric field. These are pure arithmetic predicates
over the field values; `daysInMonth` and `isLeapYear` transcribe the two auxiliary functions the
day constraint depends on.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.isLeapYear
items.doc: The grammar's `isLeapYear(y) = (4 | y) ∧ (¬(100 | y) ∨ (400 | y))`, as a decidable `Bool`.
items.statement: public def isLeapYear (y : Nat) : Bool

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.daysInMonth
items.doc:
The grammar's `daysInMonth(y, m)`: 30 for April/June/September/November, 28 or 29 for
February depending on the leap year, and 31 otherwise.
items.statement: public def daysInMonth (y m : Nat) : Nat

items.note:
## Components

Each nonterminal of the grammar becomes a record of its fixed-width digit fields. A `syntaxWf`
predicate pins the field widths (`Digit{n}`) and a `constraintsWf` predicate imposes the numeric
bounds from the grammar's `Constraints` block.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DateComponents
items.doc: The grammar's `Date ::= YYYY '-' MM '-' DD`.
items.statement:
public structure DateComponents where
  year : String
  month : String
  day : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DateComponents.syntaxWf
items.doc: `YYYY` is `Digit{4}`; `MM` and `DD` are `Digit{2}`.
items.statement: public def DateComponents.syntaxWf (d : DateComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DateComponents.constraintsWf
items.doc: The month/day bounds: `01 ≤ MM ≤ 12` and `01 ≤ DD ≤ daysInMonth(YYYY, MM)`.
items.statement: public def DateComponents.constraintsWf (d : DateComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DateComponents.asString
items.doc: Render a date as `YYYY '-' MM '-' DD`.
items.statement: public def DateComponents.asString (d : DateComponents) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimeComponents
items.doc: The grammar's `Time ::= hh ':' mm ':' ss`.
items.statement:
public structure TimeComponents where
  hours : String
  minutes : String
  seconds : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimeComponents.syntaxWf
items.doc: `hh`, `mm`, and `ss` are each `Digit{2}`.
items.statement: public def TimeComponents.syntaxWf (t : TimeComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimeComponents.constraintsWf
items.doc: The time bounds: `00 ≤ hh ≤ 23`, `00 ≤ mm ≤ 59`, `00 ≤ ss ≤ 59`.
items.statement: public def TimeComponents.constraintsWf (t : TimeComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimeComponents.asString
items.doc: Render a time as `hh ':' mm ':' ss`.
items.statement: public def TimeComponents.asString (t : TimeComponents) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.OffsetComponents
items.doc:
The grammar's `Offset ::= ('+' | '-') hh mm`. `negative` records the sign character;
`hours` and `mm` reuse the `hh`/`mm` nonterminals of `Time`.
items.statement:
public structure OffsetComponents where
  negative : Bool
  hours : String
  minutes : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.OffsetComponents.syntaxWf
items.doc: The offset's `hh` and `mm` are each `Digit{2}`, matching the `Time` nonterminals.
items.statement: public def OffsetComponents.syntaxWf (o : OffsetComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.OffsetComponents.constraintsWf
items.doc:
Because the offset reuses the `hh`/`mm` nonterminals, it inherits their bounds:
`00 ≤ hh ≤ 23` and `00 ≤ mm ≤ 59`.
items.statement: public def OffsetComponents.constraintsWf (o : OffsetComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.OffsetComponents.asString
items.doc: Render an offset as `('+' | '-') hh mm`.
items.statement: public def OffsetComponents.asString (o : OffsetComponents) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.Zone
items.doc:
The zone designator that terminates a datetime with a time: either the UTC marker `'Z'`
(`Date 'T' Time 'Z'` / `Date 'T' Time '.' SSS 'Z'`) or an explicit `Offset`.
items.statement:
public inductive Zone where
  | utc
  | offset (o : OffsetComponents)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.Zone.syntaxWf
items.doc: A UTC marker imposes nothing; an offset must have well-formed digit fields.
items.statement: public def Zone.syntaxWf : Zone → Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.Zone.constraintsWf
items.doc: A UTC marker imposes nothing; an offset must satisfy the `hh`/`mm` bounds.
items.statement: public def Zone.constraintsWf : Zone → Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.Zone.asString
items.doc: Render the zone: `'Z'` for UTC, otherwise the offset's `('+' | '-') hh mm`.
items.statement: public def Zone.asString : Zone → String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimePart
items.doc:
The time-bearing tail of a datetime: a `Time`, an optional fractional-seconds field `SSS`
(`'.' SSS`), and a `Zone`. Absent `SSS` (`none`) corresponds to the forms without a
`'.' SSS`; `some` corresponds to the `'.' SSS` forms.
items.statement:
public structure TimePart where
  time : TimeComponents
  millis : Option String
  zone : Zone

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.IsWfOptionalMillis
items.doc:
Lift `IsFixedDigits 3` (the grammar's `SSS ::= Digit{3}`) to the optional field:
an absent `SSS` is trivially valid.
items.statement: public def IsWfOptionalMillis : Option String → Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimePart.syntaxWf
items.doc: The time, the optional `SSS`, and the zone are each well-formed.
items.statement: public def TimePart.syntaxWf (tp : TimePart) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimePart.constraintsWf
items.doc:
The time and zone satisfy their numeric bounds. `SSS` is unconstrained (`000`–`999` are all
valid), so it contributes no numeric constraint.
items.statement: public def TimePart.constraintsWf (tp : TimePart) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimePart.asString
items.doc: Render the tail: `'T' Time ['.' SSS] Zone`, so `some sss` inserts `'.' sss`.
items.statement: public def TimePart.asString (tp : TimePart) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DatetimeComponents
items.doc:
A datetime is a `Date` optionally followed by a time-bearing tail. `none` is the date-only
form `Date`; `some tp` covers the four `Date 'T' Time …` forms, with the presence of `SSS`
and the choice of `Zone` selecting among them.
items.statement:
public structure DatetimeComponents where
  date : DateComponents
  time : Option TimePart

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DatetimeComponents.syntaxWf
items.doc: Every present component has well-formed digit fields.
items.statement: public def DatetimeComponents.syntaxWf (c : DatetimeComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DatetimeComponents.constraintsWf
items.doc: Every present component satisfies its numeric bounds.
items.statement: public def DatetimeComponents.constraintsWf (c : DatetimeComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DatetimeComponents.asString
items.doc:
Canonical string representation: the date, followed by the time-bearing tail when present.
Phrasing well-formedness existentially over `asString` (below) bakes the grammar's structure
in for free — the separators, the fixed field order, and the choice among the five top-level
forms all follow from the shape of the witnessing record.
items.statement: public def DatetimeComponents.asString (c : DatetimeComponents) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DatetimeProduction
items.doc:
The datetime grammar production witnessed by a syntactically and numerically valid component
record and its rendering.
items.statement: public def DatetimeProduction (str : String) (components : DatetimeComponents) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.IsWfDatetime
items.doc: A datetime string is well-formed exactly when it has a valid grammar production.
items.statement: public def IsWfDatetime (str : String) : Prop

items.note:
## Value relation

The component value functions below transcribe the grammar's date/time →
milliseconds-since-epoch formula. `IsDatetimeValue str v` then reuses the same witnesses as
`IsWfDatetime` and states that their denotation is `v`. No second string parser is part of the
trusted grammar specification.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.epochDays
items.doc:
Day count of a date since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01), via Howard Hinnant's `days_from_civil`
algorithm. This transcribes `Std.Time.PlainDate.toEpochDay` over raw `Nat` fields, independently
of the `Std.Time` date type.
items.statement: public def epochDays (year month day : Nat) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.OffsetComponents.seconds
items.doc:
The offset's signed second count: `± (hh × 3600 + mm × 60)`. Positive offsets (`+hhmm`) are
east of UTC, so the parser subtracts this to normalize to UTC.
items.statement: public def OffsetComponents.seconds (o : OffsetComponents) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.Zone.offsetSeconds
items.doc:
Signed UTC-normalization seconds contributed by a zone: `0` for the `'Z'` marker, and the
offset's second count otherwise.
items.statement: public def Zone.offsetSeconds : Zone → Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DateComponents.toMillis
items.doc: Milliseconds-since-epoch value of a well-formed date's midnight UTC.
items.statement: public def DateComponents.toMillis (d : DateComponents) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.TimePart.toMillis
items.doc:
Milliseconds-since-epoch value of a datetime's time-bearing tail relative to its date's
midnight: the wall-clock time in milliseconds, less the zone offset (converting to UTC),
plus the optional fractional-seconds field.
items.statement: public def TimePart.toMillis (tp : TimePart) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.DatetimeComponents.toMillis
items.doc:
Milliseconds-since-epoch value of a whole datetime: the date's midnight plus the time-bearing
tail's contribution (`0` for the date-only form).
items.statement: public def DatetimeComponents.toMillis (c : DatetimeComponents) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.IsDatetimeValue
items.doc:
`v` is the value of the datetime literal `str`: `str` is the rendering of syntactically and
numerically well-formed datetime components, and `v` is their epoch-millisecond denotation.

The existential supplies the grammar decomposition directly, so this relation does not
re-parse the string. It is total on well-formed syntax (`wf_iff_exists_value`) and
single-valued (`isDatetimeValue_unique`).
items.statement: public def IsDatetimeValue (str : String) (v : Int) : Prop

items.note:
## Canonical serialization

`Datetime` stores an arbitrary `Int64` millisecond value, while the concrete syntax restricts
years to `0000` through `9999`. Serialization is therefore partial. It always emits the most
explicit grammar form, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSS±HHMM`, using a zero offset when UTC is in range and
the smallest minute offset needed at either endpoint. All decimal fields are rendered here rather
than through `Std.Time`'s formatter.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.MILLIS_PER_DAY
items.doc: Milliseconds in one day.
items.statement: public def MILLIS_PER_DAY : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.MIN_UTC_MILLIS
items.doc: Smallest millisecond value whose UTC civil date has a four-digit nonnegative year.
items.statement: public def MIN_UTC_MILLIS : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.MAX_UTC_MILLIS
items.doc: Largest millisecond value whose UTC civil date has a four-digit nonnegative year.
items.statement: public def MAX_UTC_MILLIS : Int

items.statement: public def MAX_OFFSET_MILLIS : Int

items.statement: public def MIN_REPRESENTABLE_MILLIS : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.MAX_REPRESENTABLE_MILLIS
items.doc: Exact upper endpoint representable by the datetime grammar.
items.statement: public def MAX_REPRESENTABLE_MILLIS : Int
