items.note:
## Bridge to `Std.Time`: `Datetime.parse` ↔ the grammar value relation

The lemmas above (roundtrip + `Parsec` foundations) are the parser-independent half — they relate
`IsWfDatetime`, `IsDatetimeValue`, the proof-local structural decoder, and the primitive `Parsec`
combinators, all of which we control. The lemmas below are the missing half: they relate the
*actual* `Datetime.parse` (which delegates to `Std.Time.GenericFormat.parse`) to those definitions.
Each is a self-contained obligation about `Std.Time`'s behavior on the five fixed datetime formats;
discharging them requires symbolically evaluating `Std.Time`'s well-founded-recursion parsers — the
`Parsec` foundations above are the first rung of that ladder (see the note in the aggregator).

The decomposition mirrors the structure of `Datetime.parse`:
1. three Boolean guards (`dateContainsLeapSeconds`, `checkOffsetLen`, `tzOffsetMinsLt60`);
2. the five-way format alternation `DateOnly.parse <|> … <|> DateWithOffsetAndMillis.parse`;
3. the offset-range check `< MAX_OFFSET_SECONDS` and the final `datetime?` (i.e. `Int64.ofInt?`).

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.datetime?_some_toInt
items.doc:
If `datetime? v = some d` then `d.val.toInt = v` (the `Int64.ofInt?` roundtrip on the datetime
encoding). Mirror of `Cedar.Thm.Duration.duration?_some_toInt`.
items.statement:
theorem datetime?_some_toInt (v : Int) (d : Datetime) (h : datetime? v = some d) :
    d.val.toInt = v

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_some_decompose
items.doc:
**Structural decomposition of a successful parse.** Reading `Datetime.parse str = some d`
backwards through its `do`-block: the three Boolean guards must have passed, the `Std.Time`
format alternation must have produced some `zt`, its offset must have satisfied the
`< MAX_OFFSET_SECONDS` range check, and the final `datetime?` (`Int64.ofInt?`) of `zt`'s
epoch-millisecond value must have returned `d`. This is pure `Option`-monad reasoning about the
shape of `Datetime.parse` — no `Std.Time` internals — so it is fully proven, and it is what lets
`parse_sound` reduce to the genuine `Std.Time` obligations.
items.statement:
theorem parse_some_decompose {str : String} {d : Datetime} (h : Datetime.parse str = some d) :
    dateContainsLeapSeconds str = false ∧ checkOffsetLen str = true ∧
    tzOffsetMinsLt60 str = true ∧
    ∃ zt, (DateOnly.parse str <|> DateUTC.parse str <|> DateUTCWithMillis.parse str <|>
             DateWithOffset.parse str <|> DateWithOffsetAndMillis.parse str).toOption = some zt ∧
          zt.timezone.offset.second.val.natAbs < MAX_OFFSET_SECONDS ∧
          datetime? zt.toTimestamp.toMillisecondsSinceUnixEpoch.toInt = some d

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.exactlyChars_go_inv
items.doc:
**`exactlyChars.go` success-inversion.** If the digit-consuming loop succeeds from position `p`
(splitting the string as `pre ++ suf`) advancing to `p'` returning `result`, then `result` is
`acc` followed by an `out` segment of exactly `size - count` digit characters, `suf` begins with
`out`, and `p'` sits just past `out`. This is the converse of `exactlyChars_go_digits`.
items.statement:
theorem exactlyChars_go_inv {s : String} :
    ∀ (k size count : Nat) (acc pre suf : String) (p p' : s.Pos) (result : String),
      size - count = k →
      p.Splits pre suf →
      exactlyChars.go (satisfy Char.isDigit) size acc count ⟨s, p⟩
          = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ result →
      ∃ out rest : String,
        result = acc ++ out ∧
        suf = out ++ rest ∧
        out.length = size - count ∧
        (∀ c ∈ out.toList, c.isDigit = true) ∧
        p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.exactlyChars_inv_at
items.doc:
**`exactlyChars` success-inversion (position-general).** If `exactlyChars (satisfy isDigit) n`
succeeds at position `p` (splitting `s` as `pre ++ suf`) advancing to `p'` returning `out`, then
`out` is exactly `n` digit characters, `suf` begins with `out`, and `p'` splits `s` as
`pre ++ out | rest`. Converse of `exactlyChars_digits_at`.
items.statement:
theorem exactlyChars_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf out : String) (n : Nat)
    (hn : 0 < n) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : exactlyChars (satisfy Char.isDigit) n ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ out) :
    ∃ rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits n out ∧ suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseNum_inv_at
items.doc:
**`parseNum` success-inversion.** If `parseNum n` succeeds at `p` returning value `v`, then the
consumed segment is a fixed `n`-digit string `out` with `v = natOf out`.
items.statement:
theorem parseNum_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String) (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n)
    (v : Nat) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseNum n ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits n out ∧ v = natOf out ∧ suf = out ++ rest ∧
      p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.pstring_inv_at
items.doc:
**`pstring` success-inversion.** If `pstring sep` succeeds at `p` (splitting `s` as `pre ++ suf`)
advancing to `p'`, then `sep` is a prefix of `suf` (`suf = sep ++ rest`) and `p'` splits `s` as
`pre ++ sep | rest`.
items.statement:
theorem pstring_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf sep : String) (out : String)
    (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : pstring sep ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ out) :
    ∃ rest : String, out = sep ∧ suf = sep ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ sep) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseNatToBounded_two_inv_at
items.doc:
**`parseNatToBounded (parseFlexibleNum 2)` success-inversion.** Success at `p` forces a fixed
2-digit segment `out`, the bound `n ≤ natOf out ≤ m`, and the value `ofNat' (natOf out)`.
items.statement:
theorem parseNatToBounded_two_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    {n m : Nat} (v : Bounded.LE n m) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : (parseNatToBounded (parseFlexibleNum 2) : Parser (Bounded.LE n m)) ⟨s, p⟩
        = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits 2 out ∧ (n ≤ natOf out ∧ natOf out ≤ m) ∧
      v.val = natOf out ∧ suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_year_inv_at
items.doc: **`parseWith (.y .fourDigit)` success-inversion.**
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_year_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String) (config : FormatConfig)
    (v : Int) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.y .fourDigit) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits 4 out ∧ v = Int.ofNat (natOf out) ∧ suf = out ++ rest ∧
      p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_month_inv_at
items.doc:
Bridge: `parseWith config (.M (.inl {padding:=2}))` is `parseNatToBounded (parseFlexibleNum 2)`
at `Bounded.LE 1 12`. Month inversion.
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_month_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (v : Month.Ordinal) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.M (.inl {padding := 2})) ⟨s, p⟩
        = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits 2 out ∧ (1 ≤ natOf out ∧ natOf out ≤ 12) ∧
      (v.val = natOf out) ∧
      suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_day_inv_at
items.doc: Day inversion (`Bounded.LE 1 31`).
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_day_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (v : Day.Ordinal) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.d {padding := 2}) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits 2 out ∧ (1 ≤ natOf out ∧ natOf out ≤ 31) ∧
      (v.val = natOf out) ∧
      suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_hour_inv_at
items.doc: Hour inversion (`Bounded.LE 0 23`).
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_hour_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (v : Hour.Ordinal) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.H {padding := 2}) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits 2 out ∧ natOf out ≤ 23 ∧
      suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_minute_inv_at
items.doc: Minute inversion (`Bounded.LE 0 59`).
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_minute_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (v : Minute.Ordinal) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.m {padding := 2}) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits 2 out ∧ natOf out ≤ 59 ∧
      suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_second_inv_at
items.doc:
`.s` field inversion: a successful second-parse consumed exactly 2 digit chars with value ≤ 59.
Handles the `allowLeapSeconds = false` else-branch (parse to `Bounded.LE 0 59` then `expandTop`).
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_second_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (hcfg : config.allowLeapSeconds = false) (v : Second.Ordinal true)
    (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.s {padding := 2}) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsFixedDigits 2 out ∧ natOf out ≤ 59 ∧
      suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_fraction_inv_at
items.doc:
`.S (.truncated 3)` field inversion: a successful fraction-parse consumed exactly 3 digit
chars. Mirrors `parseWith_second_inv_at`; only the 3-digit segment + position matter.
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_fraction_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (v : Nanosecond.Ordinal) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.S (.truncated 3)) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String, IsFixedDigits 3 out ∧ suf = out ++ rest ∧ p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.pchar_success_inv_at
items.doc:
**`pchar` success-inversion.** A successful `pchar c` at `p` (splitting `s` as `pre ++ suf`)
forces the string unchanged, the consumed char `c` at the head of `suf`, and advances to a `p'`
splitting `s` as `pre ++ singleton c | rest`.
items.statement:
theorem pchar_success_inv_at {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (pre suf : String) (c : Char) (rem : ParseIt)
    (out : Char) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : pchar c ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem out) :
    ∃ (p' : s.Pos) (rest : String),
      rem = ⟨s, p'⟩ ∧ out = c ∧ suf = String.singleton c ++ rest ∧
      p'.Splits (pre ++ String.singleton c) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.sign_inv_at
items.doc:
**Sign-alternation success-inversion.** A successful `(pchar '+' *> pure 1) <|>
(pchar '-' *> pure (-1))` consumed exactly one sign character (`+`→`neg=false`, `-`→`neg=true`),
leaving the string unchanged and advancing past that character.
items.statement:
theorem sign_inv_at {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (pre suf : String) (rem : ParseIt) (a : Int)
    (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : ((pchar '+' *> pure 1) <|> (pchar '-' *> pure (-1)) : Parser Int) ⟨s, p⟩
        = ParseResult.success rem a) :
    ∃ (neg : Bool) (p1 : s.Pos) (rest : String),
      rem = ⟨s, p1⟩ ∧
      suf = String.singleton (if neg then '-' else '+') ++ rest ∧
      p1.Splits (pre ++ String.singleton (if neg then '-' else '+')) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWithDate_modifier_app
items.doc: `parseWithDate` on a `.modifier` reduces to running `parseWith` then inserting.
items.statement:
theorem parseWithDate_modifier_app (b : DateBuilder) (config : FormatConfig) (m : Modifier)
    (it : ParseIt) :
    parseWithDate b config (.modifier m) it
      = (match parseWith config m it with
         | .success rem a => ParseResult.success rem (b.insert m a)
         | .error pos msg => .error pos msg)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWithDate_string_app
items.doc: `parseWithDate` on a `.string` reduces to running `pstring` then keeping the builder.
items.statement:
theorem parseWithDate_string_app (b : DateBuilder) (config : FormatConfig) (sep : String)
    (it : ParseIt) :
    parseWithDate b config (.string sep) it
      = (match pstring sep it with
         | .success rem _ => ParseResult.success rem b
         | .error pos msg => .error pos msg)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.go_nil_inv
items.doc: `parser.go` at `[]` succeeding forces `build` to have succeeded with the same value/position.
items.statement:
theorem go_nil_inv {s : String} (config : FormatConfig) (b : DateBuilder) (p p' : s.Pos)
    (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hgo : parser.go config .any b [] ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ zt) :
    b.build .any = some zt ∧ p = p'

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.go_nil_preserves
items.statement:
theorem go_nil_preserves {s : String} (config : FormatConfig) (b : DateBuilder) (p : s.Pos)
    (rem : ParseIt) (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hgo : parser.go config .any b [] ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem zt) :
    rem.1 = s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.exactlyChars_go_preserves
items.doc: `exactlyChars.go` preserves the string component of the iterator.
items.statement:
theorem exactlyChars_go_preserves {s : String} :
    ∀ (size count : Nat) (acc : String) (p : s.Pos) (rem : ParseIt) (out : String),
      exactlyChars.go (satisfy Char.isDigit) size acc count ⟨s, p⟩
          = ParseResult.success rem out → rem.1 = s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseNum_preserves
items.doc:
`parseWith` (for the modifiers used by the datetime formats) preserves the string component.
Proven for the specific modifiers via their `exactlyChars`/`parseNum` cores. This is stated for
an arbitrary modifier by falling back to: if a `parseWith` succeeds we can always read off the
string, but here we only need the datetime ones. We give the generic `parseNum`-based fields.
items.statement:
theorem parseNum_preserves {s : String} (n : Nat) (p : s.Pos) (rem : ParseIt) (v : Nat)
    (hpar : parseNum n ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem v) : rem.1 = s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.satisfy_digit_preserves
items.doc: `satisfy Char.isDigit` preserves the string component on success.
items.statement:
theorem satisfy_digit_preserves {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (rem : ParseIt) (c : Char)
    (hpar : (satisfy Char.isDigit : Parser Char) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem c) :
    rem.1 = s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.optional_satisfy_digit_preserves
items.doc: `optional (satisfy Char.isDigit)` preserves the string component on success.
items.statement:
theorem optional_satisfy_digit_preserves {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (rem : ParseIt)
    (c : Option Char)
    (hpar : optional (satisfy Char.isDigit : Parser Char) ⟨s, p⟩ =
      ParseResult.success rem c) : rem.1 = s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseOneOrTwoNum_preserves
items.doc: `parseOneOrTwoNum` preserves the string component on success.
items.statement:
theorem parseOneOrTwoNum_preserves {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (rem : ParseIt) (v : Nat)
    (hpar : parseOneOrTwoNum ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem v) : rem.1 = s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.satisfy_digit_success_inv_at
items.doc: A successful digit `satisfy` consumes exactly the returned character.
items.statement:
theorem satisfy_digit_success_inv_at {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (rem : ParseIt) (out : Char) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : (satisfy Char.isDigit : Parser Char) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem out) :
    ∃ (p' : s.Pos) (rest : String),
      rem = ⟨s, p'⟩ ∧ out.isDigit = true ∧
      suf = String.singleton out ++ rest ∧
      p'.Splits (pre ++ String.singleton out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.satisfy_digit_error_pos_eq
items.doc: A failed digit `satisfy` reports the unchanged iterator.
items.statement:
theorem satisfy_digit_error_pos_eq {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (pos : ParseIt)
    (msg : Error)
    (hpar : (satisfy Char.isDigit : Parser Char) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.error pos msg) :
    pos = ⟨s, p⟩

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.optional_satisfy_digit_none_eq
items.doc: Returning `none` from the optional second digit leaves the iterator unchanged.
items.statement:
theorem optional_satisfy_digit_none_eq {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (rem : ParseIt)
    (hpar : optional (satisfy Char.isDigit : Parser Char) ⟨s, p⟩ =
      ParseResult.success rem none) :
    rem = ⟨s, p⟩

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.optional_satisfy_digit_some_inv_at
items.doc: Returning `some c` from the optional second digit consumes exactly that digit.
items.statement:
theorem optional_satisfy_digit_some_inv_at {s : String} (p : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (rem : ParseIt) (out : Char) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : optional (satisfy Char.isDigit : Parser Char) ⟨s, p⟩ =
      ParseResult.success rem (some out)) :
    ∃ (p' : s.Pos) (rest : String),
      rem = ⟨s, p'⟩ ∧ out.isDigit = true ∧
      suf = String.singleton out ++ rest ∧
      p'.Splits (pre ++ String.singleton out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseOneOrTwoNum_inv_at
items.doc: A successful `parseOneOrTwoNum` consumes one or two digits and returns their value.
items.statement:
theorem parseOneOrTwoNum_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (v : Nat) (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseOneOrTwoNum ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ out rest : String,
      IsAtMostNDigits 2 out ∧ v = natOf out ∧ suf = out ++ rest ∧
      p'.Splits (pre ++ out) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.no_beq_of_isDigits
items.statement:
theorem no_beq_of_isDigits {s : String} (hs : IsDigits s) (sep : Char)
    (hsep : sep.isDigit = false) :
    ∀ c ∈ s.toList, (c == sep) = false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.no_sign_of_isDigits
items.statement:
theorem no_sign_of_isDigits {s : String} (hs : IsDigits s) :
    ∀ c ∈ s.toList, (c == '+' || c == '-') = false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.three_fields_no_pred
items.statement:
theorem three_fields_no_pred (a b c : String) (sep : Char) (pred : Char → Bool)
    (ha : ∀ ch ∈ a.toList, pred ch = false)
    (hb : ∀ ch ∈ b.toList, pred ch = false)
    (hc : ∀ ch ∈ c.toList, pred ch = false)
    (hsep : pred sep = false) :
    ∀ ch ∈ (a ++ String.singleton sep ++ b ++ String.singleton sep ++ c).toList,
      pred ch = false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.append_sep_no_pred
items.statement:
theorem append_sep_no_pred (a b : String) (sep : Char) (pred : Char → Bool)
    (ha : ∀ ch ∈ a.toList, pred ch = false)
    (hb : ∀ ch ∈ b.toList, pred ch = false)
    (hsep : pred sep = false) :
    ∀ ch ∈ (a ++ String.singleton sep ++ b).toList, pred ch = false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.checkOffsetLen_offset_fields
items.doc: Cedar's offset-length guard strengthens the two raw one-or-two-digit fields to two digits.
items.statement:
theorem checkOffsetLen_offset_fields {date time hh mm : String} (neg : Bool)
    (hdateT : ∀ ch ∈ date.toList, (ch == 'T') = false)
    (htimeT : ∀ ch ∈ time.toList, (ch == 'T') = false)
    (htimeSign : ∀ ch ∈ time.toList, (ch == '+' || ch == '-') = false)
    (hhh : IsAtMostNDigits 2 hh) (hmm : IsAtMostNDigits 2 mm)
    (hcheck : checkOffsetLen
      (date ++ String.singleton 'T' ++ time ++
        String.singleton (if neg then '-' else '+') ++ hh ++ mm) = true) :
    IsFixedDigits 2 hh ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 mm

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parseWith_offset_inv_at
items.doc:
**`.x .hourMinute` (offset) field inversion.** A successful offset parse consumes a sign and
one-or-two-digit hour/minute fields within bounds. Cedar's `checkOffsetLen` guard later
strengthens both fields to exactly two digits.
items.statement:
theorem parseWith_offset_inv_at {s : String} (p p' : s.Pos) (pre suf : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (v : Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset)
    (hsplit : p.Splits pre suf)
    (hpar : parseWith config (.x .hourMinute) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v) :
    ∃ (neg : Bool) (hh mm rest : String),
      IsAtMostNDigits 2 hh ∧ IsAtMostNDigits 2 mm ∧
      natOf hh ≤ 23 ∧ natOf mm ≤ 59 ∧
      suf = String.singleton (if neg then '-' else '+') ++ (hh ++ (mm ++ rest)) ∧
      p'.Splits (pre ++ String.singleton (if neg then '-' else '+') ++ hh ++ mm) rest

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.pstring_preserves
items.doc: `pstring` preserves the string component.
items.statement:
theorem pstring_preserves {s : String} (sep : String) (p : s.Pos) (rem : ParseIt) (out : String)
    (hpar : pstring sep ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem out) : rem.1 = s

items.note:
### Packaged walk steps

Every `*_full_inv` / `*_go_preserves` walk repeats the same ~20-line block per format item:
`go_cons_app`, case the `parseWithDate`, thread string-preservation, expose the underlying
`parseWith`/`pstring`, and `injection` the positions. These two lemmas package one step each
(modifier / string separator), so a walk step becomes a single
`obtain ⟨p', v, hstep, hgo⟩ := go_step_modifier … hpres hgo`. The modifier version takes the
field's string-preservation fact as a hypothesis (each field has its own `*_preserves` lemma).

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.go_step_modifier
items.doc:
One `.modifier m` step of a `parser.go` walk: success through `.modifier m :: xs` yields a
same-string success of the underlying `parseWith m` and the continuation on the inserted
builder. `hpres` is the field's `parseWithDate`-level string-preservation fact — the level
every existing `*_preserves` lemma is stated at (`parseWithDate_dateFields_preserves`,
`parseWithDate_hour_preserves`, …).
items.statement:
theorem go_step_modifier {s : String} (config : FormatConfig) (aw : Awareness)
    (b : DateBuilder) (m : Modifier) (xs : FormatString) (p : s.Pos)
    (out : ParseIt) (zt : aw.type)
    (hpres : ∀ (rem : ParseIt) (b' : DateBuilder),
      parseWithDate b config (.modifier m) ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success rem b' → rem.1 = s)

    ∃ (p' : s.Pos) (v : TypeFormat m),
      parseWith config m ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p'⟩ v ∧
      parser.go config aw (b.insert m v) xs ⟨s, p'⟩ = ParseResult.success out zt

**DateOnly full parse inversion.** If the DateOnly format's `parser.go` succeeds from the empty
builder over the whole string `s`, ending at `endPos` with value `zt`, then `s` decomposes as the
rendering of a well-formed date, and `build` succeeds on the corresponding filled builder.
items.statement:
theorem dateOnly_full_inv {s : String} (config : FormatConfig) (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hgo : parser.go config .any {}
        [.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
         .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2})]
        ⟨s, s.startPos⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, s.endPos⟩ zt) :
    ∃ (year month day : String)
      (hm : 1 ≤ natOf month ∧ natOf month ≤ 12)
      (hd : 1 ≤ natOf day ∧ natOf day ≤ 31),
      IsFixedDigits 4 year ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 month ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 day ∧
      s = year ++ "-" ++ month ++ "-" ++ day ∧
      ({ ({} : DateBuilder) with
              y := some (Int.ofNat (natOf year)),
              M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf month) hm),
              d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf day) hd) }).build .any = some zt

    (hm : 1 ≤ mo ∧ mo ≤ 12) (hd : 1 ≤ dy ∧ dy ≤ 31)
    (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)

        y := some (Int.ofNat yr),
        M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' mo hm),
        d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' dy hd),
        H := H, m := m, s := sec, S := S, x := off }).build .any = some zt) :
    dy ≤ daysInMonth yr mo

items.doc:
**`build` inversion (date-only).** If the DateOnly builder (with `y`/`M`/`d` set from
nonnegative year/month/day fields) `build`s successfully, then the day satisfies the exact
grammar bound `day ≤ daysInMonth year month`. This is where `constraintsWf`'s day bound comes
from — the `year.Valid` guard inside `build`, bridged to `daysInMonth` via `days_eq_daysInMonth`
and `isLeap_ofNat`.
items.statement:
theorem build_dateOnly_inv {yr mo dy : Nat}
    (hm : 1 ≤ mo ∧ mo ≤ 12) (hd : 1 ≤ dy ∧ dy ≤ 31)
    (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hbuild : ({ ({} : DateBuilder) with
        y := some (Int.ofNat yr),
        M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' mo hm),
        d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' dy hd) }).build .any = some zt) :
    dy ≤ daysInMonth yr mo

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.datetimePrefix_inv
items.statement:
theorem datetimePrefix_inv {s : String} (config : FormatConfig)
    (hcfg : config.allowLeapSeconds = false) (tail : FormatString)
    (out : ParseIt) (zt : ZonedDateTime)
    (hgo : parser.go config .any {}
      ([.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
        .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2}), .string "T",
        .modifier (.H {padding := 2}), .string ":", .modifier (.m {padding := 2}),
        .string ":", .modifier (.s {padding := 2})] ++ tail)
      ⟨s, s.startPos⟩ = ParseResult.success out zt) :
    ∃ (year month day hh mm ss rest : String)
      (hm : 1 ≤ natOf month ∧ natOf month ≤ 12)
      (hd : 1 ≤ natOf day ∧ natOf day ≤ 31)
      (H : Hour.Ordinal) (m : Minute.Ordinal) (sec : Second.Ordinal true)
      (p : s.Pos),
      IsFixedDigits 4 year ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 month ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 day ∧
      IsFixedDigits 2 hh ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 mm ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 ss ∧
      natOf hh ≤ 23 ∧ natOf mm ≤ 59 ∧ natOf ss ≤ 59 ∧
      s = year ++ "-" ++ month ++ "-" ++ day ++ "T" ++ hh ++ ":" ++ mm ++ ":" ++ ss ++ rest ∧
      p.Splits (year ++ "-" ++ month ++ "-" ++ day ++ "T" ++ hh ++ ":" ++ mm ++ ":" ++ ss)
        rest ∧
      parser.go config .any
        { ({} : DateBuilder) with
          y := some (Int.ofNat (natOf year)),
          M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf month) hm),
          d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf day) hd),
          H := some H, m := some m, s := some sec }
        tail ⟨s, p⟩ = ParseResult.success out zt

builder over the whole string `s`, ending at `endPos` with value `zt`, then `s` decomposes as the
rendering of a well-formed UTC datetime, and `build` succeeds on the corresponding filled builder
(whose time fields are the parsed hour/minute/second values).
items.statement:
theorem dateUTC_full_inv {s : String} (config : FormatConfig)
    (hcfg : config.allowLeapSeconds = false) (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hgo : parser.go config .any {}
        [.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
         .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2}), .string "T",
         .modifier (.H {padding := 2}), .string ":", .modifier (.m {padding := 2}),
         .string ":", .modifier (.s {padding := 2}), .string "Z"]
        ⟨s, s.startPos⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, s.endPos⟩ zt) :
    ∃ (year month day hh mm ss : String)
      (hm : 1 ≤ natOf month ∧ natOf month ≤ 12)
      (hd : 1 ≤ natOf day ∧ natOf day ≤ 31),
      IsFixedDigits 4 year ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 month ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 day ∧
      IsFixedDigits 2 hh ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 mm ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 ss ∧
      natOf hh ≤ 23 ∧ natOf mm ≤ 59 ∧ natOf ss ≤ 59 ∧
      s = year ++ "-" ++ month ++ "-" ++ day ++ "T" ++ hh ++ ":" ++ mm ++ ":" ++ ss ++ "Z" ∧
      ∃ (H : Hour.Ordinal) (m : Minute.Ordinal) (sec : Second.Ordinal true),
        ({ ({} : DateBuilder) with
                y := some (Int.ofNat (natOf year)),
                M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf month) hm),
                d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf day) hd),
                H := some H, m := some m, s := some sec }).build .any = some zt

`±hhmm` offset (`.x .hourMinute`) rather than the `'Z'` marker.
items.statement:
theorem dateWithOffset_full_inv {s : String} (config : FormatConfig)
    (hcfg : config.allowLeapSeconds = false) (hlen : checkOffsetLen s = true)
    (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hgo : parser.go config .any {}
        [.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
         .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2}), .string "T",
         .modifier (.H {padding := 2}), .string ":", .modifier (.m {padding := 2}),
         .string ":", .modifier (.s {padding := 2}), .modifier (.x .hourMinute)]
        ⟨s, s.startPos⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, s.endPos⟩ zt) :
    ∃ (year month day hh mm ss : String) (neg : Bool) (ohh omm : String)
      (hm : 1 ≤ natOf month ∧ natOf month ≤ 12)
      (hd : 1 ≤ natOf day ∧ natOf day ≤ 31),
      IsFixedDigits 4 year ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 month ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 day ∧
      IsFixedDigits 2 hh ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 mm ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 ss ∧
      IsFixedDigits 2 ohh ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 omm ∧
      natOf hh ≤ 23 ∧ natOf mm ≤ 59 ∧ natOf ss ≤ 59 ∧
      natOf ohh ≤ 23 ∧ natOf omm ≤ 59 ∧
      s = year ++ "-" ++ month ++ "-" ++ day ++ "T" ++ hh ++ ":" ++ mm ++ ":" ++ ss
          ++ ((if neg then "-" else "+") ++ ohh ++ omm) ∧
      ∃ (H : Hour.Ordinal) (m : Minute.Ordinal) (sec : Second.Ordinal true)
        (off : Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset),
        ({ ({} : DateBuilder) with
                y := some (Int.ofNat (natOf year)),
                M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf month) hm),
                d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf day) hd),
                H := some H, m := some m, s := some sec, x := some off }).build .any = some zt

        H := some H, m := some m, s := some sec, x := some off }).build .any = some zt) :

items.doc:
**DateWithOffsetAndMillis full parse inversion.** Hybrid of `dateUTCWithMillis_full_inv` (the

items.statement:

    (hcfg : config.allowLeapSeconds = false) (hlen : checkOffsetLen s = true)
    (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hgo : parser.go config .any {}
        [.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
         .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2}), .string "T",
         .modifier (.H {padding := 2}), .string ":", .modifier (.m {padding := 2}),
         .string ":", .modifier (.s {padding := 2}), .string ".",
         .modifier (.S (.truncated 3)), .modifier (.x .hourMinute)]
        ⟨s, s.startPos⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, s.endPos⟩ zt) :
    ∃ (year month day hh mm ss sss : String) (neg : Bool) (ohh omm : String)
      (hm : 1 ≤ natOf month ∧ natOf month ≤ 12)
      (hd : 1 ≤ natOf day ∧ natOf day ≤ 31),
      IsFixedDigits 4 year ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 month ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 day ∧
      IsFixedDigits 2 hh ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 mm ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 ss ∧ IsFixedDigits 3 sss ∧
      IsFixedDigits 2 ohh ∧ IsFixedDigits 2 omm ∧
      natOf hh ≤ 23 ∧ natOf mm ≤ 59 ∧ natOf ss ≤ 59 ∧
      natOf ohh ≤ 23 ∧ natOf omm ≤ 59 ∧
      s = year ++ "-" ++ month ++ "-" ++ day ++ "T" ++ hh ++ ":" ++ mm ++ ":" ++ ss
          ++ "." ++ sss ++ ((if neg then "-" else "+") ++ ohh ++ omm) ∧
      ∃ (H : Hour.Ordinal) (m : Minute.Ordinal) (sec : Second.Ordinal true)
        (S : Nanosecond.Ordinal) (off : Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset),
        ({ ({} : DateBuilder) with
                y := some (Int.ofNat (natOf year)),
                M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf month) hm),
                d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf day) hd),
                H := some H, m := some m, s := some sec, S := some S,
                x := some off }).build .any = some zt

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.wf_of_parse
items.doc:
**`wf_of_parse`** (the target). Dispatch on which parser in the 5-way alternation succeeded.
The DateOnly branch is fully discharged by `dateOnly_wf_inv`; the other four formats require the
analogous full inversions (see the honest-blocker note in the report).
items.statement:
theorem wf_of_parse {str : String} (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hlen : checkOffsetLen str = true)
    (hzt : (DateOnly.parse str <|> DateUTC.parse str
        <|> DateUTCWithMillis.parse str <|> DateWithOffset.parse str
        <|> DateWithOffsetAndMillis.parse str).toOption = some zt) :
    ∃ c : DatetimeComponents, str = c.asString ∧ c.syntaxWf ∧ c.constraintsWf

items.note:
## Master "parse produces error" helpers

`GenericFormat.parse F s = (parser F.string F.config .any <* eof).run s`. Two ways the alternation's
earlier parsers fail on a wrong-form string:
  (A) the inner `parser` itself errors (a `pstring`/offset step diverges); or
  (B) the inner `parser` succeeds but *not at end of string* (leftover), so the trailing `<* eof`
      rejects.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_error_of_parser_error
items.doc: (A) If the inner `parser` errors, so does `.parse`.
items.statement:
theorem parse_error_of_parser_error {aw : Awareness} (F : GenericFormat aw) (s : String)
    (pos : ParseIt) (err : Std.Internal.Parsec.Error)
    (h : parser F.string F.config aw ⟨s, s.startPos⟩ = ParseResult.error pos err) :
    ∃ e, F.parse s = .error e

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_error_of_parser_success_ne_end
items.doc:
(B) If the inner `parser` succeeds at a position `p ≠ endPos`, `<* eof` rejects, so `.parse`
errors.
items.statement:
theorem parse_error_of_parser_success_ne_end {aw : Awareness} (F : GenericFormat aw) (s : String)
    (p : s.Pos) (a : aw.type) (hp : p ≠ s.endPos)
    (h : parser F.string F.config aw ⟨s, s.startPos⟩ = ParseResult.success ⟨s, p⟩ a) :
    ∃ e, F.parse s = .error e

items.note:
## DateOnly fails on a time-bearing string

`c.asString = c.date.asString ++ tp.asString` with `tp.asString = "T" ++ ...` nonempty. The DateOnly
format's `parser.go` threads the five date steps identically (they only inspect the date prefix),
`build` succeeds, but the resulting position sits right after the date (before `"T"`), which is not
`endPos`. So `<* eof` rejects.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.dateOnly_go_on_prefix
items.doc:
The DateOnly `parser.go` threaded on `c.date.asString ++ tail` (any `tail`) reaches `[]` with the
date builder at the position splitting `c.date.asString | tail`.
items.statement:
theorem dateOnly_go_on_prefix {d : DateComponents} (tail : String) (config : FormatConfig)
    (hsyn : d.syntaxWf) (hcon : d.constraintsWf) :
    ∃ (hm : 1 ≤ natOf d.month ∧ natOf d.month ≤ 12)
      (hd : 1 ≤ natOf d.day ∧ natOf d.day ≤ 31)
      (p : (d.asString ++ tail).Pos),
      parser.go config .any {}
          [.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
           .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2})]
          ⟨d.asString ++ tail, (d.asString ++ tail).startPos⟩
        = parser.go config .any
            { ({} : DateBuilder) with
              y := some (Int.ofNat (natOf d.year)),
              M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf d.month) hm),
              d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf d.day) hd) }
            [] ⟨d.asString ++ tail, p⟩ ∧
      p.Splits d.asString tail

items.doc:

`c.asString = c.date.asString ++ tp.asString` with `tp.asString` nonempty (starts with `"T"`),

theorem dateOnly_parse_error_of_time {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart)

    ∃ e, DateOnly.parse c.asString = .error e

items.doc: `pstring (singleton lc)` fails at position `p` whose remaining suffix starts with `c ≠ lc`.

items.note:
## Shared `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` prefix threading

All four time-bearing formats share the 11-part prefix `[y,"-",M,"-",d,"T",H,":",m,":",s]`. This
lemma threads that prefix on `c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString ++ tail` (any `tail`, any
format suffix `suf`), leaving `parser.go` positioned after the seconds field with the six-field
builder, ready to run `suf`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.prefix_thread
items.statement:
theorem prefix_thread {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart) (tail : String)
    (config : FormatConfig) (hcfg : config.allowLeapSeconds = false)
    (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf) (htime : c.time = some tp)
    (suf : FormatString) :
    ∃ (hm : 1 ≤ natOf c.date.month ∧ natOf c.date.month ≤ 12)
      (hd : 1 ≤ natOf c.date.day ∧ natOf c.date.day ≤ 31)
      (hh : 0 ≤ natOf tp.time.hours ∧ natOf tp.time.hours ≤ 23)
      (hmin : 0 ≤ natOf tp.time.minutes ∧ natOf tp.time.minutes ≤ 59)
      (hsec : 0 ≤ natOf tp.time.seconds ∧ natOf tp.time.seconds ≤ 59)
      (p : (c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString ++ tail).Pos),
      parser.go config .any {}
          ([.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
            .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2}), .string "T",
            .modifier (.H {padding := 2}), .string ":", .modifier (.m {padding := 2}),
            .string ":", .modifier (.s {padding := 2})] ++ suf)
          ⟨c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString ++ tail,
            (c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString ++ tail).startPos⟩
        = parser.go config .any
            { ({} : DateBuilder) with
              y := some (Int.ofNat (natOf c.date.year)),
              M := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf c.date.month) hm),
              d := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf c.date.day) hd),
              H := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf tp.time.hours) hh),
              m := some (Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf tp.time.minutes) hmin),
              s := some ((Bounded.LE.ofNat' (natOf tp.time.seconds) hsec).expandTop (by decide)
                          : Bounded.LE 0 60) }
            suf ⟨c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString ++ tail, p⟩ ∧
      p.Splits (c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString) tail

items.note:
## Tail structure after `time.asString`

`c.asString = c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString ++ tail`, where
`tail = (millis-part) ++ tp.zone.asString`. We expose `tail = singleton c₀ ++ rest` and identify the
leading char `c₀` for each form.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.asString_prefix_tail
items.doc: `c.asString` factors through the shared prefix and a tail.
items.statement:
theorem asString_prefix_tail {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart) (htime : c.time = some tp) :
    c.asString = c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.asString
      ++ ((match tp.millis with | none => "" | some sss => "." ++ sss) ++ tp.zone.asString)

items.note:
## Wrong-form failure via prefix + next-part mismatch

Given a `.string (singleton lc)` as the first suffix part, if the tail (after `ss`) starts with
`c₀ ≠ lc`, the format `F = prefix ++ [.string (singleton lc), ...]` errors on `c.asString`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_error_string_suffix
items.doc:
Master wrong-form failure for formats whose first post-prefix part is a `.string (singleton lc)`
literal, when the actual tail starts with `c₀ ≠ lc`.
items.statement:
theorem parse_error_string_suffix (F : GenericFormat .any)
    {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart) (lc c₀ : Char) (rest : String) (suf' : FormatString)
    (hcfg : F.config.allowLeapSeconds = false)
    (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf) (htime : c.time = some tp)
    (hstr : F.string
      = [.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
         .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2}), .string "T",
         .modifier (.H {padding := 2}), .string ":", .modifier (.m {padding := 2}),
         .string ":", .modifier (.s {padding := 2})] ++ (.string (String.singleton lc) :: suf'))
    (htail : (match tp.millis with | none => "" | some sss => "." ++ sss) ++ tp.zone.asString
      = String.singleton c₀ ++ rest)
    (hne : lc ≠ c₀) :
    ∃ e, F.parse c.asString = .error e

items.note:
## Tail leading-char decompositions

Identify `tail = singleton c₀ ++ rest` for each shape.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.tail_millis
items.doc: Millis present: tail starts with `'.'`.
items.statement:
theorem tail_millis {tp : TimePart} {sss : String} (hmillis : tp.millis = some sss) :
    ((match tp.millis with | none => "" | some sss => "." ++ sss) ++ tp.zone.asString)
      = String.singleton '.' ++ (sss ++ tp.zone.asString)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.tail_offset
items.doc: No millis, offset zone: tail starts with the sign char.
items.statement:
theorem tail_offset {tp : TimePart} {o : OffsetComponents}
    (hmillis : tp.millis = none) (hzone : tp.zone = Zone.offset o) :
    ((match tp.millis with | none => "" | some sss => "." ++ sss) ++ tp.zone.asString)
      = String.singleton (if o.negative then '-' else '+') ++ (o.hours ++ o.minutes)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.tail_utc
items.doc: No millis, UTC zone: tail is exactly `"Z"`.
items.statement:
theorem tail_utc {tp : TimePart} (hmillis : tp.millis = none) (hutc : tp.zone = Zone.utc) :
    ((match tp.millis with | none => "" | some sss => "." ++ sss) ++ tp.zone.asString)
      = String.singleton 'Z' ++ ""

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.parse_error_offset_suffix
items.doc:
Master wrong-form failure for formats whose first post-prefix part is the offset modifier
`.x .hourMinute`, when the actual tail starts with `c₀ ∉ {'+','-'}`.
items.statement:
theorem parse_error_offset_suffix (F : GenericFormat .any)
    {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart) (c₀ : Char) (rest : String) (suf' : FormatString)
    (hcfg : F.config.allowLeapSeconds = false)
    (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf) (htime : c.time = some tp)
    (hstr : F.string
      = [.modifier (.y .fourDigit), .string "-", .modifier (.M (.inl {padding := 2})),
         .string "-", .modifier (.d {padding := 2}), .string "T",
         .modifier (.H {padding := 2}), .string ":", .modifier (.m {padding := 2}),
         .string ":", .modifier (.s {padding := 2})] ++ (.modifier (.x .hourMinute) :: suf'))
    (htail : (match tp.millis with | none => "" | some sss => "." ++ sss) ++ tp.zone.asString
      = String.singleton c₀ ++ rest)
    (hp : c₀ ≠ '+') (hm : c₀ ≠ '-') :
    ∃ e, F.parse c.asString = .error e

items.note:
## Forward parse-guard lemmas

`Datetime.parse` applies three Boolean guards (`dateContainsLeapSeconds`, `checkOffsetLen`,
`tzOffsetMinsLt60`) before the format alternation. On a well-formed rendering `c.asString` all three
pass; these lemmas discharge them for `parse_complete`. The offset-minutes guard reduces to the
grammar bound `natOf o.minutes ≤ 59`, which requires the `String.Slice`-level fact that
`toNat?` and `isNat` depend only on the character list.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.slice_toNat?_congr
items.doc:
`String.Slice.isNat` and `String.Slice.toNat?` see only the underlying character list, so two
slices with equal `copy.toList` have equal `toNat?`.
items.statement:
theorem slice_toNat?_congr (s t : String.Slice) (h : s.copy.toList = t.copy.toList) :
    s.toNat? = t.toNat?

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.toNat?_congr
items.doc: `String.toNat?` depends only on the character list.
items.statement: theorem toNat?_congr (s t : String) (h : s.toList = t.toList) : s.toNat? = t.toNat?

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.toNat?_eq_natOf
items.doc: On a digit string, `toNat?` succeeds with the grammar's `natOf`.
items.statement: theorem toNat?_eq_natOf (s : String) (h : IsDigits s) : s.toNat? = some (natOf s)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.takeEnd_two_toList
items.doc:
Taking the last two characters of `pre ++ mm`, where `mm` has length two, yields exactly `mm`
(at the level of character lists).
items.statement:
theorem takeEnd_two_toList {pre mm : String} (h2 : mm.length = 2) :
    ((pre ++ mm).takeEnd 2).copy.toList = mm.toList

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.endsWith_singleton
items.doc: A string that ends in a `String.singleton c` character `endsWith` its singleton.
items.statement:
theorem endsWith_singleton {pre : String} {c : Char} :
    (pre ++ String.singleton c).endsWith (String.singleton c) = true

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.tzOffsetMinsLt60_asString
items.doc:
**Timezone-offset-minutes guard.** On a well-formed rendering the `tzOffsetMinsLt60` guard
passes: date-only strings are length ≤ 10, UTC strings end in `'Z'`, and offset strings end in
the two-digit minutes field `mm`, which the grammar bounds by `59 < 60`.
items.statement:
theorem tzOffsetMinsLt60_asString {c : DatetimeComponents} (hsyn : c.syntaxWf)
    (hcon : c.constraintsWf) :
    tzOffsetMinsLt60 c.asString = true

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.splitOnPPrepend_head
items.doc:
List-level: splitting `pre ++ sep :: suf` on `P`, with `pre` separator-free and `P sep`, yields
a first segment `acc.reverse ++ pre`.
items.statement:
theorem splitOnPPrepend_head {α} (P : α → Bool) (pre suf acc : List α) (sep : α)
    (hsep : P sep = true) (hpre : ∀ x ∈ pre, P x = false) :
    ∃ tl, List.splitOnPPrepend P (pre ++ sep :: suf) acc = (acc.reverse ++ pre) :: tl

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.splitToList_head_sep
items.doc:
String-level: splitting `pre ++ sep ++ rest` on `P`, with `pre` separator-free and `P sep`,
puts `pre` at the head of the result.
items.statement:
theorem splitToList_head_sep (pre rest : String) (P : Char → Bool) (sep : Char)
    (hsep : P sep = true) (hpre : ∀ ch ∈ pre.toList, P ch = false) :
    ∃ tl, (pre ++ String.singleton sep ++ rest).splitToList P = pre :: tl

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.date_no_T
items.doc: The date rendering `year ++ "-" ++ month ++ "-" ++ day` contains no `'T'`.
items.statement:
theorem date_no_T {d : DateComponents} (h : d.syntaxWf) :
    ∀ ch ∈ d.asString.toList, decide (ch = 'T') = false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.checkComponentLen_asString
items.doc:
**Offset-length guard.** On a well-formed rendering the `checkOffsetLen` guard passes:
splitting on `'T'` separates the date from the time-bearing tail, then splitting the tail on
an offset sign isolates exactly four digit characters. Date-only and UTC renderings contain no
offset sign and pass directly.
items.statement:
theorem checkComponentLen_asString {c : DatetimeComponents} (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) :
    checkOffsetLen c.asString = true

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.build_tz_offset
items.doc:
**Built `ZonedDateTime`'s timezone offset.** `DateBuilder.build .any` produces a
`ZonedDateTime` whose timezone offset is the builder's resolved offset field
(`O <|> X <|> x <|> Z`, defaulting to zero).
items.statement:
theorem build_tz_offset (b : DateBuilder) (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (h : b.build .any = some zt) :
    zt.timezone.offset = (b.O <|> b.X <|> b.x <|> b.Z).getD TimeZone.Offset.zero

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.build_tz_offset_zero
items.doc:
**Timezone offset of a DateOnly/UTC parse.** When the builder's offset field is unset
(the zero-offset zone, as in the DateOnly / UTC / UTC-with-millis forms), the parsed
`ZonedDateTime`'s offset seconds are zero.
items.statement:
theorem build_tz_offset_zero (b : DateBuilder) (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (h : b.build .any = some zt) (hb : b.O = none ∧ b.X = none ∧ b.x = none ∧ b.Z = none) :
    zt.timezone.offset.second.val = 0

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.build_tz_offset_x
items.doc:
**Timezone offset of an offset-form parse.** When the builder's `x` field carries the parsed
`±(hh·3600+mm·60)` offset (and `O`/`X`/`Z` are unset, as in the two offset forms), the parsed
`ZonedDateTime`'s offset seconds are exactly that signed magnitude.
items.statement:
theorem build_tz_offset_x (b : DateBuilder) (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime) (v : Int)
    (h : b.build .any = some zt)
    (hb : b.O = none ∧ b.X = none ∧ b.x = some (TimeZone.Offset.ofSeconds ⟨v⟩) ∧ b.Z = none) :
    zt.timezone.offset.second.val = v

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.dateOnly_parse_tz
items.doc: DateOnly parse: the timezone offset is zero (the builder sets no offset field).
items.statement:
theorem dateOnly_parse_tz {d : DateComponents} (hsyn : d.syntaxWf) (hcon : d.constraintsWf) :
    ∃ zt, DateOnly.parse d.asString = .ok zt ∧ zt.timezone.offset.second.val = 0

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.dateUTC_parse_tz
items.doc: DateUTC parse: the timezone offset is zero.
items.statement:
theorem dateUTC_parse_tz {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart)
    (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf)
    (htime : c.time = some tp) (hutc : tp.zone = Zone.utc) (hmillis : tp.millis = none) :
    ∃ zt, DateUTC.parse c.asString = .ok zt ∧ zt.timezone.offset.second.val = 0

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.dateUTCWithMillis_parse_tz
items.doc: DateUTCWithMillis parse: the timezone offset is zero.
items.statement:
theorem dateUTCWithMillis_parse_tz {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart) (sss : String)
    (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf)
    (htime : c.time = some tp) (hutc : tp.zone = Zone.utc) (hmillis : tp.millis = some sss) :
    ∃ zt, DateUTCWithMillis.parse c.asString = .ok zt ∧ zt.timezone.offset.second.val = 0

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.dateWithOffset_parse_tz
items.doc: DateWithOffset parse: the timezone offset is the parsed `±(hh·3600+mm·60)`, bounded by `hcon`.
items.statement:
theorem dateWithOffset_parse_tz {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart) (o : OffsetComponents)
    (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf)
    (htime : c.time = some tp) (hzone : tp.zone = Zone.offset o) (hmillis : tp.millis = none) :
    ∃ zt, DateWithOffset.parse c.asString = .ok zt ∧
      zt.timezone.offset.second.val
        = ((natOf o.hours : Int) * 3600 + (natOf o.minutes : Int) * 60)
            * (if o.negative then -1 else 1)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.dateWithOffsetAndMillis_parse_tz
items.doc: DateWithOffsetAndMillis parse: the timezone offset is the parsed `±(hh·3600+mm·60)`.
items.statement:
theorem dateWithOffsetAndMillis_parse_tz {c : DatetimeComponents} (tp : TimePart)
    (o : OffsetComponents) (sss : String)
    (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf)
    (htime : c.time = some tp) (hzone : tp.zone = Zone.offset o) (hmillis : tp.millis = some sss) :
    ∃ zt, DateWithOffsetAndMillis.parse c.asString = .ok zt ∧
      zt.timezone.offset.second.val
        = ((natOf o.hours : Int) * 3600 + (natOf o.minutes : Int) * 60)
            * (if o.negative then -1 else 1)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.offset_lt_max_of_syntaxWf
items.doc:
**Offset-range side condition.** The `< MAX_OFFSET_SECONDS` check that `Datetime.parse` applies
to the parsed zone always passes on a well-formed string, because the grammar bounds offsets to
`±23:59` (`|hh·3600 + mm·60| ≤ 86340 < 86400`). Needs `hcon` for the numeric bounds `hh ≤ 23`,
`mm ≤ 59`; `hsyn` alone (fixed-digit widths) would only give `hh, mm ≤ 99`.
items.statement:
theorem offset_lt_max_of_syntaxWf {c : DatetimeComponents} (hsyn : c.syntaxWf)
    (hcon : c.constraintsWf)
    (zt : Std.Time.ZonedDateTime)
    (hzt : (DateOnly.parse c.asString <|> DateUTC.parse c.asString
        <|> DateUTCWithMillis.parse c.asString <|> DateWithOffset.parse c.asString
        <|> DateWithOffsetAndMillis.parse c.asString).toOption = some zt) :
    zt.timezone.offset.second.val.natAbs < MAX_OFFSET_SECONDS

items.note:
## Leap-seconds guard

`dateContainsLeapSeconds str` reads the two bytes at positions 17 and 18 (the seconds field of a
`Date 'T' Time …` rendering, whose prefix `yyyy-MM-ddThh:mm:` is exactly 17 ASCII bytes) and rejects
`"…60…"`. On a well-formed rendering it always returns `false`: date-only strings are too short
(length 10 < 20), and for time-bearing strings the grammar bounds the seconds field by `59`, so it
is never `"60"`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.isDigit_utf8Size_one
items.doc: An ASCII digit occupies exactly one UTF-8 byte.
items.statement: theorem isDigit_utf8Size_one {c : Char} (h : c.isDigit = true) : c.utf8Size = 1

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.isDigits_utf8Size_one
items.doc: Every character of a digit string occupies one UTF-8 byte.
items.statement:
theorem isDigits_utf8Size_one {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) :
    ∀ c ∈ s.toList, c.utf8Size = 1

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.utf8GetAux?_ascii_skip
items.doc:
`utf8GetAux?` skips over an all-ASCII (one-byte-per-char) prefix `l1`: reading at byte index `n`
past the prefix is the same as reading `l2` starting at byte index `i.byteIdx + l1.length`.
items.statement:
theorem utf8GetAux?_ascii_skip (l2 : List Char) (n : Nat) :
    ∀ (l1 : List Char) (i : String.Pos.Raw),
      (∀ c ∈ l1, c.utf8Size = 1) →
      i.byteIdx + l1.length ≤ n →
      String.Pos.Raw.utf8GetAux? (l1 ++ l2) i ⟨n⟩
        = String.Pos.Raw.utf8GetAux? l2 ⟨i.byteIdx + l1.length⟩ ⟨n⟩

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.utf8GetAux?_pair
items.doc:
On a character list `pre ++ a :: b :: rest` with a 17-char all-ASCII prefix `pre`, positions 17
and 18 read off `a` and `b`.
items.statement:
theorem utf8GetAux?_pair (pre : List Char) (a b : Char) (rest : List Char)
    (hlen : pre.length = 17) (hpre : ∀ c ∈ pre, c.utf8Size = 1) (ha : a.utf8Size = 1) :
    String.Pos.Raw.utf8GetAux? (pre ++ a :: b :: rest) 0 ⟨17⟩ = some a ∧
    String.Pos.Raw.utf8GetAux? (pre ++ a :: b :: rest) 0 ⟨18⟩ = some b

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.asString_seconds_split
items.doc: A time-bearing rendering splits as (17-char prefix `yyyy-MM-ddThh:mm:`) ++ seconds ++ tail.
items.statement:
theorem asString_seconds_split {c : DatetimeComponents} {tp : TimePart} (htime : c.time = some tp) :
    ∃ tail, c.asString = (c.date.asString ++ "T" ++ tp.time.hours ++ ":" ++ tp.time.minutes ++ ":")
      ++ tp.time.seconds ++ tail

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.dateContainsLeapSeconds_asString
items.doc:
**Leap-seconds guard.** On a well-formed rendering the `dateContainsLeapSeconds` guard is
`false`: date-only strings are length 10 < 20, and for time-bearing strings the seconds field
(positions 17–18) is bounded by 59 by the grammar's constraints, so it is never `"60"`.
items.statement:
theorem dateContainsLeapSeconds_asString {c : DatetimeComponents} (hsyn : c.syntaxWf)
    (hcon : c.constraintsWf) :
    dateContainsLeapSeconds c.asString = false

items.note:
## Int64-range bound for the datetime value

The grammar bounds a datetime to 4-digit years and `±23:59` offsets, so `toMillis` always fits in
`Int64`. We prove this by bounding `epochDays` (the Hinnant forward algorithm) and then the linear
`toMillis` combination. `omega` treats `Int.tdiv`/`Int.tmod` as opaque, so each `tdiv` site is fed the
Euclidean identity `Int.mul_tdiv_add_tmod` plus `tmod` sign/magnitude facts.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.epochDays_era_block
items.doc:
The era-and-year-of-era contribution of `epochDays` for a nonnegative shifted year `yp ≤ 9999`.
Feeds `omega` the `tdiv`/`tmod` facts for the `/400`, `/4`, and `/100` divisions.
items.statement:
theorem epochDays_era_block (yp : Int) (hlb : 0 ≤ yp) (hub : yp ≤ 9999) :
    -3 ≤ yp.tdiv 400 * 146097 +
        ((yp - yp.tdiv 400 * 400) * 365 + (yp - yp.tdiv 400 * 400).tdiv 4
          - (yp - yp.tdiv 400 * 400).tdiv 100) ∧
      yp.tdiv 400 * 146097 +
        ((yp - yp.tdiv 400 * 400) * 365 + (yp - yp.tdiv 400 * 400).tdiv 4
          - (yp - yp.tdiv 400 * 400).tdiv 100) ≤ 3652062

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.epochDays_bounds
items.doc:
`epochDays` is bounded for any grammar-legal `(y, m, d)` with `y ≤ 9999`, `1 ≤ m ≤ 12`,
`1 ≤ d ≤ 31`. The endpoints `epochDays 0 1 1 = -719528` and `epochDays 9999 12 31 = 2932896`
are tight on the low side; the high bound is loosened to `2933000` (gap 104 days) to keep the
`omega` combination robust.
items.statement:
theorem epochDays_bounds {y m d : Nat} (hy : y ≤ 9999) (hm : 1 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ 12)
    (hd : 1 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ 31) :
    -719528 ≤ epochDays y m d ∧ epochDays y m d ≤ 2933000

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.daysInMonth_le_31
items.doc: `daysInMonth` is at most `31` for any year/month.
items.statement: theorem daysInMonth_le_31 (y m : Nat) : daysInMonth y m ≤ 31

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.offsetSeconds_bound
items.doc: A constraint-well-formed zone contributes at most `±86340` seconds (`23:59` in seconds).
items.statement:
theorem offsetSeconds_bound {z : Zone} (h : z.constraintsWf) :
    -86340 ≤ z.offsetSeconds ∧ z.offsetSeconds ≤ 86340

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.toMillis_range
items.doc:
A well-formed datetime's epoch-millisecond value fits in a small range. The endpoints are
`0000-01-01T00:00:00+2359` (`-62167305540000`) and `9999-12-31T23:59:59.999-2359`; the upper
bound is loosened to `253411372739999` to absorb the `epochDays` slack (104 days × 86400000 ms),
still far inside `Int64`.
items.statement:
theorem toMillis_range {c : DatetimeComponents} (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf) :
    -62167305540000 ≤ c.toMillis ∧ c.toMillis ≤ 253411372739999

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Datetime.toMillis_int64_range
items.doc: Corollary: a well-formed datetime's value never overflows `Int64`.
items.statement:
theorem toMillis_int64_range {c : DatetimeComponents} (hsyn : c.syntaxWf) (hcon : c.constraintsWf) :
    Int64.MIN ≤ c.toMillis ∧ c.toMillis ≤ Int64.MAX

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.wf_iff_exists_value
items.doc: Well-formed decimal syntax is exactly syntax to which the grammar assigns some value.
items.statement:
public theorem wf_iff_exists_value {s : String} :
    IsWfDecimal s ↔ ∃ v, IsDecimalValue s v

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.parse_complete
items.doc:
Completeness of `Decimal.parse`: if the grammar assigns `s` the value `d.toInt`, then parsing
accepts the string as `d`. Well-formedness is not a separate hypothesis — `IsDecimalValue`
already asserts that `s` is a rendering of the grammar's productions.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_complete (s : String) (d : Decimal)
    (hval : IsDecimalValue s d.toInt) : Decimal.parse s = some d

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.parse_sound
items.doc:
Soundness of `Decimal.parse`: if parsing succeeds, then the input is a well-formed rendering
whose grammar value is exactly the returned decimal's value. (The value is automatically in
`Int64` range, since `d : Decimal = Int64`, so no range conjunct is stated.)
items.statement:
public theorem parse_sound (s : String) (d : Decimal) (h : Decimal.parse s = some d) :
    IsDecimalValue s d.toInt

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.parse_eq_some_iff_isDecimalValue
items.doc:
Exact parser characterization: parsing succeeds with `d` precisely when the declarative
grammar relation assigns the input the value `d.toInt`.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_eq_some_iff_isDecimalValue (s : String) (d : Decimal) :
    Decimal.parse s = some d ↔ IsDecimalValue s d.toInt

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.parse_toString_roundtrip
items.doc: Parsing the canonical string representation of a decimal returns the same decimal.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_toString_roundtrip (d : Decimal) :
    Decimal.parse (toString d) = some d

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.parse_eq_none_iff
items.doc:
Failure characterization for `Decimal.parse`: parsing rejects exactly malformed strings and
well-formed strings whose grammar value overflows the `Int64` range. The value relation is
total on well-formed syntax, so these cases are exhaustive and mutually exclusive.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.toString_injective
items.doc: `toString` is injective: distinct decimals produce distinct strings.
items.statement: public theorem toString_injective (d d' : Decimal) (h : toString d = toString d') : d = d'

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq
items.doc: Equal normal form iff equal value: normalization decides decimal equality.
items.statement:
public theorem normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq (s s' : String) :
    normalize s = normalize s' ↔ Decimal.parse s = Decimal.parse s'

modules.title: Decimal grammar: definitions
modules.doc:
This file contains only the grammar-level definitions — the well-formedness predicates and the
value relation — as a direct, parser-independent transcription of the decimal grammar.
`DecimalProduction` relates a rendering to its grammar fields, `IsWfDecimal` existentially hides
those fields, `value` gives their denotation, and `IsDecimalValue s v` adds that denotation to the
same production witness. The lemmas connecting these definitions to `Decimal.parse` (in
particular the digit-string ↔ `toInt?'`/`toNat?'` bridges) live in
`Cedar.Thm.Ext.Decimal.Lemmas`.

`Sign ::= ['-']` uses the shared `IsWfSign` predicate. The decimal-specific `Natural` and
`Fraction` productions are named locally using the shared digit predicates `IsDigits` and
`IsAtMostNDigits`. Their value readers (`natOf`, `signOf`, and `lenOf`) and string-to-number bridges
live in `Cedar.Thm.Data.String`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.IsNatural
items.doc:
The grammar's `Natural ::= Digit⁺`: the unsigned natural-number production. An `abbrev` for
the shared `IsDigits` predicate, so every `IsDigits` lemma applies without unfolding.
items.statement: public abbrev IsNatural (s : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.IsWfFrac
items.doc:
The grammar's `Fraction ::= Digit{1,4}`: 1 to `DECIMAL_DIGITS` digits, an instance of the
shared bounded-digits predicate.
items.statement: public def IsWfFrac (s : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.DecimalProduction
items.doc:
A decimal grammar production: `s` is the rendering of well-formed `Sign`, `Natural`, and
`Fraction` fields, concatenated around the literal decimal point.
items.statement: public def DecimalProduction (s sign natural fraction : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.IsWfDecimal
items.doc:
Well-formed decimal syntax: `s` is the rendering of a well-formed `Sign ::= ['-']`,
`Natural ::= Digit⁺`, `'.'`, and `Fraction ::= Digit{1,4}`, concatenated in that order.
This is the direct grammar transcription; it does not compute a value or invoke a parser.
items.statement: public def IsWfDecimal (s : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.value
items.doc:
The grammar's value function, applied to an already-decomposed literal:

  value = sign × (nat(Natural) × 10⁴ + nat(Fraction) × 10^(4 − |Fraction|))

`IsWfFrac fraction` bounds `lenOf fraction ≤ DECIMAL_DIGITS`, so converting the second
exponent to `Nat` does not clamp a negative value on a well-formed field.
items.statement: public def value (sign natural fraction : String) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.IsDecimalValue
items.doc:
`v` is the value of the decimal literal `s`: `s` is the rendering of a well-formed
`Sign ::= ['-']`, `Natural ::= Digit⁺`, `'.'`, and `Fraction ::= Digit{1,4}`, concatenated in
that order, and `v` is what the grammar's value function assigns to those fields.

The existential supplies the split, so no string surgery (`front`/`drop`/`splitToList`) and no
`Option` appear here. The relation is single-valued (`isDecimalValue_unique`), and a string is
well-formed exactly when it has some value (`wf_iff_exists_value`).
items.statement: public def IsDecimalValue (s : String) (v : Int) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.normalize
items.doc:
Canonical-form normalizer: parse the string and re-serialize.
Returns `none` for malformed or out-of-range inputs.
items.statement: public def normalize (s : String) : Option String

modules.doc:
============================================================================================
# Grammar ↔ parser bridge lemmas

`IsDecimalValue` is phrased over the grammar's productions (`IsWfSign`/`IsNatural`/`IsWfFrac`)
as a rendering `sign ++ natural ++ "." ++ fraction`, with the value read off those three
fields. `Decimal.parse` instead splits on `'.'` first and parses the signed left field through
`toInt?'`. These lemmas connect the views: the rendering splits back into its parts, a digit
string is exactly one the stdlib parser accepts, and the two value expressions agree. Together
they reduce `Decimal.parse s` on a string with a value to a single `Int64` range check
(`parse_eq_decimal?_of_isDecimalValue`), which is what the soundness/completeness proofs
consume.

The `IsDigits` predicate and its `toNat?'` bridges (`no_underscore_of_isDigits`,
`isNat_of_isDigits`, `isDigits_of_isNat`, `toNat?'_isSome_of_isDigits`,
`isDigits_of_toNat?'_isSome`) are shared with the duration grammar and live in
`Cedar.Thm.Data.String`; the integer-specific lemmas below build on them.
============================================================================================

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.no_underscore_of_sign_nat
items.doc:
The concatenation of a well-formed `Sign` and `Natural` — the grammar's integer part —
contains no `'_'`.
items.statement:
theorem no_underscore_of_sign_nat {sign natural : String}
    (hs : IsWfSign sign) (hn : IsDigits natural) : (sign ++ natural).contains '_' = false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.toInt?'_isSome_of_sign_nat
items.doc: Forward bridge (integer): a well-formed `Sign` followed by a `Natural` parses as an integer.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.sign_nat_of_toInt?'_isSome
items.doc:
Backward bridge (integer): anything `toInt?'` accepts splits into a well-formed `Sign` and
`Natural`.
items.statement:
theorem sign_nat_of_toInt?'_isSome {s : String} (h : (toInt?' s).isSome = true) :
    ∃ sign natural, s = sign ++ natural ∧ IsWfSign sign ∧ IsDigits natural

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.ne_dash_of_sign_nat
items.doc:
A well-formed integer part is never a bare `"-"`: the grammar's `Digit⁺` requires at least one
digit after the sign. This is what the `left ≠ "-"` side condition asserts explicitly.
items.statement:
theorem ne_dash_of_sign_nat {sign natural : String}
    (hs : IsWfSign sign) (hn : IsDigits natural) : sign ++ natural ≠ "-"

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.no_dot_of_isDigits
items.doc: A digit string contains no `'.'` — the separator can only appear where the grammar puts it.
items.statement:
theorem no_dot_of_isDigits {s : String} (h : IsDigits s) :
    ∀ c ∈ s.toList, decide (c = '.') = false

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.no_dot_of_sign_nat
items.doc: The grammar's integer part contains no `'.'`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.splitToList_of_isWfDecimal
items.doc:
Splitting a well-formed rendering on `'.'` recovers the integer part and the fraction: the
only `'.'` in `sign ++ natural ++ "." ++ fraction` is the separator the grammar writes.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.parser_value_eq_value
items.doc:
The grammar's `value` equals the parser's value expression, which reads the sign
together with the left field through `toInt?'` and branches between adding and subtracting the
fraction. This is the one place the outer sign of the rendering has to be reconciled with the
signed integer the parser reads.
items.statement:
theorem parser_value_eq_value {sign natural fraction : String} {l : Int} {r : Nat}
    (hs : IsWfSign sign) (hn : IsNatural natural)
    (hl : toInt?' (sign ++ natural) = some l) (hr : toNat?' fraction = some r) :
    (if !(sign ++ natural).startsWith "-"
      then l * Int.pow 10 DECIMAL_DIGITS + r * Int.pow 10 (DECIMAL_DIGITS - fraction.length)
      else l * Int.pow 10 DECIMAL_DIGITS - r * Int.pow 10 (DECIMAL_DIGITS - fraction.length))
      = value sign natural fraction

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.parse_eq_decimal?_of_isDecimalValue
items.doc:
`Decimal.parse` on a string the grammar assigns the value `v`: the parser gets all the way to
the range check with exactly `v` in hand, so acceptance is decided by `decimal?` alone. Both
completeness and the overflow half of the failure characterization are corollaries.
items.statement:
theorem parse_eq_decimal?_of_isDecimalValue {s : String} {v : Int} (h : IsDecimalValue s v) :
    Decimal.parse s = Decimal.decimal? v

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.isDecimalValue_unique
items.doc:
The value spec is single-valued: a string has at most one value. Because the grammar puts
exactly one `'.'` in the rendering and `Natural` is a non-empty digit run, the decomposition a
witness supplies is forced, so `IsDecimalValue` is a function in relational clothing.
items.statement:
public theorem isDecimalValue_unique {s : String} {v₁ v₂ : Int}
    (h₁ : IsDecimalValue s v₁) (h₂ : IsDecimalValue s v₂) : v₁ = v₂

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.isDecimalValue_toString
items.doc:
The canonical string representation of a decimal is well-formed and denotes exactly that
decimal's value. Together with `parse_toString_roundtrip` this is what rules out a vacuously
satisfiable spec.
items.statement: public theorem isDecimalValue_toString (d : Decimal) : IsDecimalValue (toString d) d.toInt

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Decimal.toString_isWfDecimal
items.doc: The string produced by `toString d` is well-formed for parsing.
items.statement: public theorem toString_isWfDecimal (d : Decimal) : IsWfDecimal (toString d)

modules.doc:
Duration parser theorem surface.

`parse_sound` and `parse_complete` characterize successful parsing against the declarative
`IsDurationValue` relation. `parse_eq_none_iff` characterizes exactly when parsing rejects.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.wf_iff_exists_value
items.doc: Well-formed duration syntax is exactly syntax to which the grammar assigns some value.
items.statement:
public theorem wf_iff_exists_value {str : String} :
    IsWfDuration str ↔ ∃ v, IsDurationValue str v

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parse_complete
items.doc:
Completeness of `Duration.parse`: if the grammar assigns `str` the value `d.val.toInt`, then
parsing accepts the string as `d`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parse_sound
items.doc:
Soundness of `Duration.parse`: if parsing succeeds, the declarative grammar relation assigns
the input exactly the returned duration's value.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parse_eq_some_iff_isDurationValue
items.doc:
Exact parser characterization: parsing succeeds with `d` precisely when the declarative
grammar relation assigns the input the value `d.val.toInt`.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_eq_some_iff_isDurationValue (str : String) (d : Duration) :
    Duration.parse str = some d ↔ IsDurationValue str d.val.toInt

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parse_eq_none_iff
items.doc:
Failure characterization for `Duration.parse`: parsing rejects exactly malformed strings and
well-formed strings whose grammar value overflows the `Int64` range.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_eq_none_iff (str : String) :
    Duration.parse str = none ↔
    ¬ IsWfDuration str ∨
      ∃ v, IsDurationValue str v ∧ (v < Int64.MIN ∨ v > Int64.MAX)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parse_neg
items.doc: Parsing a negated duration string negates the underlying value.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_neg (s : String) (d : Duration)
    (hpos : ¬ s.startsWith "-")
    (h : Duration.parse s = some d) :
    Duration.parse ("-" ++ s) = duration? (-d.val.toInt)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.offset_durationSince_inverse
items.doc:
`offset` and `durationSince` are inverses: adding a duration then computing
the difference gives back the same duration.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parse_toString_roundtrip
items.doc: `parse ∘ toString` roundtrip: parsing the string representation recovers the original.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_toString_roundtrip (d : Duration) :
    Duration.parse (Duration.toString d) = some d

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.toString_injective
items.doc: `toString` is injective: distinct durations produce distinct strings.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq
items.doc: Equal normal form iff equal value: normalization decides duration equality.
items.statement:
public theorem normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq (s s' : String) :
    normalize s = normalize s' ↔ Duration.parse s = Duration.parse s'

modules.title: Duration grammar: definitions
modules.doc:
This file contains only grammar-level definitions: the well-formedness predicates and the value
relation. `IsWfDuration` states the syntax, `value` gives the denotation of already identified
components, and `IsDurationValue str v` combines the same witnesses to say that `str` denotes `v`.
The executable extraction machinery used to connect these definitions to `Duration.parse` lives
in `Cedar.Thm.Ext.Duration.Lemmas`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.durationChunk
items.doc:
Render an optional duration component as its string representation.
`none` produces `""`, `some digits` produces `digits ++ suffix`.
items.statement: public def durationChunk (digits? : Option String) (suffix : String) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.IsWfOptionalQuantity
items.doc:
Lift the `Digit⁺` quantity-token predicate (`IsDigits`) to optional components:
`none` is trivially valid.
items.statement: public def IsWfOptionalQuantity : Option String → Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.Components
items.doc:
The five optional digit-string components of a duration body, one per time unit.
Each field holds `none` (unit absent) or `some digits` (unit present with that value).
items.statement:
public structure Components where
  days : Option String
  hours : Option String
  minutes : Option String
  seconds : Option String
  milliseconds : Option String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.Components.nonempty
items.doc: At least one component must be present (the body cannot be empty).
items.statement: public def Components.nonempty (components : Components) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.Components.quantitiesWf
items.doc: Every present component must be a valid duration quantity (nonempty, parseable digits).
items.statement:
public def Components.quantitiesWf
    (components : Components) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.Components.asString
items.doc:
Canonical string representation: concatenate present components in order `d h m s ms`.
Absent components contribute `""`.
items.statement: public def Components.asString (components : Components) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.optionalNatOf
items.doc:
Natural-number value of an optional duration quantity. An absent component denotes zero;
a present well-formed component is read by the shared grammar-level `natOf`.
items.statement: public def optionalNatOf : Option String → Nat

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.Components.toMillis
items.doc: Unsigned millisecond value of already identified duration components.
items.statement: public def Components.toMillis (components : Components) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.value
items.doc: The grammar's value function, applied to an already identified sign and component record.
items.statement: public def value (sign : String) (components : Components) : Int

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.canonicalComponents
items.doc:
Canonical maximized components for a duration value split into days, hours, minutes,
seconds, and milliseconds. All five fields are present, including zero-valued fields.
items.statement:
public def canonicalComponents (days hours minutes seconds ms : Nat) :
    Components

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.canonicalBody
items.doc:
Canonical maximized duration body: `days d`, `hours h`, `minutes m`, `seconds s`,
and `milliseconds ms`, printed largest-to-smallest.
items.statement: public def canonicalBody (days hours minutes seconds ms : Nat) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.IsWfBody
items.doc:
A duration body string is well-formed iff it equals `components.asString` for some
`Components` that is nonempty and has valid quantities.
items.statement: public def IsWfBody (body : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.DurationProduction
items.doc: The grammar production witnessed by an optional sign and a nonempty component record.
items.statement: public def DurationProduction (str sign : String) (components : Components) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.IsWfDuration
items.doc: A duration string is well-formed iff it has a valid grammar production.
items.statement: public def IsWfDuration (str : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.IsDurationValue
items.doc: `v` is the value assigned to a valid duration production.
items.statement: public def IsDurationValue (str : String) (v : Int) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.normalize
items.doc:
Canonical-form normalizer: parse the string and re-serialize.
Returns `none` for malformed or out-of-range inputs.
items.statement: public def normalize (str : String) : Option String

modules.doc:
============================================================================================
# Duration parser lemmas

Duration quantity tokens are the `Digit⁺` strings characterized by `IsDigits`; the
`IsDigits.ne_empty` / `IsDigits.toNat?'_isSome` / `IsDigits.all_isDigit` projections (in
`Cedar.Thm.Data.String`) recover the facts these proofs consume.
============================================================================================

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.duration?_eq_none_iff_overflow
items.doc: `duration?` fails exactly when the value lies outside the Int64 range.
items.statement:
theorem duration?_eq_none_iff_overflow (value : Int) :
    duration? value = none ↔ value < Int64.MIN ∨ value > Int64.MAX

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.duration_body_front_ne_dash
items.statement:
theorem duration_body_front_ne_dash (body : String)
    (h : IsWfBody body) :
    body.front ≠ '-'

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.wf_of_parseDuration?_eq_some
items.doc:
A successful `parseDuration?` call implies the input body is well-formed.
Used to prove that `parseDuration?_none_of_not_wf` is the right converse.
items.statement:
theorem wf_of_parseDuration?_eq_some (isNeg : Bool) (body : String) (d : Duration)
    (h : parseDuration? isNeg body = some d) :
    IsWfBody body

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parseDuration?_eq_duration?_of_wf
items.doc:
On a well-formed duration body, `parseDuration?` agrees with `duration?` applied to the
computed signed millisecond value. This is the key bridge between the parser and the
arithmetic semantics.
items.statement:
theorem parseDuration?_eq_duration?_of_wf (isNegative : Bool) (body : String)
    (h : IsWfBody body) :
    parseDuration? isNegative body = duration? (computeSignedBodyValueD isNegative body)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parseDuration?_none_of_not_wf
items.doc: `parseDuration?` always returns `none` on a body string that is not well-formed.
items.statement:
theorem parseDuration?_none_of_not_wf (isNegative : Bool) (body : String)
    (h : ¬ IsWfBody body) :
    parseDuration? isNegative body = none

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parseDuration?_eq_none_iff_overflow_of_wf
items.doc:
On a well-formed body, `parseDuration?` fails if and only if the computed value overflows Int64.
Phrased in terms of the total `computeSignedBodyValueD`, which coincides with
`computeSignedBodyValue`'s payload on well-formed input.
items.statement:
theorem parseDuration?_eq_none_iff_overflow_of_wf (isNegative : Bool) (body : String)
    (h : IsWfBody body) :
    parseDuration? isNegative body = none ↔
      computeSignedBodyValueD isNegative body < Int64.MIN ∨
        computeSignedBodyValueD isNegative body > Int64.MAX

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parseDuration?_eq_none_iff
items.doc:
`parseDuration?` fails if and only if the body is not well-formed, or the computed value
overflows Int64. Combines `parseDuration?_none_of_not_wf` and
`parseDuration?_eq_none_iff_overflow_of_wf` into a single biconditional.
items.statement:
theorem parseDuration?_eq_none_iff (isNegative : Bool) (body : String) :
    parseDuration? isNegative body = none ↔
      ¬ IsWfBody body ∨
        (computeSignedBodyValueD isNegative body < Int64.MIN ∨
          computeSignedBodyValueD isNegative body > Int64.MAX)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.wf_str_iff_signed_body
items.doc:
`IsWfDuration` on a full duration string is equivalent to `IsWfBody` on its body
(the part after stripping any leading `-`). This bridges the string-level and body-level
well-formedness predicates.
items.statement:
theorem wf_str_iff_signed_body (str : String) :
    IsWfDuration str ↔
      let (_, body) := isNegativeDuration str
      IsWfBody body

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.duration?_some_toInt
items.statement:
theorem duration?_some_toInt (value : Int) (d : Duration)
    (h : duration? value = some d) :
    d.val.toInt = value

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.Int64.sub?_add?_inverse
items.statement:
theorem Int64.sub?_add?_inverse (a b c : Int64)
    (h : Int64.add? a b = some c) :
    Int64.sub? c a = some b

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.duration?_of_val_toInt
items.statement:
theorem duration?_of_val_toInt (d : Duration) :
    duration? d.val.toInt = some d

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.canonicalDurationBody_wf
items.statement:
theorem canonicalDurationBody_wf (days hours minutes seconds ms : Nat) :
    IsWfBody (canonicalBody days hours minutes seconds ms)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.isNegativeDuration_neg_body
items.statement:
theorem isNegativeDuration_neg_body (body : String) :
    isNegativeDuration ("-" ++ body) = (true, body)
