items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.isNegativeDuration_canonical_body
items.statement:
theorem isNegativeDuration_canonical_body (body : String) (hfront : body.front ≠ '-') :
    isNegativeDuration body = (false, body)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.parse_eq_duration?_of_isDurationValue
items.doc:
On a rendering to which the grammar assigns `v`, `Duration.parse` reaches the range check with
exactly `v`. Thus acceptance is decided by `duration?` alone.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.isDurationValue_unique
items.doc:
The declarative value relation is single-valued: a duration string denotes at most one
integer, including when that integer lies outside the parser's `Int64` range.
items.statement:
public theorem isDurationValue_unique {str : String} {v₁ v₂ : Int}
    (h₁ : IsDurationValue str v₁) (h₂ : IsDurationValue str v₂) : v₁ = v₂

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.canonicalDurationBody_value
items.statement:
theorem canonicalDurationBody_value (days hours minutes seconds ms : Nat) :
    computeBodyValue (canonicalBody days hours minutes seconds ms) =
      (days : Int) * MILLISECONDS_PER_DAY +
      (hours : Int) * MILLISECONDS_PER_HOUR +
      (minutes : Int) * MILLISECONDS_PER_MINUTE +
      (seconds : Int) * MILLISECONDS_PER_SECOND +
      (ms : Int)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.Duration.durationParts_value_int
items.statement:
theorem durationParts_value_int (n : Nat) :
    (↑(n / MILLISECONDS_PER_DAY.toNat) : Int) * MILLISECONDS_PER_DAY +
        (↑(n % MILLISECONDS_PER_DAY.toNat / MILLISECONDS_PER_HOUR.toNat) : Int) *
          MILLISECONDS_PER_HOUR +
      (↑(n % MILLISECONDS_PER_DAY.toNat % MILLISECONDS_PER_HOUR.toNat /
          MILLISECONDS_PER_MINUTE.toNat) : Int) *
        MILLISECONDS_PER_MINUTE +
    (↑(n % MILLISECONDS_PER_DAY.toNat % MILLISECONDS_PER_HOUR.toNat %
        MILLISECONDS_PER_MINUTE.toNat / MILLISECONDS_PER_SECOND.toNat) : Int) *
      MILLISECONDS_PER_SECOND +
    (↑(n % MILLISECONDS_PER_DAY.toNat % MILLISECONDS_PER_HOUR.toNat %
        MILLISECONDS_PER_MINUTE.toNat % MILLISECONDS_PER_SECOND.toNat) : Int) =
      n

modules.title: IPAddr parser correctness
modules.doc:
`parse_sound`, `parse_complete`, and `parse_eq_none_iff` characterize exactly when
`Cedar.Spec.Ext.IPAddr.ip` (a.k.a. `ip`) succeeds, in terms of the grammar-level `IsWfIPNet`
predicate and declarative `IsIPNetValue` relation. Its two branches use `v4Value` and `v6Value` to
give the denotation of the same components that witness the input rendering. The parser-independent
bridge lemmas they build on live in `Cedar.Thm.Ext.IPAddr.Lemmas`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.wf_iff_exists_value
items.doc: Well-formed IP-net syntax is exactly syntax to which the grammar assigns some `IPNet`.
items.statement:
public theorem wf_iff_exists_value {str : String} :
    IsWfIPNet str ↔ ∃ net, IsIPNetValue str net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_sound
items.doc:
Soundness of `IPAddr.ip`: if parsing succeeds, the declarative grammar relation assigns the
input exactly the returned `IPNet`.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_sound (str : String) (net : IPNet) (h : IPAddr.ip str = some net) :
    IsIPNetValue str net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_complete_v4
items.doc: Completeness for the V4 form: a well-formed V4 string parses to its `v4Value`.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_complete_v4 {v : V4Components} {pre : Option String}
    (hsyn : v.syntaxWf) (hcon : v.constraintsWf)
    (hpre : IsWfOptionalPrefix 2 (ADDR_SIZE V4_WIDTH) pre) :
    IPAddr.ip (v.asString ++ (match pre with | none => "" | some p => "/" ++ p))
      = some (v4Value v pre)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_complete_v6
items.doc: Completeness for the V6 form: a well-formed V6 string parses to its `v6Value`.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_complete_v6 {v : V6Components} {pre : Option String}
    (hsyn : v.syntaxWf)
    (hpre : IsWfOptionalPrefix 3 (ADDR_SIZE V6_WIDTH) pre) :
    IPAddr.ip (v.asString ++ (match pre with | none => "" | some p => "/" ++ p))
      = some (v6Value v pre)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_complete
items.doc:
Completeness of `IPAddr.ip`: if the grammar assigns `str` the value `net`, parsing returns that
exact `IPNet`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_eq_some_iff_isIPNetValue
items.doc:
Exact parser characterization: parsing succeeds with `net` precisely when the declarative
grammar relation assigns the input that `IPNet`.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_eq_some_iff_isIPNetValue (str : String) (net : IPNet) :
    IPAddr.ip str = some net ↔ IsIPNetValue str net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.isIPNetValue_unique
items.doc:
The relational value specification is single-valued: an IP-net string denotes at most one
`IPNet`.
items.statement:
public theorem isIPNetValue_unique {str : String} {net₁ net₂ : IPNet}
    (h₁ : IsIPNetValue str net₁) (h₂ : IsIPNetValue str net₂) : net₁ = net₂

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_eq_none_iff
items.doc:
Failure characterization: `IPAddr.ip` rejects exactly the strings that are not well-formed
IP-nets. (There is no overflow condition — the grammar's field bounds already exclude
out-of-range values.)
items.statement:
public theorem parse_eq_none_iff (str : String) :
    IPAddr.ip str = none ↔ ¬ IsWfIPNet str

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_toString_roundtrip
items.doc:
`parse ∘ toString` roundtrip: parsing the canonical representation recovers the original
IP-net.
items.statement:
public theorem parse_toString_roundtrip (net : IPNet) :
    IPAddr.ip (toString net) = some net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.toString_injective
items.doc: `toString` is injective: distinct IP-nets produce distinct canonical strings.
items.statement:
public theorem toString_injective (net net' : IPNet) (h : toString net = toString net') :
    net = net'

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq
items.doc: Equal normal form iff equal value: normalization decides IP-net equality.
items.statement:
public theorem normalize_eq_iff_parse_eq (str str' : String) :
    normalize str = normalize str' ↔ IPAddr.ip str = IPAddr.ip str'

modules.title: IPAddr grammar: definitions
modules.doc:
This file contains only the grammar-level definitions: the well-formedness predicates, component
value functions, and relational value specification. `IsWfIPNet` states the syntax,
`v4Value`/`v6Value` give the denotation of identified components, and `IsIPNetValue str net`
combines those same witnesses to say that `str` denotes `net`. The lemmas connecting these
definitions to `IPAddr.parse` live in `Cedar.Thm.Ext.IPAddr.Lemmas`.

The accepted syntax (transcribed from the spec parser) is, informally:

```
IPNet    ::= V4Net | V6Net          -- V4 tried first; a string is V6 only if it is not V4
V4Net    ::= V4Addr ['/' V4Prefix]
V4Addr   ::= NumV4 '.' NumV4 '.' NumV4 '.' NumV4
NumV4    ::= Digit{1,3}             -- no leading zeros unless the group is exactly "0"; value ≤ 255
V4Prefix ::= Digit{1,2}            -- no leading zeros unless exactly "0"; value ≤ 32

V6Net    ::= V6Addr ['/' V6Prefix]
V6Addr   ::= a `::`-compressed sequence of hextets that expands to exactly 8 groups
NumV6    ::= HexDigit{1,4}          -- value ≤ 0xffff (automatic from ≤ 4 hex digits)
V6Prefix ::= Digit{1,3}            -- no leading zeros unless exactly "0"; value ≤ 128
```

The `::` compression may appear at most once and denotes a run of zero hextets that pads the total
to 8 groups.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsCanonicalNat
items.doc:
A `Digit⁺` string that additionally forbids a leading zero unless it is exactly `"0"` — the
"no leading zeros" rule the spec parser enforces on every numeric group and prefix
(`str.startsWith "0" → str = "0"`).
items.statement: public def IsCanonicalNat (s : String) : Prop

items.note:
## IPv4 grammar

`V4Addr` is four dot-separated groups, each a canonical 1–3 digit number `≤ 255`; the optional
prefix is a canonical 1–2 digit number `≤ 32`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V4Components
items.doc: The grammar's `V4Addr ::= NumV4 '.' NumV4 '.' NumV4 '.' NumV4`: four decimal groups.
items.statement:
public structure V4Components where
  g₀ : String
  g₁ : String
  g₂ : String
  g₃ : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V4Components.syntaxWf
items.doc: Each group is a canonical number of at most 3 digits.
items.statement: public def V4Components.syntaxWf (v : V4Components) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V4Components.constraintsWf
items.doc: Each group's value is at most `255` (`0xff`).
items.statement: public def V4Components.constraintsWf (v : V4Components) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V4Components.asString
items.doc: Render a `V4Addr` as `g₀ '.' g₁ '.' g₂ '.' g₃`.
items.statement: public def V4Components.asString (v : V4Components) : String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V4Components.toAddr
items.doc: The `IPv4Addr` value of well-formed V4 groups.
items.statement: public def V4Components.toAddr (v : V4Components) : IPv4Addr

items.note:
## IPv6 grammar

`V6Addr` is a `::`-compressed sequence of hextets. Rather than model the compression syntactically
here, a `V6Components` record holds the eight expanded hextets together with the *rendering* (the
concrete `::`-form string), and well-formedness is phrased existentially over that rendering (as in
the duration/datetime grammars). Each hextet is a 1–4 character hex-digit string.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsHexGroup
items.doc:
A `Digit⁺`-style predicate for hex groups: a non-empty string all of whose characters are hex
digits, of length at most 4.
items.statement: public def IsHexGroup (s : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.hexValue
items.doc: Numeric value of a hex group (`Σ digit · 16ⁱ`), matching the spec parser's `foldl`.
items.statement: public def hexValue (s : String) : Nat

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V6Components
items.doc:
A V6 address, as the spec parser accepts it: either a full list of hextets with no `::`
compression, or a `::`-compressed form with a left and right list of hextets and an implicit
run of zero hextets between them. This mirrors `parseSegsV6`'s `splitOn "::"`:
- `full gs`     ↔ the string has no `::`; `gs` is the `':'`-separated hextet list;
- `gap l r`     ↔ the string is `l₀:…:lₘ '::' r₀:…:rₙ`; the gap expands to `8 − (|l|+|r|)`
  zero hextets.
items.statement:
public inductive V6Components where
  | full (gs : List String)
  | gap  (l r : List String)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V6Components.expand
items.doc:
The eight expanded hextet strings a `V6Components` denotes: the full list itself, or the two
sides padded with the appropriate number of `"0"` hextets between them.
items.statement: public def V6Components.expand : V6Components → List String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V6Components.syntaxWf
items.statement: public def V6Components.syntaxWf : V6Components → Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V6Components.asString
items.doc:
Render a V6 address to its concrete string: hextets joined by `':'`, with `"::"` at the gap.
(`intercalate ":"` matches the parser's `splitToList (· = ':')` / `splitOn "::"` inverse.)
items.statement: public def V6Components.asString : V6Components → String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V6Components.toAddr
items.doc:
The `IPv6Addr` value: the eight expanded hextets' hex values. Well-formedness guarantees
`expand` has length 8; on other lengths this defaults the missing groups to `0`.
items.statement: public def V6Components.toAddr (v : V6Components) : IPv6Addr

items.note:
## Prefix grammar

An optional CIDR suffix `'/' Prefix`, where `Prefix` is a canonical decimal number bounded by the
address width (`≤ 32` for V4, `≤ 128` for V6). Absence of the suffix denotes the full-width prefix
(`ADDR_SIZE`).

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsWfOptionalPrefix
items.doc:
The optional prefix, with its digit-count and value bounds `(digits, size)`
(`(2, 32)` for V4, `(3, 128)` for V6). `none` is the implicit full-width prefix.
items.statement: public def IsWfOptionalPrefix (digits size : Nat) : Option String → Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.prefixValue
items.doc: The `IPNetPrefix` value of an optional prefix string: `none` maps to the full-width prefix.
items.statement: public def prefixValue (w : Nat) : Option String → IPNetPrefix w

items.note:
## Top-level well-formedness

An IP-net string is well-formed when it is either a well-formed V4 rendering or a well-formed V6
rendering (with V4 taking precedence, mirroring the parser's `if ipv4.isSome then … else …`). Both
are phrased existentially over the components' `asString` rendering (as in the duration/datetime
grammars), baking the separators, group count, and `::`-compression rules into the witness.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V4Production
items.doc: The IPv4 grammar production witnessed by address components and an optional CIDR prefix.
items.statement: public def V4Production (str : String) (v : V4Components) (pre : Option String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsWfV4
items.doc: A well-formed IPv4-net string has a valid IPv4 grammar production.
items.statement: public def IsWfV4 (str : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.V6Production
items.doc: The IPv6 grammar production witnessed by address components and an optional CIDR prefix.
items.statement: public def V6Production (str : String) (v : V6Components) (pre : Option String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsWfV6
items.doc: A well-formed IPv6-net string has a valid IPv6 grammar production.
items.statement: public def IsWfV6 (str : String) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsWfIPNet
items.doc:
A string is a well-formed IP-net iff it is a well-formed V4 or V6 net. Because the parser tries
V4 first and only falls through to V6 when V4 fails, and the two grammars are disjoint on their
accepted strings, this disjunction faithfully characterizes acceptance.
items.statement: public def IsWfIPNet (str : String) : Prop

items.note:
## Value relation

The component value functions are independent of the parser. The relational definitions below
tie those values to the same witnesses used by the syntax predicates, so no second string decoder
is needed.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.v4Value
items.doc: The `IPNet` value of a well-formed V4 string's components.
items.statement: public def v4Value (v : V4Components) (pre : Option String) : IPNet

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.v6Value
items.doc: The `IPNet` value of a well-formed V6 string's components.
items.statement: public def v6Value (v : V6Components) (pre : Option String) : IPNet

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsV4Value
items.doc: `net` is the value of a well-formed IPv4-net rendering.
items.statement: public def IsV4Value (str : String) (net : IPNet) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsV6Value
items.doc: `net` is the value of a well-formed IPv6-net rendering.
items.statement: public def IsV6Value (str : String) (net : IPNet) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.IsIPNetValue
items.doc: `net` is the value of the IP-net literal `str`, through either the V4 or V6 production.
items.statement: public def IsIPNetValue (str : String) (net : IPNet) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.normalize
items.doc:
Canonical-form normalizer: parse the string and re-serialize.
Returns `none` for malformed inputs.
items.statement: public def normalize (str : String) : Option String

modules.title: IPAddr grammar bridge lemmas
modules.doc:
These lemmas connect the parser-independent grammar definitions in
`Cedar.Thm.Ext.IPAddr.Grammar` (`IsWfIPNet`, `IsIPNetValue`, and the component value functions) to
the actual `Cedar.Spec.Ext.IPAddr.parse`. They culminate in the per-form parse characterizations
the aggregator `parse_sound`/`parse_complete` build on.

The parser structure (from `Cedar.Spec.Ext.IPAddr`) is:
- `parse str = if (parseIPv4Net str).isSome then parseIPv4Net str else parseIPv6Net str`;
- `parseIPv4Net` splits on `'/'`, parses four `parseNumV4` groups (split on `'.'`) and an optional
  `parsePrefixNat` prefix;
- `parseIPv6Net` splits on `'/'`, parses the address via `parseSegsV6` (which handles `::` via
  `splitOn "::"` and pads to eight hextets) and an optional `parsePrefixNat` prefix.

Each numeric primitive (`parseNumV4`, `parseNumV6`, `parsePrefixNat`) enforces the length /
leading-zero / range side conditions that the grammar predicates transcribe.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseNumV4_eq_some
items.doc:
`parseNumV4` accepts exactly the canonical ≤ 3-digit groups with value ≤ 255, returning
`natOf`.
items.statement:
theorem parseNumV4_eq_some {s : String} (hwf : IsCanonicalNat s ∧ s.length ≤ 3)
    (hcon : natOf s ≤ 255) :
    parseNumV4 s = some (BitVec.ofNat 8 (natOf s))

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseNumV4_isSome_wf
items.doc:
Conversely, if `parseNumV4` accepts `s`, it is a canonical ≤ 3-digit group whose value is at
most 255.
items.statement:
theorem parseNumV4_isSome_wf {s : String} (h : (parseNumV4 s).isSome) :
    (IsCanonicalNat s ∧ s.length ≤ 3) ∧ natOf s ≤ 255

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseNumV6_eq_some
items.statement:
theorem parseNumV6_eq_some {s : String} (hwf : IsHexGroup s) :
    parseNumV6 s = some (BitVec.ofNat 16 (hexValue s))

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseNumV6_isSome_wf
items.doc: Conversely, if `parseNumV6` accepts `s` it is a well-formed hex group.
items.statement: theorem parseNumV6_isSome_wf {s : String} (h : (parseNumV6 s).isSome) : IsHexGroup s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parsePrefixNat_eq_some
items.doc:
`parsePrefixNat` accepts exactly the canonical numbers with at most `digits` digits and value
at most `size`.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseSegsV4_asString
items.doc: `parseSegsV4` inverts `V4Components.asString` on well-formed, in-range V4 groups.
items.statement:
theorem parseSegsV4_asString {v : V4Components} (hsyn : v.syntaxWf) (hcon : v.constraintsWf) :
    parseSegsV4 v.asString = some v.toAddr

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseIPv4Net_eq_some
items.doc: `parseIPv4Net` succeeds on a well-formed V4 string, yielding `v4Value`.
items.statement:
theorem parseIPv4Net_eq_some {v : V4Components} {pre : Option String}
    (hsyn : v.syntaxWf) (hcon : v.constraintsWf)
    (hpre : IsWfOptionalPrefix 2 (ADDR_SIZE V4_WIDTH) pre) :
    parseIPv4Net (v.asString ++ (match pre with | none => "" | some p => "/" ++ p))
      = some (v4Value v pre)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseIPv4Net_isSome_wf
items.doc:
Soundness for V4: a successful `parseIPv4Net` means the string is a well-formed V4 rendering
whose value is the returned net.
items.statement:
theorem parseIPv4Net_isSome_wf {str : String} {net : IPNet} (h : parseIPv4Net str = some net) :
    IsV4Value str net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.splitDoubleColonModel
items.doc: The proof-layer model of `String.splitOn "::"`.
items.statement: public def splitDoubleColonModel (str : String) : List String

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.splitOn_doubleColon_eq
items.doc: `String.splitOn "::"` agrees with the proof-layer character-list model on every string.
items.statement:
public theorem splitOn_doubleColon_eq (s : String) :
    s.splitOn "::" = splitDoubleColonModel s

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseSegsV6_asString
items.doc:
`parseSegsV6` inverts `V6Components.asString` on a syntactically well-formed V6 address:
`full gs` (no `::`) splits to exactly 8 hextets; `gap l r` splits on `::` into two sides that
`parseSegsV6` pads to 8.
items.statement:
theorem parseSegsV6_asString {v : V6Components} (hsyn : v.syntaxWf) :
    parseSegsV6 v.asString = some v.toAddr

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseIPv6Net_eq_some
items.doc: `parseIPv6Net` succeeds on a well-formed V6 string, yielding `v6Value`.
items.statement:
theorem parseIPv6Net_eq_some {v : V6Components} {pre : Option String}
    (hsyn : v.syntaxWf)
    (hpre : IsWfOptionalPrefix 3 (ADDR_SIZE V6_WIDTH) pre) :
    parseIPv6Net (v.asString ++ (match pre with | none => "" | some p => "/" ++ p))
      = some (v6Value v pre)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseIPv6Net_isSome_wf
items.doc: Soundness for V6: a successful `parseIPv6Net` means the string is a well-formed V6 rendering.
items.statement:
theorem parseIPv6Net_isSome_wf {str : String} {net : IPNet} (h : parseIPv6Net str = some net) :
    IsV6Value str net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parseIPv4Net_none_of_isWfV6
items.doc:
The V4 and V6 accepted-string sets are disjoint: no string parses as both. In particular a
well-formed V6 string is not accepted by `parseIPv4Net` (needed for the `parse`'s V4-first
fall-through to reach V6).
items.statement:
theorem parseIPv4Net_none_of_isWfV6 {str : String} (h : IsWfV6 str) :
    parseIPv4Net str = none

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.isWfV4_iff_exists_value
items.doc: Well-formed IPv4 syntax is exactly syntax to which the grammar assigns some V4 value.
items.statement:
public theorem isWfV4_iff_exists_value {str : String} :
    IsWfV4 str ↔ ∃ net, IsV4Value str net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.isWfV6_iff_exists_value
items.doc: Well-formed IPv6 syntax is exactly syntax to which the grammar assigns some V6 value.
items.statement:
public theorem isWfV6_iff_exists_value {str : String} :
    IsWfV6 str ↔ ∃ net, IsV6Value str net

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_toString_v4
items.statement:
theorem parse_toString_v4 (addr : IPv4Addr) (pre : IPv4Prefix) :
    IPAddr.ip (toString (IPNet.V4 ⟨addr, pre⟩)) = some (IPNet.V4 ⟨addr, pre⟩)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.IPAddr.parse_toString_v6
items.statement:
theorem parse_toString_v6 (addr : IPv6Addr) (pre : IPv6Prefix) :
    IPAddr.ip (toString (IPNet.V6 ⟨addr, pre⟩)) = some (IPNet.V6 ⟨addr, pre⟩)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_preserves_definitions
items.doc:
Every entity or action definition from either input appears unchanged in the
result.
items.statement:
theorem linker_preserves_definitions
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t) :
    (∀ ety entry, p.ets.find? ety = some (.defined entry) →
      t.ets.find? ety = some (.defined entry)) ∧
    (∀ ety entry, c.ets.find? ety = some (.defined entry) →
      t.ets.find? ety = some (.defined entry)) ∧
    (∀ uid entry, p.acts.find? uid = some (.defined entry) →
      t.acts.find? uid = some (.defined entry)) ∧
    (∀ uid entry, c.acts.find? uid = some (.defined entry) →
      t.acts.find? uid = some (.defined entry))

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_preserves_entity_declarations
items.doc: The result declares exactly the entity types declared by either input.
items.statement:
theorem linker_preserves_entity_declarations
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t)
    (ety : EntityType) :
    t.ets.contains ety ↔ p.ets.contains ety ∨ c.ets.contains ety

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_preserves_action_declarations
items.doc: The result declares exactly the action UIDs declared by either input.
items.statement:
theorem linker_preserves_action_declarations
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t)
    (uid : EntityUID) :
    t.acts.contains uid ↔ p.acts.contains uid ∨ c.acts.contains uid

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_preserves_action_ancestors
items.doc: Every action from either input keeps its ancestors in the result.
items.statement:
theorem linker_preserves_action_ancestors
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t) :
    (∀ uid entry, p.acts.find? uid = some entry →
      ∃ entry', t.acts.find? uid = some entry' ∧ entry'.ancestors = entry.ancestors) ∧
    (∀ uid entry, c.acts.find? uid = some entry →
      ∃ entry', t.acts.find? uid = some entry' ∧ entry'.ancestors = entry.ancestors)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_preserves_standard_entities
items.doc:
Every standard or external entity type from either input is standard or
external in the result. In particular, an external entity type never links to
an enumerated entity type.
items.statement:
theorem linker_preserves_standard_entities
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t) :
    (∀ ety entry, p.ets.find? ety = some entry → entry.isStandard = true →
      ∃ entry', t.ets.find? ety = some entry' ∧ entry'.isStandard = true) ∧
    (∀ ety entry, c.ets.find? ety = some entry → entry.isStandard = true →
      ∃ entry', t.ets.find? ety = some entry' ∧ entry'.isStandard = true)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_action_types_not_entity_types
items.doc: The result never declares the entity type of an action as an entity type.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_definitions_come_from_inputs
items.doc: Every entity definition of the result is a definition from either input.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_actions_come_from_inputs
items.doc: Every action entry of the result is that action's entry in either input.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_entity_ancestors
items.doc:
An entity type's ancestors in the result are exactly the entity types reachable
from it through the ancestors listed by either input.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_keeps_declarations
items.doc: The result keeps every declaration of either input.
items.statement:
theorem linker_keeps_declarations
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t) :
    DeclarationsKept p t ∧ DeclarationsKept c t

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_result_kept
items.doc:
A partial schema with closed ancestors that keeps the declarations of both
inputs keeps the declarations of the result.
items.statement:
theorem linker_result_kept
    {p c t u : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t)
    (hclosed : u.ets.AncestorsClosed)
    (hpu : DeclarationsKept p u)
    (hcu : DeclarationsKept c u) :
    DeclarationsKept t u

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_definitions_disjoint
items.doc: No entity type or action is defined by both inputs.
items.statement:
theorem linker_definitions_disjoint
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t) :
    (∀ ety e₁ e₂, p.ets.find? ety = some (.defined e₁) →
      c.ets.find? ety ≠ some (.defined e₂)) ∧
    (∀ uid e₁ e₂, p.acts.find? uid = some (.defined e₁) →
      c.acts.find? uid ≠ some (.defined e₂))

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_completion
items.doc:
A well-formed partial schema links into the schema that completes it with
attributes `attrs`, when these are well-formed and lifted.
items.statement:
theorem linker_completion
    {p : PartialSchema}
    {attrs : RecordType}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hwf : ∀ env, (CedarType.record attrs).WellFormed env)
    (hlifted : (CedarType.record attrs).IsLifted) :
    ∃ c, c.WellFormed ∧ link p c = .ok (p.completeWith attrs)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_completion_validationView
items.doc: A well-formed partial schema links into its validation view.
items.statement:
theorem linker_completion_validationView
    {p : PartialSchema}
    (hp : p.WellFormed) :
    ∃ c, c.WellFormed ∧ link p c = .ok p.validationView

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_commutativity
items.doc: Changing the input order does not change a successful link.
items.statement:
theorem linker_commutativity
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hc : c.WellFormed)
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t) :
    link c p = .ok t

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_commutativity_error
items.doc: Changing the input order does not change whether linking fails.
items.statement:
theorem linker_commutativity_error
    {p c : PartialSchema}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hc : c.WellFormed) :
    (∃ err, link p c = .error err) ↔
    (∃ err, link c p = .error err)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_preserves_well_formedness
items.doc: Linking well-formed partial schemas produces a well-formed partial schema.
items.statement:
theorem linker_preserves_well_formedness
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hc : c.WellFormed)
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t) :
    t.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_completed_schema_well_formed
items.doc: A complete link passes the existing schema well-formedness check.
items.statement:
theorem linker_completed_schema_well_formed
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    {schema : Schema}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hc : c.WellFormed)
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t)
    (hcomplete : t.asSchema? = some schema) :
    schema.validateWellFormed = .ok ()

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_associativity
items.doc: Changing the grouping does not change a successful link.
items.statement:
theorem linker_associativity
    {p c d t₁ t : PartialSchema}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hc : c.WellFormed)
    (hd : d.WellFormed)
    (hpc : link p c = .ok t₁)
    (hpcd : link t₁ d = .ok t) :
    ∃ t₂, link c d = .ok t₂ ∧ link p t₂ = .ok t

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_associativity_error
items.doc: Changing the grouping does not change whether linking fails.
items.statement:
theorem linker_associativity_error
    {p c d : PartialSchema}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hc : c.WellFormed)
    (hd : d.WellFormed) :
    (∃ err, (do
      let t₁ ← link p c
      link t₁ d) = .error err) ↔
    (∃ err, (do
      let t₂ ← link c d
      link p t₂) = .error err)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.linker_completion_exists
items.doc: Every well-formed partial schema has a complete linking extension.
items.statement:
theorem linker_completion_exists
    {p : PartialSchema}
    (hp : p.WellFormed) :
    ∃ c t schema,
      c.WellFormed ∧
      link p c = .ok t ∧
      t.asSchema? = some schema

items.name: Cedar.Validation.stable_entity_ancestor
items.doc: A defined entity keeps its closed ancestor set after linking.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchema.AncestorsClosed
items.doc:
Every ancestor set is transitively closed.
TODO: it is a bit suprising how this does not already exists.
Maybe define it for complete schema and see if it is useful for proving some nice facts about schema.
items.statement: def PartialEntitySchema.AncestorsClosed (schema : PartialEntitySchema) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchema.ExternalParentsStandard
items.doc:
No external entity type declaration lists an enum entity type as a parent: a
definition of the external must list the parent, so only a declaration of the
parent, which an enum definition cannot be, can supply it.
items.statement: def PartialEntitySchema.ExternalParentsStandard (schema : PartialEntitySchema) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed
items.doc:
A partial schema is well-formed when its definitions satisfy the existing
schema conditions, its externals satisfy those conditions using only their
known ancestors, and no external lists an enum entity type as a parent.
items.statement: def PartialSchema.WellFormed (schema : PartialSchema) : Prop

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.wfEnv
items.doc:
The environment in which `PartialSchema.WellFormed` checks a partial schema and
`PartialSchema.validateEntities` validates entities: the validation view with the
default request type.
items.statement: def PartialSchema.wfEnv (schema : PartialSchema) : TypeEnv

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept
items.doc:
`t` keeps every declaration of `s`: its entity types with their definitions,
standard entity types, and listed ancestors, and its actions with their
ancestors and definitions.
items.statement:
structure DeclarationsKept (s t : PartialSchema) : Prop where
  entities : ∀ ety, s.ets.contains ety → t.ets.contains ety
  definitions : ∀ ety entry, s.ets.find? ety = some (.defined entry) →
    t.ets.find? ety = some (.defined entry)
  standard : ∀ ety entry, s.ets.find? ety = some entry → entry.isStandard = true →
    ∃ entry', t.ets.find? ety = some entry' ∧ entry'.isStandard = true
  ancestors : ∀ ety entry ancestor, s.ets.find? ety = some entry → ancestor ∈ entry.ancestors →
    ∃ entry', t.ets.find? ety = some entry' ∧ ancestor ∈ entry'.ancestors
  actions : ∀ uid entry, s.acts.find? uid = some entry →
    ∃ entry', t.acts.find? uid = some entry' ∧ entry'.ancestors = entry.ancestors
  actionDefinitions : ∀ uid entry, s.acts.find? uid = some (.defined entry) →
    t.acts.find? uid = some (.defined entry)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.EntryKept
items.doc: `z` keeps the definition, the standard kind, and the ancestors of the entity entry `x`.
items.statement:
structure EntryKept (x z : PartialEntitySchemaEntry) : Prop where
  definition : ∀ entry, x = .defined entry → z = .defined entry
  standard : x.isStandard = true → z.isStandard = true
  ancestors : x.ancestors ⊆ z.ancestors

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchemaEntry.completeWith
items.doc:
The definition that completes an entity entry: its definition, or a standard
entity type with its ancestors, the attributes `attrs`, and no tags.
items.statement:
def PartialEntitySchemaEntry.completeWith (attrs : RecordType) :
    PartialEntitySchemaEntry → EntitySchemaEntry

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.completeWith
items.doc:
The schema that completes `p`: it defines each external entity type of `p` with
the attributes `attrs`, and each external action by its validation view.
items.statement: def PartialSchema.completeWith (p : PartialSchema) (attrs : RecordType) : Schema

items.name: Cedar.Validation.toPartialSchema_asSchema?
items.doc: Coercing a schema to a partial schema and back preserves it.
items.statement:
theorem toPartialSchema_asSchema? (schema : Schema) :
    (Schema.toPartialSchema schema).asSchema? = some schema

items.name: Cedar.Validation.toPartialSchema_validationView
items.doc: Coercing a schema to a partial schema preserves its validation view.
items.statement:
theorem toPartialSchema_validationView (schema : Schema) :
    (Schema.toPartialSchema schema).validationView = schema

items.name: Cedar.Validation.toPartialSchema_ets_find?
items.doc: Coercing a schema to a partial schema defines each of its entity types.
items.statement:
theorem toPartialSchema_ets_find? (schema : Schema) (ety : EntityType) :
    (Schema.toPartialSchema schema).ets.find? ety = (schema.ets.find? ety).map .defined

items.name: Cedar.Validation.toPartialSchema_acts_find?
items.doc: Coercing a schema to a partial schema defines each of its actions.
items.statement:
theorem toPartialSchema_acts_find? (schema : Schema) (uid : EntityUID) :
    (Schema.toPartialSchema schema).acts.find? uid = (schema.acts.find? uid).map .defined

items.name: Cedar.Validation.toPartialSchema_wfEnv
items.doc: A coerced schema is checked in the environment with its own maps.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.asSchema?_isSome_iff_isComplete
items.doc: A partial schema converts to a schema exactly when it is complete.
items.statement:
theorem asSchema?_isSome_iff_isComplete (schema : PartialSchema) :
    schema.asSchema?.isSome ↔ schema.isComplete

items.name: Cedar.Validation.validationView_find?_ets
items.doc: The entity validation view maps the entry found in the partial schema.
items.statement:
theorem validationView_find?_ets (schema : PartialSchema) (ety : EntityType) :
    schema.validationView.ets.find? ety =
      (schema.ets.find? ety).map PartialEntitySchemaEntry.validationView

items.name: Cedar.Validation.validationView_find?_acts
items.doc: The action validation view maps the entry found in the partial schema.
items.statement:
theorem validationView_find?_acts (schema : PartialSchema) (uid : EntityUID) :
    schema.validationView.acts.find? uid =
      (schema.acts.find? uid).map PartialActionSchemaEntry.validationView

items.name: Cedar.Validation.validationView_eq_of_asSchema?
items.doc: A completed partial schema agrees with its validation view.
items.statement:
theorem validationView_eq_of_asSchema?
    {ps : PartialSchema} {schema : Schema}
    (h : ps.asSchema? = some schema) :
    ps.validationView = schema

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialActionSchemaEntry.validationView_ancestors
items.doc: The validation view keeps an action's ancestors.
items.statement:
theorem PartialActionSchemaEntry.validationView_ancestors
    (entry : PartialActionSchemaEntry) :
    entry.validationView.ancestors = entry.ancestors

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchemaEntry.validationView_isStandard
items.doc: The validation view keeps whether an entity type is standard or external.
items.statement:
theorem PartialEntitySchemaEntry.validationView_isStandard
    (entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry) :
    entry.validationView.isStandard = entry.isStandard

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchemaEntry.validationView_isValidEntityEID
items.doc: A standard or external entity type accepts every entity id in the validation view.
items.statement:
theorem PartialEntitySchemaEntry.validationView_isValidEntityEID
    {entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry}
    (h : entry.isStandard = true)
    (eid : String) :
    entry.validationView.isValidEntityEID eid = true

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchemaEntry.withAncestors_isStandard
items.doc: Replacing ancestors keeps an entry standard or external.
items.statement:
theorem PartialEntitySchemaEntry.withAncestors_isStandard
    (entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry) (ancestors : Set EntityType) :
    (entry.withAncestors ancestors).isStandard = entry.isStandard

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.etsMap
items.doc: A well-formed partial schema has a well-formed entity map.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.etsMap
    {schema : PartialSchema} (h : schema.WellFormed) :
    schema.ets.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.actsMap
items.doc: A well-formed partial schema has a well-formed action map.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.actsMap
    {schema : PartialSchema} (h : schema.WellFormed) :
    schema.acts.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.wellFormed_iff
items.doc: `PartialSchema.WellFormed` checks the maps in `wfEnv`.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.wellFormed_iff {schema : PartialSchema} :
    schema.WellFormed ↔ schema.ets.AncestorsClosed ∧
      schema.ets.ExternalParentsStandard ∧
      schema.wfEnv.ets.WellFormed schema.wfEnv ∧ schema.wfEnv.acts.WellFormed schema.wfEnv

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.wfEnv_ets_find?
items.doc: Each entity entry of `wfEnv` is the view of an entry of the partial schema.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.wfEnv_acts_find?
items.doc: Each action entry of `wfEnv` is the view of an entry of the partial schema.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.wfEnv_ets_contains
items.doc: `wfEnv` declares the entity types of the partial schema.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.wfEnv_ets_contains (schema : PartialSchema) (ety : EntityType) :
    schema.wfEnv.ets.contains ety = schema.ets.contains ety

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.wfEnv_acts_contains
items.doc: `wfEnv` declares the actions of the partial schema.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.wfEnv_acts_contains (schema : PartialSchema) (uid : EntityUID) :
    schema.wfEnv.acts.contains uid = schema.acts.contains uid

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.entry
items.doc: In a well-formed partial schema, the view of each entity entry is well-formed.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.entry {schema : PartialSchema} {ety : EntityType}
    {entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry} (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind : schema.ets.find? ety = some entry) :
    entry.validationView.WellFormed schema.wfEnv

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.action
items.doc: In a well-formed partial schema, the view of each action is well-formed.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.action {schema : PartialSchema} {uid : EntityUID}
    {entry : PartialActionSchemaEntry} (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind : schema.acts.find? uid = some entry) :
    entry.validationView.WellFormed schema.wfEnv

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.external_parent_isStandard
items.doc: In a well-formed partial schema, no parent of an external entity type is an enum.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.external_parent_isStandard {schema : PartialSchema}
    {ety parent : EntityType} {parents : Set EntityType} (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind : schema.ets.find? ety = some (.external parents)) (hmem : parent ∈ parents) :
    ∃ entry, schema.ets.find? parent = some entry ∧ entry.isStandard

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.ancestor_declared
items.doc: In a well-formed partial schema, every ancestor of an entity type is declared.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.ancestor_declared {schema : PartialSchema}
    {ety ancestor : EntityType} {entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry} (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind : schema.ets.find? ety = some entry) (hmem : ancestor ∈ entry.ancestors) :
    ∃ entry', schema.ets.find? ancestor = some entry'

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.action_ancestor
items.doc: In a well-formed partial schema, every ancestor of an action is an action.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.action_ancestor {schema : PartialSchema}
    {uid ancestor : EntityUID} {entry : PartialActionSchemaEntry} (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind : schema.acts.find? uid = some entry) (hmem : ancestor ∈ entry.ancestors) :
    schema.acts.contains ancestor

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.acyclic
items.doc: A well-formed partial schema has no action among its own ancestors.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.acyclic {schema : PartialSchema} {uid : EntityUID}
    {entry : PartialActionSchemaEntry} (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind : schema.acts.find? uid = some entry) :
    uid ∉ entry.ancestors

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.transitive
items.doc: A well-formed partial schema has transitively closed action ancestors.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.transitive {schema : PartialSchema}
    {uid₁ uid₂ : EntityUID} {entry₁ entry₂ : PartialActionSchemaEntry}
    (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind₁ : schema.acts.find? uid₁ = some entry₁)
    (hfind₂ : schema.acts.find? uid₂ = some entry₂)
    (hmem : uid₂ ∈ entry₁.ancestors) :
    entry₂.ancestors ⊆ entry₁.ancestors

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.disjoint
items.doc: A well-formed partial schema declares no action type as an entity type.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.WellFormed.ancestors_wf
items.doc: In a well-formed partial schema, every entity entry has well-formed ancestors.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.WellFormed.ancestors_wf {schema : PartialSchema}
    {ety : EntityType} {entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry} (h : schema.WellFormed)
    (hfind : schema.ets.find? ety = some entry) :
    entry.ancestors.WellFormed

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchema.AncestorsClosed.reach
items.doc: With closed ancestors, every entity type reachable through listed ancestors is listed.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialActionSchemaEntry.external_validationView_wf
items.doc: An external action's view is well-formed when its ancestors are a well-formed set of actions.
items.statement:
theorem PartialActionSchemaEntry.external_validationView_wf {env : TypeEnv}
    {ancestors : Set EntityUID} (hwf : ancestors.WellFormed)
    (hactions : ∀ a ∈ ancestors, env.acts.contains a) :
    (PartialActionSchemaEntry.external ancestors).validationView.WellFormed env

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.acts_contains
items.doc: `t` declares every action of `s`.
items.statement:
theorem DeclarationsKept.acts_contains {s t : PartialSchema} (h : DeclarationsKept s t)
    {uid : EntityUID} (hs : s.acts.contains uid) :
    t.acts.contains uid

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.entityType_wf
items.doc: An entity type well-formed for `s` is well-formed for `t`.
items.statement:
theorem DeclarationsKept.entityType_wf {s t : PartialSchema} (h : DeclarationsKept s t)
    {ety : EntityType} (hwf : EntityType.WellFormed s.wfEnv ety) :
    EntityType.WellFormed t.wfEnv ety

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.cedarType_wf
items.doc: A type well-formed for `s` is well-formed for `t`.
items.statement:
theorem DeclarationsKept.cedarType_wf {s t : PartialSchema} (h : DeclarationsKept s t)
    {ty : CedarType} (hwf : CedarType.WellFormed s.wfEnv ty) :
    CedarType.WellFormed t.wfEnv ty

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.ancestor_declared
items.doc: An ancestor listed in a well-formed `s` is declared in `t`.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.definition_wf
items.doc: A definition of a well-formed `s` is well-formed in `t`.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.action_wf
items.doc: An action of a well-formed `s` is well-formed in `t`.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.transitive
items.doc:
In `t`, the ancestors of an ancestor of an action of a well-formed `s` are
ancestors of that action.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.trans
items.doc: Keeping declarations is transitive.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.entry
items.doc: The entry of `t` for an entity type of `s` keeps the entry of `s`.
items.statement:
theorem DeclarationsKept.entry {s t : PartialSchema} (h : DeclarationsKept s t)
    {ety : EntityType} {x z : PartialEntitySchemaEntry}
    (hx : s.ets.find? ety = some x) (hz : t.ets.find? ety = some z) :
    EntryKept x z

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.antisymm
items.doc: Well-formed partial schemas that keep each other's declarations are equal.
items.statement:
theorem DeclarationsKept.antisymm {s t : PartialSchema}
    (hs : s.WellFormed) (ht : t.WellFormed)
    (hst : DeclarationsKept s t) (hts : DeclarationsKept t s) :
    s = t

items.name: Cedar.Validation.DeclarationsKept.eq_toPartialSchema
items.doc: A partial schema with well-formed maps is a schema that it keeps and that keeps it.
items.statement:
theorem DeclarationsKept.eq_toPartialSchema {t : PartialSchema} {schema : Schema}
    (hets : t.ets.WellFormed) (hacts : t.acts.WellFormed)
    (hschema : (Schema.toPartialSchema schema).WellFormed)
    (hts : DeclarationsKept t schema) (hst : DeclarationsKept schema t) :
    t = schema

items.name: Cedar.Validation.completeWith_ets_find?
items.doc: Completing a partial schema completes each of its entity entries.
items.statement:
theorem completeWith_ets_find? (p : PartialSchema) (attrs : RecordType) (ety : EntityType) :
    (p.completeWith attrs).ets.find? ety = (p.ets.find? ety).map (·.completeWith attrs)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.completeWith_empty
items.doc: Completing with no attributes gives the validation view.
items.statement: theorem completeWith_empty (p : PartialSchema) : p.completeWith Map.empty = p.validationView

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchemaEntry.completeWith_ancestors
items.doc: Completing an entry keeps its ancestors.
items.statement:
theorem PartialEntitySchemaEntry.completeWith_ancestors (attrs : RecordType)
    (entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry) :
    (entry.completeWith attrs).ancestors = entry.ancestors

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialEntitySchemaEntry.completeWith_isStandard
items.doc: Completing an entry keeps whether it is standard or external.
items.statement:
theorem PartialEntitySchemaEntry.completeWith_isStandard (attrs : RecordType)
    (entry : PartialEntitySchemaEntry) :
    (entry.completeWith attrs).isStandard = entry.isStandard

items.name: Cedar.Validation.toPartialSchema_completeWith_ets_find?
items.doc: The partial schema of a completion defines each entity type of `p` by its completion.
items.statement:
theorem toPartialSchema_completeWith_ets_find? (p : PartialSchema) (attrs : RecordType)
    (ety : EntityType) :
    (Schema.toPartialSchema (p.completeWith attrs)).ets.find? ety =
      (p.ets.find? ety).map fun entry => .defined (entry.completeWith attrs)

items.name: Cedar.Validation.toPartialSchema_completeWith_acts_find?
items.doc: The partial schema of a completion defines each action of `p` by its validation view.
items.statement:
theorem toPartialSchema_completeWith_acts_find? (p : PartialSchema) (attrs : RecordType)
    (uid : EntityUID) :

items.name: Cedar.Validation.PartialSchema.validateEntities_ok_iff
items.doc:
Partial entity validation accepts a store exactly when no entity has an external
type and every entity is valid in `wfEnv`.
items.statement:
theorem PartialSchema.validateEntities_ok_iff {ps : PartialSchema} {entities : Entities} :
    ps.validateEntities entities = .ok () ↔
      ∀ uid data, (uid, data) ∈ entities.toList →
        (∀ ancestors, ps.ets.find? uid.ty ≠ some (.external ancestors)) ∧
        instanceOfSchema.instanceOfSchemaEntry ps.wfEnv uid data = .ok ()

items.name: Cedar.Validation.value_validation_soundness

environment of its validation view has a counterpart in the result's.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.entity_validation_completeness
items.doc:
Entities valid against every complete linking extension are valid against the
partial schema.

    {p : PartialSchema}
    {entities : Entities}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hvalid : ∀ c t,
      c.WellFormed →
      link p c = .ok t →
      t.asSchema?.isSome = true →
      t.validateEntities entities = .ok ()) :
    p.validateEntities entities = .ok ()

Requests valid against every complete linking extension are valid against the

items.doc: A complete partial schema validates requests exactly as the schema completing it.

items.name: Cedar.Validation.complete_entity_validation_agreement
items.doc:
At a complete link, partial entity validation implies complete validation after
adding the canonical entity for every action.
items.statement:
theorem complete_entity_validation_agreement
    {p c t : PartialSchema}
    {schema : Schema}
    {entities : Entities}
    (hp : p.WellFormed)
    (hc : c.WellFormed)
    (hlink : link p c = .ok t)
    (hcomplete : t.asSchema? = some schema)
    (hvalid : t.validateEntities entities = .ok ()) :
    validateEntities schema
      (entities ++ schema.acts.mapOnValues actionSchemaEntryToEntityData) = .ok ()

modules.doc:
This file defines what it means for a policy slice to be sound.

We prove two main theorems:

* Authorization returns the same response for a sound policy slice as for the
  original collection of policies (`isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice`).
* It is sound to slice policies based on scope constraints (see
  `isAuthorized_eq_for_scope_based_policy_slice`). The proof is based on a more
  general lemma (`sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices`) that covers all
  forms of slicing that are based on identifying "bound" principal and resource
  entities (if any) for a policy, such that the policy evaluates to true on an
  input only if the request principal and resource are descendents of the
  corresponding bound entities. Currently, we are extracting bounds only from
  the scope constraints. The general lemma also covers more sophisticated
  analyses that can extract bounds from policy conditions as well.
-

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice
items.doc:
Policy slicing soundness: `isAuthorized` produces the same result for a sound
slice (subset) of a collection of policies as it does for the original policies.
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice (req : Request) (entities : Entities) (slice policies : Policies) :
  IsSoundPolicySlice req entities slice policies →
  isAuthorized req entities slice = isAuthorized req entities policies

items.name: Cedar.Thm.sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices
items.doc: A sound bound analysis produces sound policy slices.
items.statement:
theorem sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices (ba : BoundAnalysis) (request : Request) (entities : Entities) (policies : Policies) :
  IsSoundBoundAnalysis ba →
  IsSoundPolicySlice request entities (ba.slice request entities policies) policies

items.name: Cedar.Thm.scope_bound_is_sound
items.doc: Scope-based bounds are sound.
items.statement:
theorem scope_bound_is_sound (policy : Policy) :
  IsSoundPolicyBound (scopeAnalysis policy) policy

items.name: Cedar.Thm.scope_analysis_is_sound
items.doc: Scope-based bound analysis is sound.
items.statement:
theorem scope_analysis_is_sound :
  IsSoundBoundAnalysis scopeAnalysis

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_eq_for_scope_based_policy_slice
items.doc:
Scope-based slicing is sound: `isAuthorized` produces the same result for a
scope-based slice of a collection of policies as it does for the original
policies.
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_eq_for_scope_based_policy_slice (request : Request) (entities : Entities) (policies : Policies) :
  isAuthorized request entities (BoundAnalysis.slice scopeAnalysis request entities policies) =
  isAuthorized request entities policies

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compileWithEffect_error_implies
items.statement:
theorem compileWithEffect_error_implies {effect : Effect} {p : Policy} {εnv : SymEnv} {err : SymCC.Error }:
  compileWithEffect effect p εnv = .error err →
  p.effect = effect ∧ compile p.toExpr εnv = .error err

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compileWithEffect_none_implies
items.statement:
theorem compileWithEffect_none_implies {effect : Effect} {p : Policy} {εnv : SymEnv} :
  compileWithEffect effect p εnv = .ok .none →
  p.effect ≠ effect

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compileWithEffect_some_implies
items.statement:
theorem compileWithEffect_some_implies {effect : Effect} {p : Policy} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  compileWithEffect effect p εnv = Except.ok (some t) →
  p.effect = effect ∧ compile p.toExpr εnv = .ok t

items.name: Cedar.Thm.satisfiedPolicies_filterMapM_eq
items.statement:
theorem satisfiedPolicies_filterMapM_eq {effect : Effect} {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} :
  List.filterMapM (compileWithEffect effect · εnv) ps =
  (ps.filter (λ p => p.effect == effect)).mapM (λ p => compile p.toExpr εnv)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_policy_wf
items.statement:
theorem compile_policy_wf {p : Policy} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  εnv.WellFormedFor p.toExpr →
  compile p.toExpr εnv = .ok t →
  (t.WellFormed εnv.entities ∧ t.typeOf = .option .bool)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.satisfiedPolicies_ok_implies
items.statement:
theorem satisfiedPolicies_ok_implies {effect : Effect} {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  satisfiedPolicies effect ps εnv = .ok t →
  ∃ ts,
    t = anyTrue (eq · (Term.some (Term.bool true))) ts ∧
    List.mapM (λ p => compile p.toExpr εnv) (List.filter (λ p => p.effect == effect) ps) = Except.ok ts

items.name: Cedar.Thm.eqSomeTrue
items.statement: abbrev eqSomeTrue

items.name: Cedar.Thm.satisfiedPolicies_wf
items.statement:
theorem satisfiedPolicies_wf {effect : Effect} {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term}
  (hwε : εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps)
  (hok : Cedar.SymCC.satisfiedPolicies effect ps εnv = .ok t) :

items.name: Cedar.Thm.satisfiedPolicies_interpret
items.statement:
theorem satisfiedPolicies_interpret {effect : Effect} {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} {I : Interpretation}
  (hwε : εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps)

  Cedar.SymCC.satisfiedPolicies effect ps (εnv.interpret I) = t.interpret I

items.name: Cedar.Thm.satisfiedPolicies_eq
items.statement:
theorem satisfiedPolicies_eq {effect : Effect} {ps : Policies} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term}
  (hwε : εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps)
  (hwe : env.WellFormedForPolicies ps)
  (heq : env ∼ εnv)
  (hok : Cedar.SymCC.satisfiedPolicies effect ps εnv = .ok t) :
  t = .bool (!(Cedar.Spec.satisfiedPolicies effect ps env.request env.entities).isEmpty)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.satisfiedPolicies_bisimulation

theorem satisfiedPolicies_bisimulation {effect : Effect} {ps : Policies} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} {I : Interpretation}
  (hwε : εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps)
  (hwe : env.WellFormedForPolicies ps)
  (hwI : I.WellFormed εnv.entities)
  (heq : env ∼ εnv.interpret I)
  (hok : Cedar.SymCC.satisfiedPolicies effect ps εnv = .ok t) :
  t.interpret I = .bool (!(Cedar.Spec.satisfiedPolicies effect ps env.request env.entities).isEmpty)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.same_decisions_def
items.statement:

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_ok_implies
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_ok_implies {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t →
  ∃ tp tf,
    satisfiedPolicies .permit ps εnv = .ok tp ∧
    satisfiedPolicies .forbid ps εnv = .ok tf ∧
    t = and tp (not tf)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_wf
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_wf {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t →
  t.WellFormed εnv.entities ∧ t.typeOf = .bool

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_interpret_eq_when_interpret_eq
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_interpret_eq_when_interpret_eq {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {I I' : Interpretation} {t : Term}
  (hwε : εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps)
  (hwI : I.WellFormed εnv.entities)
  (hwI' : I'.WellFormed εnv.entities)
  (heq : ∀ (p : Policy) (t : Term), p ∈ ps → compile p.toExpr εnv = Except.ok t → Term.interpret I t = Term.interpret I' t)
  (hok : SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t) :
  Term.interpret I t = Term.interpret I' t

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_interpret
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_interpret {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} {I : Interpretation} :
  εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t →
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps (εnv.interpret I) = .ok (t.interpret I)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_same
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_same {ps : Policies} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  env.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  env ∼ εnv →
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t →
  Cedar.Spec.isAuthorized env.request env.entities ps ∼ t

items.name: Cedar.Thm.isAuthorized_bisimulation
items.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_bisimulation {ps : Policies} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} {I : Interpretation} :
  εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  env.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  env ∼ εnv.interpret I →
  Cedar.SymCC.isAuthorized ps εnv = .ok t →
  Cedar.Spec.isAuthorized env.request env.entities ps ∼ t.interpret I

modules.doc:
This file proves two key auxiliary lemmas used to show the soundness
and completeness of Cedar's symbolic compiler.
-

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_evaluate
items.doc:
The lemma shows that the symbolic compiler (`compile`) behaves like the
concrete evaluator (`evaluate`) on literal inputs.

In particular, let `x` be an expression, `εnv` a well-formed symbolic
environment for `x`, and `env` a well-formed concrete environment for `x` that
is equivalent to `εnv`. Then, the result produced by the symbolic compiler on
`x` and `εnv` is equivalent to the result produced by the concrete evaluator `x`
and `env`.
items.statement:
theorem compile_evaluate {x : Expr} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} :
  env ∼ εnv →
  env.WellFormedFor x →
  εnv.WellFormedFor x →
  compile x εnv = .ok t →
  evaluate x env.request env.entities ∼ t

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_interpret
items.doc:
The lemma shows that `interpret` and `compile` can be applied in any order to get
the same result. In particular, let `x` be an expression, `εnv` a well-formed
symbolic environment for `x`, and `I` a well-formed interpretion for `εnv`.
Then, compiling `x` with respect to `(εnv.interpret I)` gives the same result as
interpreting the output of compiling `x` with respect to `εnv`.
items.statement:
theorem compile_interpret {x : Expr} {εnv : SymEnv} {I : Interpretation} {t : Term} :
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  εnv.WellFormedFor x →
  compile x εnv = .ok t →
  compile x (εnv.interpret I) = .ok (t.interpret I)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_bisimulation
items.statement:
theorem compile_bisimulation {x : Expr} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term} {I : Interpretation} :
  εnv.WellFormedFor x →
  env.WellFormedFor x →
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  env ∼ εnv.interpret I →
  compile x εnv = .ok t →
  evaluate x env.request env.entities ∼ t.interpret I

This file contains utility lemmas for proving compilation theorems
about lists of argument terms.

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_wfs
items.statement:
theorem compile_wfs {xs : List Expr} {εnv : SymEnv} {ts : List Term}
  (hwφ : ∀ (x : Expr), x ∈ xs → SymEnv.WellFormedFor εnv x)
  (hok : List.Forall₂ (λ x t => compile x εnv = Except.ok t) xs ts) :
  ∀ t ∈ ts, t.WellFormed εnv.entities

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_interpret_ihs
items.statement:
theorem compile_interpret_ihs {xs : List Expr} {εnv : SymEnv} {I : Interpretation} {ts : List Term}
  (hI  : Interpretation.WellFormed I εnv.entities)
  (hwε : ∀ (x : Expr), x ∈ xs → SymEnv.WellFormedFor εnv x)
  (ih  : ∀ (x : Expr), x ∈ xs → CompileInterpret x)
  (hok : List.Forall₂ (fun x t => compile x εnv = Except.ok t) xs ts) :
  List.Forall₂ (fun x t => compile x (SymEnv.interpret I εnv) = Except.ok (Term.interpret I t)) xs ts

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_interpret_args_not_error
items.statement:
theorem compile_interpret_args_not_error {εnv : SymEnv} {I : Interpretation} {xs : List Expr} {ts : List Term} {e : SymCC.Error} :
  List.Forall₂ (fun x t => compile x (SymEnv.interpret I εnv) = Except.ok (Term.interpret I t)) xs ts →
  List.mapM (fun x => compile x (SymEnv.interpret I εnv)) xs = Except.error e →
  False

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_interpret_terms
items.statement:
theorem compile_interpret_terms {xs : List Expr} {εnv : SymEnv} {I : Interpretation} {ts ts' : List Term}
  (h₁ : List.Forall₂ (λ x t => compile x (SymEnv.interpret I εnv) = Except.ok (Term.interpret I t)) xs ts)
  (h₂ : List.Forall₂ (λ x t => compile x (SymEnv.interpret I εnv) = Except.ok t) xs ts') :
  List.Forall₂ (λ t t' => Term.interpret I t = t') ts ts'

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_evaluate_ihs
items.statement:
theorem compile_evaluate_ihs {xs : List Expr} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv}
  (heq : env ∼ εnv)
  (hwe : ∀ (x : Expr), x ∈ xs → env.WellFormedFor x)
  (hwε : ∀ (x : Expr), x ∈ xs → εnv.WellFormedFor x)
  (ih  : ∀ (x : Expr), x ∈ xs → CompileEvaluate x)
  (hok : List.Forall₂ (fun x t => compile x εnv = Except.ok t) xs ts) :
  List.Forall₂ (fun x t => evaluate x env.request env.entities ∼ t) xs ts

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_evaluate_hasAttr_record
items.statement:
theorem compile_evaluate_hasAttr_record
  {a : Attr} {v₁ : Value} {es : Entities}
  {εs : SymEntities} {t₁ t₂ : Term} {ty₁ : TermType} {rty rty': Map Attr TermType}
  (hwφ₁ : Term.WellFormed εs t₁)
  (hty₁ : Term.typeOf t₁ = TermType.option ty₁)
  (hwo : Term.WellFormed εs (option.get t₁) ∧ Term.typeOf (option.get t₁) = TermType.record rty')
  (hwφ₂: Term.WellFormed εs t₂ ∧ Term.typeOf t₂ = TermType.option TermType.bool)
  (ha : RecordHasAttr t₂ (option.get t₁) rty a)
  (ih : (Except.ok v₁ : Spec.Result Value) ∼ t₁) :
  (hasAttr v₁ a es : Spec.Result Value) ∼ ifSome t₁ t₂

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_evaluate_hasAttr_entity
items.statement:
theorem compile_evaluate_hasAttr_entity
  {a : Attr} {v₁ : Value} {es : Entities}
  {εs : SymEntities} {t₁ t₂ : Term} {fₐ : UnaryFunction}
  {ety : EntityType} {rty : Map Attr TermType}
  (heq : SameEntities es εs)
  (hwε : εs.WellFormed)
  (hwf₁ : Value.WellFormed es v₁)
  (hwφ₁ : Term.WellFormed εs t₁)
  (hty₁ : Term.typeOf t₁ = TermType.option (.entity ety))
  (hwo  : Term.WellFormed εs (option.get t₁) ∧ Term.typeOf (option.get t₁) = .entity ety)
  (hwφ₂ : Term.WellFormed εs t₂ ∧ Term.typeOf t₂ = TermType.option TermType.bool)
  (hf : εs.attrs ety = some fₐ)
  (ha : RecordHasAttr t₂ (app fₐ (option.get t₁)) rty a)
  (ih : (Except.ok v₁ : Spec.Result Value) ∼ t₁) :
  (hasAttr v₁ a es : Spec.Result Value) ∼ ifSome t₁ t₂

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compile_evaluate_hasAttr
items.statement:
theorem compile_evaluate_hasAttr {x₁ : Expr} {a : Attr} {env : Env} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term}
  (heq : env ∼ εnv)
  (hwe : env.WellFormedFor (.hasAttr x₁ a))
  (hwε : εnv.WellFormedFor (.hasAttr x₁ a))
  (hok : compile (.hasAttr x₁ a) εnv = .ok t)

  evaluate (.hasAttr x₁ a) env.request env.entities ∼ t

items.name: Cedar.Thm.interpret_compileHasAttr

  (hI  : Interpretation.WellFormed I εs)
  (hwt : Term.WellFormed εs t₁)
  (hok : compileHasAttr t₁ a εs = Except.ok t) :
  compileHasAttr (t₁.interpret I) a (εs.interpret I) = .ok (t.interpret I)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compileHasAttr_false_of_getAttr_error_typeOf_eq
items.statement:
theorem compileHasAttr_false_of_getAttr_error_typeOf_eq
  {t₁ t₂ : Term} {a : Attr} {εs : SymEntities} {e : SymCC.Error}
  (hwε : εs.WellFormed)
  (hw₁ : t₁.WellFormed εs)
  (hw₂ : t₂.WellFormed εs)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compileGetAttr_noSuchAttribute_of_error_typeOf_eq
items.statement:
theorem compileGetAttr_noSuchAttribute_of_error_typeOf_eq
  {t₁ t₂ : Term} {a : Attr} {εs : SymEntities} {e : SymCC.Error}
  (hwε : εs.WellFormed)
  (hw₁ : t₁.WellFormed εs)
  (hw₂ : t₂.WellFormed εs)
  (hty : t₁.typeOf = t₂.typeOf)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.interpret_compileGetAttr_error_of_compileHasAttr_false
items.statement:
theorem interpret_compileGetAttr_error_of_compileHasAttr_false
  {t₁ : Term} {a : Attr} {εs : SymEntities} {I : Interpretation} {e : SymCC.Error}
  (hwε : εs.WellFormed)
  (hI : I.WellFormed εs)
  (hwt : t₁.WellFormed εs)
  (hha : compileHasAttr t₁ a εs = .ok (⊙ false))

items.name: Cedar.Thm.interpret_option_get_aux
items.statement:

modules.doc:
In this file we prove the equivalence between a recursive and an iterative compilation
function for extended has. The specs use the iterative implementation, which is more
efficient and mirrors the Rust implementation, but the proofs rely on the equivalence
with the recursive implementation (which mimics the recursive compilation of the
desugared form of extended-has).

The only public theorem, at the end of this module, is:
```
compileExtHasAttr_eq_compileExtHasAttrRec (...) :
  compileExtHasAttr t as εs = compileExtHasAttrRec t as εs
```

theorem compile_ite_ok_implies {x₁ x₂ x₃ : Expr} {εnv : SymEnv} {t : Term}
  (h₁ : compile (.ite x₁ x₂ x₃) εnv = .ok t) :
  ∃ t₁,
    (compile x₁ εnv) = .ok t₁ ∧
    match t₁ with
     | .some (.prim (.bool true))  => t = compile x₂ εnv
     | .some (.prim (.bool false)) => t = compile x₃ εnv
     | t₁ => CompileIfSym t t₁ (compile x₂ εnv) (compile x₃ εnv)

items.name: Cedar.Thm.compileApp₁_ok_implies
items.statement:
theorem compileApp₁_ok_implies {op₁ : UnaryOp} {t t₁ : Term}
  (h₁ : compileApp₁ op₁ t₁ = .ok t) :
  match op₁ with
  | .not     => t₁.typeOf = .bool ∧ t = Term.some (not t₁)
  | .neg     => t₁.typeOf = .bitvec 64 ∧ t = ifFalse (bvnego t₁) (bvneg t₁)
  | .like p  => t₁.typeOf = .string ∧ t = Term.some (string.like t₁ p)
  | .is ety₁ => ∃ ety₂, t₁.typeOf = .entity ety₂ ∧ t = Term.some (ety₁ = ety₂ : Bool)
  | .isEmpty => (∃ ty, t₁.typeOf = .set ty) ∧ t = Term.some (set.isEmpty t₁)

    (t₁.typeOf = .bitvec 64 ∧ t₂.typeOf = .bitvec 64 ∧ t = Term.some (bvslt t₁ t₂)) ∨
    (t₁.typeOf = .ext .duration ∧ t₂.typeOf = .ext .duration ∧ t = Term.some (bvslt (ext.duration.val t₁) (ext.duration.val t₂))) ∨
    (t₁.typeOf = .ext .datetime ∧ t₂.typeOf = .ext .datetime ∧ t = Term.some (bvslt (ext.datetime.val t₁) (ext.datetime.val t₂)))
  )

public theorem compileApp₂_wf_types {op₂ : BinaryOp} {t t₁ t₂: Term} {εs : SymEntities}

  t.WellFormed εs ∧
  match op₂ with
  | .add | .sub | .mul => t.typeOf = .option (.bitvec 64)
  | .getTag            => ∃ ety τs, t₁.typeOf = .entity ety ∧ εs.tags ety = some (some τs) ∧ t.typeOf = τs.vals.outType.option
  | _                  => t.typeOf = .option .bool

items.name: Cedar.Thm.ofRecordType_preserves_attr
items.doc:
If some attribute exists in a record type,
then it should still exist after applying `TermType.ofRecordType`
items.statement:
theorem ofRecordType_preserves_attr
  {rty : RecordType} {attr : Attr} {qty : Qualified CedarType} {ty : CedarType}
  (hattr_exists : Data.Map.find? rty attr = some qty)
  (hattr_ty : qty.getType = ty) :
  ∃ attr_ty : TermType,
    (Data.Map.mk (TermType.ofRecordType rty.1)).find? attr = some attr_ty ∧
    match attr_ty with
    | .option attr_ty' => TermType.ofType ty = attr_ty' ∧ ¬qty.isRequired
    | _ => TermType.ofType ty = attr_ty ∧ qty.isRequired

theorem compile_binaryApp_wf_types
  {op : BinaryOp} {a : TypedExpr} {b : TypedExpr} {ty : CedarType}
  {t : Term} {tcomp_a : Term} {tcomp_b : Term}
  {εnv : SymEnv}
  (hwf_ent : εnv.entities.WellFormed)
  (hok_a : compile a.toExpr εnv = Except.ok tcomp_a)
  (hok_b : compile b.toExpr εnv = Except.ok tcomp_b)
  (hwf_get_comp_a : Term.WellFormed εnv.entities (Factory.option.get tcomp_a))
  (hwf_get_comp_b : Term.WellFormed εnv.entities (Factory.option.get tcomp_b))
  (hok : compile (TypedExpr.toExpr (.binaryApp op a b ty)) εnv = .ok t) :
  match op with
    | .add | .sub | .mul => t.typeOf = .option (.bitvec 64)
    | .getTag            =>
      ∃ ety τs,
        (Factory.option.get tcomp_a).typeOf = .entity ety ∧
        εnv.entities.tags ety = some (some τs) ∧
        t.typeOf = τs.vals.outType.option
    | _                  => t.typeOf = .option .bool

modules.doc:
This file proves a key auxiliary lemma used to show the completeness of Cedar's
symbolic compiler: for every symbolic environment `εnv` that is well-formed for
an expression `x`, and for interpretation `I` that is well-formed for εnv, there
is concrete environment `env` that is well-formed with respect to `x` and that
corresponds to the interpretation of `εnv` under `I`. The concrete environment
`env` is obtained by concretizing `εnv.interpret I` with respect to `x`.
-

items.name: Cedar.Thm.exists_wf_env
items.statement:
theorem exists_wf_env {x : Expr} {εnv : SymEnv} {I : Interpretation} :
  εnv.WellFormedFor x →
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  ∃ (env : Env),
    env ∼ εnv.interpret I ∧
    env.WellFormedFor x

items.name: Cedar.Thm.exists_wf_env_for_policies
items.statement:
theorem exists_wf_env_for_policies {ps : Policies} {εnv : SymEnv} {I : Interpretation} :
  εnv.WellFormedForPolicies ps →
  I.WellFormed εnv.entities →
  ∃ (env : Env),
    env ∼ εnv.interpret I ∧
    env.WellFormedForPolicies ps

modules.title: Well-formedness and interpretations
modules.doc:
This file defines well-formedness constraints and relations on concrete and
symbolic structures. We prove correctness properties of the symbolic compiler
with respect to these defintions.

Well-formedness of a concrete structure is defined with respect to a set of
concrete entities `es : Entities`.  A `Value`, `Request`, or `EntityData`
structure is well-formed with respect to `es` if it references only entity UIDs
that are in the _domain_ of `es`; i.e., if the structure references a `uid`,
then `uid ∈ es`. The set `es` is well-formed if it consists of well-formed
`EntityData` structures, which amounts to saying that there are no dangling
references in the entities set `es`. Finally, an environment `Env` consisting of
a request `req` and entities `es` is _well-formed for_ an expression `x` if `es`
is well-formed, `req` is well-formed with respect to `es`, and `es` supports
`x`. We say that `es` _supports_ `x` if all entity UIDs referenced by `x` are in
the domain of `es`. If `env` is well-formed for `x`, then evaluating `x` against
`env` cannot result in an `entityDoesNotExist` error.

Well-formed symbolic structures are defined analagously to well-formed concrete
structures. In particular, well-formedness of a symbolic structure is defined
with respect to a set of symbolic entity declarations `εs : SymEntities`. A
`Term`, `SymRequest`, or `SymEntityData` structure is well-formed with respect
to `εs` if it references only entity types and UIDs that are in the _domain_ of
`εs`, and if all referenced term types represent valid Cedar types. An entity
type `ety` is in the domain of `εs` if `ety ∈ εs`, and entity UID `uid` is in
the domain of `εs` if `εs.isValidEntityUID uid`.  The set `εs` is well-formed if
it consists of well-formed `SymEntityData` structures. A symbolic environment
`SymEnv` consisting of a symbolic request `ρeq` and entities `εs` is
_well-formed for_ an expression `x` if `εs` is well-formed, `ρeq` is well-formed
with respect to `εs`, and `εs` _supports_ `x`.  We say that `εs` supports `x` if
`εs.isValidEntityUID uid` for every entity `uid` referenced by `x`.

A well-formed symbolic structure represents a _set_ of well-formed symbolic
_literal_ structures, which, in turn, represent corresponding well-formed Cedar
structures. A _literal_ symbolic structure contains no term variables or
uninterpreted functions. Symbolic structures are related to literals through
_interpretations_. An `Interpretation` binds term variables to literal terms and
uninterpreted functions (`UUF`) to interpreted ones (`UDF`). When a well-formed
symbolic structure is interpreted with respect to a well-formed Interpretation,
the result is a well-formed literal symbolic structure. Interpreting a literal
against any Interpretation returns the same literal.

A literal term or symbolic request represent a single corresponding Cedar
structure (i.e., a `Value`, `Outcome Value`, or `Request`). A well-formed
literal symbolic environment `εnv : SymEnv` represents a set of well-formed
concrete environments that lead to equivalent evaluation outcomes. In
particular, if `εnv` is a literal symbolic environment that is well-formed for
an expression `x`, then `x` produces the same outcome when evaluated against any
concrete environment `env ∈ εnv` that is well-formed for `x`. We write `env ∈ εnv`
to denote that exists a well-formed interpretation `I` such that
`εnv.interpret I` is a literal that represents `env`.

items.statement:
public inductive Expr.ValidRefs (validRef : EntityUID → Prop) : Expr → Prop
  | lit_valid {p : Prim}
    (h₁ : p.ValidRef validRef) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.lit p)
  | var_valid {v : Var} :
    ValidRefs validRef (.var v)
  | ite_valid {x₁ x₂ x₃ : Expr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁)
    (h₂ : ValidRefs validRef x₂)
    (h₃ : ValidRefs validRef x₃) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.ite x₁ x₂ x₃)
  | and_valid {x₁ x₂ : Expr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁)
    (h₂ : ValidRefs validRef x₂) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.and x₁ x₂)
  | or_valid {x₁ x₂ : Expr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁)
    (h₂ : ValidRefs validRef x₂) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.or x₁ x₂)
  | binaryApp_valid {op₂ : BinaryOp} {x₁ x₂ : Expr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁)
    (h₂ : ValidRefs validRef x₂) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.binaryApp op₂ x₁ x₂)
  | unaryApp_valid {op₁ : UnaryOp} {x₁ : Expr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.unaryApp op₁ x₁)
  | hasAttr_valid {x₁ : Expr} {a : Attr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.hasAttr x₁ a)
  | extHasAttr_valid {x₁ : Expr} {a : Attr} {as : List Attr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.extHasAttr x₁ a as)
  | getAttr_valid {x₁ : Expr} {a : Attr}
    (h₁ : ValidRefs validRef x₁) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.getAttr x₁ a)
  | set_valid {xs : List Expr}
    (h₁ : ∀ x ∈ xs, ValidRefs validRef x) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.set xs)
  | record_valid {axs : List (Attr × Expr)}
    (h₁ : ∀ ax ∈ axs, ValidRefs validRef ax.snd) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.record axs)
  | call_valid {xfn : ExtFun} {xs : List Expr}
    (h₁ : ∀ x ∈ xs, ValidRefs validRef x) :
    ValidRefs validRef (.call xfn xs)

public def TermType.cedarType? : TermType → Option CedarType
  | .bool             => .some (.bool .anyBool)
  | .bitvec 64        => .some .int
  | .string           => .some .string
  | .entity ety       => .some (.entity ety)
  | .set ty           => do .some (.set (← ty.cedarType?))
  | .record rty       => do
    let crty ← rty.mapMOnValues₂ λ ⟨tyᵢ, _⟩ => qualifiedType? tyᵢ
    .some (.record crty)
  | .ext xty          => .some (.ext xty)
  | _                 => .none
